items.title: SF6-Free Switchgear
items.h1: The Blue portfolio – a cleaner future
items.description: Siemens Energy Blue portfolio offers SF6-free, eco-friendly high-voltage switchgear using vacuum and clean air technology for zero greenhouse emissions.

faqs.q: What is Blue GIS?
faqs.a: It is using vacuum switching technology combined with clean air insulation instead of SF6.

faqs.q: What is a Blue Portfolio?
faqs.a: the Blue portfolio comprises different high-voltage products used in a substation using clean air as insulation medium instead of SF6.

faqs.q: What are the different types of high-voltage switchgear?
faqs.a: air-insulated switchgear (AIS) and gas-insulated switchgear (GIS)

faqs.q: What are the main benefits of using Blue GIS?
faqs.a: Zero greenhouse gases and Zero global warming potential; zero impact on healt and safety; virtually zero maintenance, training or reporting needed

faqs.q: How does Blue GIS compare to traditional gas-insulated switchgear?
faqs.a: Blue GIS contains no SF6 nor any other harmful F-gas or greenhouse gases. It uses vacuum technology with highest switching capability with Zero degradation and a wide temperature range

faqs.q: What are the key applications of Blue GIS in the power industry?
faqs.a: onshore and offshore substations up to 145 kV

faqs.q: What voltage levels and applications are supported by Blue high-voltage products?
faqs.a: onshore and offshore substations up to 145 kV

faqs.q: What are the maintenance requirements for Blue high-voltage products?
faqs.a: vacuum interrupter is maintenance-free (sealed for life). Blue circuit breakers and GIS have a maintenance schedule of 12 years for visual inspection and checks; first mayor inspection after 25 years

faqs.q: What makes Siemens Energy’s Blue high-voltage products environmentally sustainable?
faqs.a: Blue products contain no SF6 nor any other harmful F-gas or greenhouse gases.

faqs.q: What are the challenges associated with implementing Blue GIS?
faqs.a: The use of clean air requires a larger size of the GIS, which leads to higher space requirements and material costs. This can be compensated by installing a Low Power Instrument Transformer (LPIT).

body.text: Decarbonizing the energy industry is about more than switching to renewable sources. To achieve Zero Global Warming Potential (GWP), it's essential we make the transmission of power as clean and green as its generation. This means eliminating F-gases from electrical switchgear – particularly SF6, a gas 24,300 times more climate-hostile than CO2.
Our Blue portfolio uses clean air and vacuum switching technology instead. Zero F-gases, Zero toxicity and Zero harm to human health and the environment.
The technology transforming transmission
Less global warming potential is not good enough. It has to be Zero, because 1% global warming potential is still global warming potential. It has to be Zero and it has to be now.
Siemens Energy Project Lead
A transformed plant transforming energy

We've recently invested €60 million in our Berlin facility to step up production of vacuum interrupters for our Blue portfolio. This will help to secure our supply chain – and since the plant uses 100% renewable energy, it will also increase our sustainability.
The Blue portfolio
Not just Zero F gases, but Zero reduction in performance

Our Blue products use vacuum switching technology and clean air insulation to produce Zero harmful emissions - and without having to compromise on performance or economic feasibility. With over 10 years of experience in high-voltage vacuum switching, we have been able to maintain outstanding levels of technical performance and low lifecycle costs while reducing our ecological footprint to an enormous extent. Blue is already the perfect choice for substation products. And with the help of our strong partnerships, we can develop and implement it even further and faster.
Blue switchgear: leading the way, backed by the EU
Collaboration is crucial in cutting climate-harming emissions – and the LIFE Blue project GIS 420 kV is the latest example of how this works in practice.

Backed by EU funding and in partnership with Elia, operator of the electricity transmission network in Belgium, the LIFE Blue project is set to demonstrate for the first time the economic viability of a climate-friendly and completely F-gas free 420 kV GIS.

Instead of SF6-gas, which has a global warming potential of 24,300, clean air is used for insulation. The technology is already operational in medium-voltage applications, but its use at this higher voltage will represent a major step forward.
The new net-zero 8VM3
Our new customizable 8VM3 switchgear operates at 72.5 kW and its modular design also gives it the flexibility to work in conventional onshore substations as well as offshore wind turbines.
Blue partnerships

At Siemens Energy, we see a partnership as much more than a simple supplier-client relationship. It goes way beyond the placing and delivery of an order. Rather, it's a dose alliance between both parties. We work together towards a shared goal, developing the end solution by exchanging ideas and expertise at every stage.
This collaborative, interactive approach is mutually beneficial. Solutions can be shaped to meet particular requirements and the optimal set-up is reached more quickly.
Blue installations in operation

Our Blue portfolio is already helping our customers around the world to advance towards their carbon reduction goals. Here are just a few examples of the technology - and our close collaborations – in action.
Hornsea 3: Clean switchgear technology for the world's largest offshore wind farm

Siemens Energy Berlin proudly delivers its 2000th SF6-free 8VM1 Blue GIS to the monumental Hornsea 3 wind farm in the North Sea, developed by Siemens Gamesa. This landmark project is set to supply green energy to over 3 million UK homes, marking a significant milestone in the global transition to sustainable power.
At work in Netherland's largest wind farm
We delivered 160 8VM1 Blue Gis bays to this huge project off the coast of the Netherlands, which is capable of supplying up to three million Dutch households with green energy.

"Being CO2-neutral is the future and the target for our customers in the offshore wind market, as well as for us at Siemens Energy." – Ann-Sofie Bonde Mortensen, Global Vertical Sales Manager Offshore Wind, Siemens Energy.
Bringing clean power to Bergen Port
Thanks to BKK Nett's use of Blue switchgear, the cruise ships in this Norwegian port now use only clean power - with Zero greenhouse gas emissions, Zero F-gases and Zero pollution.
"We managed to make the change in Bergen despite having restricted space in our substations. The experience is what we expected: problem-free." – Jens Skar, Division Manager, BKK Nett.
A new substation for Netze BW
This high-voltage substation in Burladingen, southern Germany is the first in the world to be eco-efficient, to operate without SF6 and to use digitalization to achieve new levels of connectivity.
"The innovation level in this project is very high. The substation of the future is a bold step for us, that requires trust." – Marcel Engel, Netze BW expert for grid development.
The first F-gas-free switchgear in Finland
When we supplied ten bays of our Blue switchgear to Fingrid, we were delivering the first GIS in the country that replaces F-gases with clean air.
"With Siemens Energy we have found a reliable partner that offers innovative products with absolutely Zero climate-harming fluorinated gases." – Timo Kiiveri, Senior Vice President at Fingrid.
Decarbonization through digitalization with Westnetz

The digitally-enabled 145 kV 3AV1 Blue circuit breakers installed at the Hesseln substation uses the Noedra Node switchgear digitalization technology to enable more eﬃcient and economic management and better-informed operational decisions.

"The medium-term replacement of the insulating gas SF6 is an essential component of the decarbonization strategy of our E.ON Group." – Dr. Markus Obergünner, Senior Vice President High Voltage Grid, Westnetz GmbH.
Digital integration of gas- and air insulated switchgear

By combining real-time data acquisition, advanced analytics, and secure automation, Node delivers a holistic view of digital substation health and performance - across transformers, switchgear, AC protection, automation & control systems, keeping breakers, insulation, and gas systems healthy and predictable. Siemens Energy's Noedra Node detects anomalies early, reduce forced outages, and streamline maintenance across your installations.
Substation digitalization
Boost grid reliability with substation digitalization solutions. Enable secure, data-driven operations and optimize digital substation performance.

body.text: At Siemens Energy, we see a partnership as much more than a simple supplier-client relationship. It goes way beyond the placing and delivery of an order. Rather, it's a close alliance between both parties. We work together towards a shared goal, co-creating the end solution by exchanging ideas and expertise at every stage. We have fostered this collaborative, interactive approach from the earliest days of the Blue portfolio.

For example, back in 2018 we joined forces with Iljin Electric to produce the first SF6-free 170 kV GIS with vacuum technology. And it's an approach we have found to be mutually beneficial in every case since. Innovation is boosted on both sides, costs are shared and the optimal solution is reached more quickly.
Working together for clean high-voltage switchgear

Backed by EU funding and in partnership with Elia, operator of the electricity transmission network in Belgium, the LIFE Blue project is set to demonstrate for the first time the economic viability of a climate-friendly and completely F-gas free 420 kV GIS.
Projects built on partnerships
Leading the switch to SF6-free switchgear

The EU has launched a multi-million euro project to reduce greenhouse gases across the entire energy chain – in particular, SF6 gas. Read how we're working together with eleven other partners from nine countries to achieve this.
Blue journey: Siemens Energy and Pfeiffer Vacuum+Fab Solutions
Siemens Energy collaborated with Pfeiffer Vacuum+Fab Solutions to develop an innovative vacuum-based leak detection method including tightness verification in clean air insulated switchgear.
A collective commitment

Together with five other leading power equipment manufacturers, we have formed the Switching Gears for Net Zero Alliance. To prevent harm to the environment and to human health, we are campaigning for:

items: F-gases to be phased out where clean alternatives are commercially available
Reporting obligations on F-gases to be extended EU policymakers to support the European
Commission's timeframe for eliminating F-gases in power grids

body.text: Agreement made with Mitsubishi Electric

Siemens Energy has signed a formal agreement with Mitsubishi Electric to work closely together on the development of high-voltage switchgear with zero GWF. Methods for scaling up the application of clean air insulation technology to higher voltage are being researched, with a 245 kV dead tank circuit breaker being the first joint project. This collaboration will speed up the availability of cleaner solutions for customers around the world.
A partnership. A pledge.

Together with other leading electrical transmission and distribution (T&D) manufacturers, we have signed a joint commitment to deliver equipment free of F-gases and PFAS-gases. In conjunction with the increasing use of renewable energy sources, we will make truly sustainable, climate-neutral power grids a reality and facilitate the transition to net zero emission economies.
TransnetBW award winners from left to right: Dr. Ulf Katschinski and Markus Klinner from Siemens Energy
Blue is honored!
Siemens Energy is the winner of this years TransnetBW supplier award in the category sustainability.
We would like to say „Thank you!" to our customers, who put so much trust into our sustainable products, with Zero compromise in environmental protection and performance.
Meet to greet the future

We were delighted to bring together valued customers from the US at our Berlin factory to demonstrate the latest developments in our Blue portfolio - in particular, our Blue Dead Tank with clean air insulation.
The factory is now 100% powered by renewable energy, providing our customers with the reassurance that we are making the whole supply chain as clean and sustainable as possible.
The Blue portfolio

To decarbonize the energy industry, it's essential we make the transmission of power as clean and green as its generation. This means eliminating climate-hostile SF6 gas from electrical switchgear as soon as possible.

Our Blue portfolio, based on clean air and vacuum switching technology, provides a viable, reliable and already available alternative. Zero F-gases, Zero toxicity and Zero harm to human health and the environment. Find out more about the future-ready Blue portfolio.

faqs.q: Vacuum interruption principle
faqs.a: Vacuum interrupters form the backbone of our 3AV1 Blue portfolio. Based on more than 40 years of experience in medium-voltage range and more than 6 million delivered vacuum interrupters, Siemens Energy has introduced this proven technology to high-voltage power networks in 2010. This game-changing technology offers several advantages: Zero C02 or F-gas emissionsHermetical tightness to protect from decomposition productsHigh switching performance without degradation Zero maintenance (sealed for life)Perfect for low temperatures, no liquefaction of switching medium

faqs.q: Self-compression principle
faqs.a: Our complete 3AP family up to 1100 kV relies on our arc-quenching principles either the self-compression or the dynamic self-compression principle using the thermal energy of arch. Siemens patented this method of arc quenching in 1973 and has continued to develop the technology of the self-compression interrupter unit ever since.

faqs.q: What is a high voltage circuit breaker and how does it work?
faqs.a: A high voltage circuit breaker is an electrical device designed to protect high voltage power systems by interrupting the flow of electricity during fault conditions, such as short circuits or overloads. It operates by detecting abnormal current levels and quickly opening the circuit to prevent damage to equipment and ensure safety. The mechanism typically involves a combination of mechanical and electrical components, including a trip unit that senses faults, and a switching mechanism that physically opens the circuit, using gas, oil, or air as an insulating medium.

faqs.q: What is the maximum voltage for a circuit breaker?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers high voltage circuit breakers that can handle voltages up to 1100 kV

faqs.q: How are high-voltage circuit breakers tested for reliability?
faqs.a: Circuit breakers are tested on several ways before leaving factories to ensure the safe and reliable operation. Testing routines are different, depending on the product type.

faqs.q: What are the common maintenance issues with high-voltage circuit breakers?
faqs.a: Circuit breakers offered by Siemens Energy are mainteance free for up 25 years.

faqs.q: How do high-voltage circuit breakers differ from medium-voltage ones?
faqs.a: They differ in voltage ratings, applications, design compexity and in several operational characteristics. Medium voltage ranges up to 66 kV, high voltage as above 72,5 KV

faqs.q: How do HVDC circuit breakers differ from AC circuit breakers?
faqs.a: HVDC circuit breakers are specifically designed to handle the unique challenges of direct current systems, while AC circuit breakers are optimized for alternating current applications.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a circuit breaker and a vacuum circuit breaker?
faqs.a: Vacuum circuit breakers operate by interrupting the current within a vacuum chamber and are known for their compact size and reliability. Other circuit breakers use different insulating mediums, air, oil or gas and different interrupting technology.

body.text: When choosing a circuit breaker, you want a solution that ensures quality, reliability, and innovation tailored to your needs. Our extensive range of circuit breakers is designed with you in mind,providing the peace of mind that comes from using industry-leading technology.

Since 2010, Siemens Energy F-gas-free breakers have set new standards, allowing you to meet environmental regulations while maintaining optimal performance. With a well-proven modular platform concept, our high-voltage circuit breakers are adaptable to your specific requirements, ensuring they can handle extremely high voltage levels effectively.​
By selecting our circuit breakers, you are investing in a solution that not only meets your operational needs but also supports your commitment to sustainability and efficiency.

Circuit breakers technology

Vacuum interrupters form the backbone of our 3AV1 Blue portfolio. body.text: Self-compression principle

Our complete 3AP family up to 1100 kV relies on our arc-quenching principles either the self-compression or the dynamic self-compression principle using the thermal energy of arch. The drive concept of the 3AP circuit breaker family is basedon the patented stored-energy spring principle. Themechanism types differ in terms of the number, size andarrangement of the opening and closing springs. body.text: The SiCEA01 contact erosion analyzer is used to determine the extent of wear to the circuit breaker contacts. The breaking currents of the circuit breaker are used to determine the contact wear. Switching operations with currents below the rated normal current are evaluated with the rated normal current. The contact burn off is calculated using the integral of the circuit breaker breaking currents. The result is compared with the configured reference values. If the result of this comparison exceeds the warning or alarm value, the corresponding signal contact is activated, and the signal light on the contact wear analysis device shows the status. With this warning or alarm, SiCEA01 shows whether the circuit breaker contact system has already been worn down to a specific level, which allows servicing work to be scheduled in good time.

body.text: Get answers: FAQs on circuit breakers
What is a high voltage circuit breaker and how does it work?

A high voltage circuit breaker is an electrical device designed to protect high voltage power systems by interrupting the flow of electricity during fault conditions, such as short circuits or overloads. It operates by detecting abnormal current levels and quickly opening the circuit to prevent damage to equipment and ensure safety. The mechanism typically involves a combination of mechanical and electrical components, including a trip unit that senses faults, and a switching mechanism that physically opens the circuit, using gas, oil, or air as an insulating medium.
What is the maximum voltage for a circuit breaker?
Siemens Energy offers high voltage circuit breakers that can handle voltages up to 1100 kV
How are high-voltage circuit breakers tested for reliability?
Circuit breakers are tested on several ways before leaving factories to ensure the safe and reliable operation. Testing routines are different, depending on the product type.
What are the common maintenance issues with high-voltage circuit breakers?
Circuit breakers offered by Siemens Energy are mainteance free for up 25 years.
How do high-voltage circuit breakers differ from medium-voltage ones?
They differ in voltage ratings, applications, design compexity and in several operational characteristics. Medium voltage ranges up to 66 kV, high voltage as above 72,5 KV
How do HVDC circuit breakers differ from AC circuit breakers?
HVDC circuit breakers are specifically designed to handle the unique challenges of direct current systems, while AC circuit breakers are optimized for alternating current applications.
What is the difference between a circuit breaker and a vacuum circuit breaker?

Vacuum circuit breakers operate by interrupting the current within a vacuum chamber and are known for their compact size and reliability. Other circuit breakers use different insulating mediums, air, oil or gas and different interrupting technology.

faqs.q: What are compressors?
faqs.a: Compressors are mechanical devices that increase the pressure of a gas thereby reducing its volume. They are used in various applications to move and compress gases for different industrial processes.

faqs.q: What are the types of compressors for industrial applications?
faqs.a: There are several types of compressors used in industrial applications, including reciprocating compressors, integrally geared centrifugal compressors and single shaft centrifugal compressors. Each type has its own specific use cases and advantages depending on the application.

faqs.q: Which compressor is best for the energy industry?
faqs.a: The best compressor for the energy industry depends on the specific requirements of the application. Factors such as flow, pressure ratio, turndown capacity, process gas variation will determine the best compressor selection. For example, integrally geared compressors (IGCs) are often used for large flow CO2 compression in carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) applications due to their efficiency and reliability.

faqs.q: What are the industrial applications for compressors?
faqs.a: Compressors are used in a wide range of industrial applications, including oil and gas production, natural gas transmission and distribution, air separation, chemical and petrochemical processing, and refining. Applications also includes key areas of industrial decarbonization including carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), decarbonization of heat, production of clean fuels, energy storage and hydrogen compression for production, transportation and utilization.

faqs.q: What is the manufacturing process for compressors?
faqs.a: The manufacturing process of compressors involves several steps, including the design and engineering of components, machining and fabrication of parts, assembly of the compressor units, and rigorous testing to ensure performance and reliability. Furthermore, the compressor is often integrated with balance of plant equipment into an overall package. Specific manufacturing processes may vary depending on the type of compressor being manufactured.

faqs.a: "Our compression solutions are used across a wide range of industries and applications, including: Oil and Gas: Onshore and offshore production, natural gas transmission and distribution. Chemicals, petrochemicals and refining: Processing and refining operations. Decarbonization: Clean fuel production, energy storage, and heat decarbonization"

faqs.q: How does Siemens Energy's compression technology improve efficiency?
faqs.a: Our compressors are designed with a focus on energy efficiency, reliability, availability and compactness. These are complemented through the use of advanced rotor designs, dry gas seals, and integrated control systems to reduce energy consumption and emissions while maximizing lifetime customer value.

faqs.q: What makes Siemens Energy's compression solutions stand out in the market?
faqs.a: Our compression solutions are known for high reliability, modularity, and adaptability across industries. We offer a broad portfolio—from single-shaft to integrally geared and reciprocating compressors—tailored for both standard and high-pressure applications. With thousands of references and millions of operational hours across dozens of applications, our compressor solutions deliver proven reliability and high performance.

faqs.q: How does Siemens Energy support the energy transition with its compression technology?
faqs.a: We support decarbonization by applying our cutting-edge technologies in applications like hydrogen and CO₂ compressors, as well as in compression systems for oil and gas applications that reduce emissions and extend the life of existing fields. These innovations help industries shift toward cleaner energy sources while maintaining robust designs that last decades.

faqs.q: What is the control system of a compressor?
faqs.a: It’s an automated system that monitors and regulates compressor operation to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable performance.

faqs.q: How does a compressor control system work?
faqs.a: It uses sensors and logic controllers to adjust parameters like pressure, temperature, and flow in real time based on system demands.

faqs.q: What are the main components of a compressor control system?
faqs.a: Key components include sensors, controllers (PLC or DCS), actuators, human-machine interfaces (HMI), and communication modules.

faqs.q: How do compressor control systems improve efficiency?
faqs.a: They optimize load sharing, reduce energy waste, and prevent unnecessary wear by adjusting operation to match demand.

faqs.q: Can compressor control systems manage multiple compressors?
faqs.a: Yes, advanced systems can coordinate multiple compressors for balanced load distribution and redundancy.

faqs.q: How do compressor control systems maintain consistent air quality?
faqs.a: They monitor and adjust parameters like dew point, pressure, and filtration to ensure stable and clean output.

faqs.q: What role do sensors play in compressor control systems?
faqs.a: Sensors provide real-time data on pressure, temperature, vibration, and flow, enabling precise control and early fault detection.

faqs.q: How do compressor control systems handle pressure regulation?
faqs.a: They adjust compressor speed, valve positions, or bypass flows to maintain target pressure within safe limits.

faqs.q: Can compressor control systems integrate with plant-wide monitoring and control?
faqs.a: Yes, they can connect with SCADA or DCS platforms for centralized monitoring, diagnostics, and control.

faqs.q: What are the key benefits of using Siemens Energy's Compressor Train One Control systems?
faqs.a: We offer integrated control of the entire compressor train, improving reliability, reducing downtime, and simplifying operations.

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy's control systems enhance compressor performance?
faqs.a: By using advanced algorithms and real-time data, they can optimize efficiency, reduce emissions, and extend equipment life.

faqs.q: Can Siemens Energy's compressor controls be monitored remotely?
faqs.a: Yes, we support secure remote access for monitoring, diagnostics, and updates.

Coolant system monitoring: Continuous monitoring of the coolant system to ensure proper cooling and prevent overheating, ensuring reliable compressor operation.

items.title: Dry Gas Seals
items.description: Our Dry Gas Seals for centrifugal compressors increase the efficiency, reliability and sustainability of your equipment.

faqs.q: What is a dry gas seal used for?
faqs.a: Dry gas seals are primarily used in centrifugal compressors, turbomachinery, and rotating equipment to prevent gas leakage. They create a hermetic seal between rotating and stationary components using a thin film of gas, typically the same medium being compressed. This non-contact seal minimizes wear and reduces the risk of leaks, enhancing the efficiency and reliability of the compression process.

faqs.q: What is the difference between wet oil seals and dry gas seals?
faqs.a: Wet oil seals use oil to lubricate and create a barrier, preventing gas leakage but requiring more maintenance and potentially causing contamination. Dry gas seals use a thin film of gas, reducing emissions, maintenance needs, and improving efficiency.

faqs.q: Where are dry gas seals used?
faqs.a: Dry gas seals are used in compressors for pipelines, offshore platforms, oil refineries, and petrochemical and gas processing plants. They prevent gas leakage by creating a non-contact seal using a thin film of gas.

faqs.q: What is the life of a dry gas seal?
faqs.a: The life of a dry gas seal in a compressor typically ranges from 5 to 10 years, depending on operating conditions and maintenance practices.

faqs.q: What causes dry gas seal failure?
faqs.a: Dry gas seal failure in compressors can be caused by contamination, improper installation, thermal shock, mechanical wear, and pressure fluctuations.

body.text: Siemens Energy's goal is to minimize customers' ongoing wet oil seal costs, unscheduled downtime and resulting productivity losses. Currently, there are thousands of centrifugal compressors installed globally that predate advanced Dry Gas Seal (DGS) technology and run with wet oil seals, which require costly maintenance and cause parasitic power losses due to oil shear and drag.
Dry Gas Seals in centrifugal compressors

The Dry Gas Seals employed in Siemens Energy's centrifugal compressors represent a significant advance in shaft sealing. This state-of-the-art solution will help by eliminating the ongoing maintenance costs associated with wet oil seals and thereby greatly increases equipment reliability and efficiency. The design of the Dry Gas Seal ensures best overall compressor performance as well as emission reduction for increased sustainability.

body.text: The heart of the DGS is a pair of rings. A stationary ring is held against a rotating ring by spring pressure. The contact face of the rotating ring incorporates special fil-riding geometries in the form of groves or tapered lands on the outer portion.

items: Patented bi-directional groove design

Liquid Phase Sintered Silicon Carbide
In-house Theoretical Gas Film Modeling

body.text: Siemens Energy, as the compressor OEM, is best suited to provide a sealing solution that ensures the best overall compressor performance and maintenance, from a single source. Applicable to all OEM and non-OEM centrifugal compressors.
A dry approach to centrifugal compressor emissions mitigation
Dry gas seal retrofits, recompression help legacy compressors comply with current, future regulations.
Seal Protect - a reliable, cost-effective sealing solution for centrifugal compressors
Siemens Energy's innovative sealing solution eliminates the need for a seal gas booster, protects dry gas seals from contamination, and reduces maintenance and downtime costs.

Seal Protect sits between the dry gas seal and process side seal, remaining open during operation to prevent contamination. In static or low-speed conditions, it ensures only clean, dry process gas reaches the Dry Gas Seal.
Benefits of Seal Protect include:

items: Increased reliability: Simplified design reduces component failure risk.
Reduced cost: With lower operational and maintenance costs.
Minimized footprint: System can replace the seal gas booster, saving space.
Lower emissions: Seal Protect uses less power, reducing emissions.

body.text: Seal Protect is compatible with most new compressor packages and can be retrofitted into existing units for improved reliability.

items.description: We are a global market leader in hydrogen compressors with over 2500+ units operating in hydrogen applications.

faqs.q: What is a hydrogen compressor?
faqs.a: A hydrogen compressor is a device used to increase the pressure of hydrogen gas by reducing its volume. This process is essential for various applications, such as storing hydrogen in high-pressure tanks, transporting it through pipelines, and utilizing it in fuel cells and other energy systems.

faqs.q: What are the challenges of compressing hydrogen?
faqs.a: Compressing hydrogen poses several challenges due to its unique properties. One of the primary issues is hydrogen embrittlement, a phenomenon where hydrogen atoms diffuse into metals, leading to reduced ductility and potential cracking. This necessitates the use of materials released for hydrogen exposure under specific boundary conditions and designs to ensure the durability and safety of compressors.Hydrogen molecules are very light and require substantial energy to be compressed to high pressures. This impacts the overall efficiency of hydrogen storage and transportation systems.

faqs.q: How big is the hydrogen compressor market?
faqs.a: The hydrogen compressor market is experiencing significant growth driven by the increasing demand for hydrogen as a clean energy source. As of recent reports, the market size was estimated to be valued at several billion dollars. This expansion is fueled by advancements in hydrogen production technologies, supportive government policies, and the growing adoption of hydrogen fuel cells in various sectors such as transportation, industrial processes, and power generation.

faqs.q: What types of compressors are suitable for hydrogen compression?
faqs.a: The best compressor for hydrogen depends on the specific application and the operating conditions. Generally, reciprocating compressors, diaphragm compressors, and centrifugal compressors are highly regarded in the industry for hydrogen compression.The optimal choice will depend on factors such as the required pressure, flow rate, purity level, and specific use case. Consulting with our hydrogen compression experts will provide tailored solutions to meet your needs effectively.

faqs.q: How does Siemens Energy ensure the quality and reliability of its hydrogen compressors?
faqs.a: We use rigorous testing protocols, advanced turbomachinery design, and hydrogen-compatible materials. Our compressors are engineered for long life, high efficiency, and minimal maintenance, even under demanding conditions. Our facilities are ISO9001 certified with strict industry compliance.

faqs.q: Can Siemens Energy’s hydrogen compressors be integrated into existing infrastructure?
faqs.a: Yes, we design our compressors for compatibility with existing hydrogen production, storage, and transport systems. Our modular and scalable solutions support seamless integration into both new and retrofitted facilities. We are able to revamp existing units with either foot print replacement, or new unit installations.

body.text: Hydrogen, the lightest and most abundant element, can be used as a clean energy source with vast potential. Growing global hydrogen demand requires flexible, cost effective and efficient compressor solutions for storage, transportation, and use in different processes.

Compressing hydrogen with tailor made compression solutions offers numerous benefits, including increased energy density and enhanced energy efficiency. Hydrogen compressors also facilitate the integration of hydrogen into existing infrastructure and support the development of renewable energy solutions, driving us towards a more sustainable future.
Compressors for hydrogen applications

Compressors are essential to move, store or transform hydrogen. From the point at which hydrogen is produced to the point where it is consumed, our wide compression portfolio supports many applications across the hydrogen value chain. Applications for hydrogen compression include:

items: Compression of hydrogen post electrolysis
Compression of hydrogen produced by steam methane or autothermal reformers (SMRs/ATRs)
Hydrogen booster stations in pipeline networks
Compression for storage (cavern/vessel)
Production of e-fuels (ammonia/methanol/eSAF)
Industrial applications (e.g. green steel)
Mobility
Petrochemical/refining feedstock
Compression for hydrogen liquefaction

body.text: Centrifugal compressors offer a compelling solution for hydrogen services as projects scale in size, and complexity. Designed to handle large hydrogen flow rates in a single machine, they significantly reduce system complexity compared to multi‑unit reciprocating compressor trains. With fewer moving parts, centrifugal compressors deliver higher reliability, longer mean time between failures, and lower maintenance demand, while also minimizing contamination risks critical for high‑purity hydrogen applications. Their ability to operate efficiently across wide pressure and flow ranges makes them well suited for variable hydrogen production profiles, supporting future‑ready, cost‑effective, and highly reliable hydrogen infrastructure.
Welcome to the next generation of large-scale H2 compression

Siemens Energy's advanced hydrogen compressor represents a new generation of hydrogen compression technology, designed to meet the scale, variability, and pressure ratio demands of the emerging hydrogen economy. Based on proven centrifugal compression principles, the advanced rotor enables high-flow hydrogen compression in a single, highly reliable machine. Optimized specifically for low molecular weight duties, it supports a wide operating range, from low-pressure to high-pressure applications, and is suitable for pure hydrogen, hydrogen-rich and other low molecular weight gases (such as helium). With its scalable design, compact footprint, and enhanced reliability, the advanced hydrogen compressor provides a future‑proof solution for large-scale hydrogen infrastructure. Compressor technology doesn't “care” about the “color” of the hydrogen and how it is produced, it simply compresses according to the physics of a low mol-weight gas application. Both reciprocating and turbo compressors cover the complete map of low mol-weight applications. With each product having its strengths in overlapping areas, the choice of the product requires both technical as well as economic considerations.

For this reason, finding a solution for hydrogen compression is always project-specific and can even combine both products to find the optimal and most efficient solution for the client's compression needs. In general, reciprocating compressors apply to applications which have small suction volume flows, high pressure ratios and/or high process flexibility requirements whilst centrifugal compressors apply to low compression ratio and medium to high volume flow applications.

What are the key considerations for hydrogen compression?
To support the development of accurate and optimized hydrogen compression solutions, several key considerations need to be clearly defined during the solution design phase:

items: What is the gas composition and is there water in the gas?
Is the flow provided the dry flow or the wet flow?
At what pressure is the gas being provided to the compressor?
At what temperature is the gas being provided to the compressor?
What cooling mediums are available on site for process gas cooling requirements between compression stages?
If there is no water on site, what is the site ambient temperature for finfan air coolers?
What discharge pressure is required?
What level of lubrication oil carryover is acceptable downstream of compressor?
What is the operating philosophy and capacity control requirement?

body.text: Integrally geared compressors overview

Integrally geared compressors are multi-shaft machines. Several pinion shafts with one or two impellers each are arranged around a central bull gear. For each pinion shaft a perfect combination of shaft speed and impeller size can be realized. All impellers are of overhung design and can be fitted with adjustable inlet guide vanes in front of each impeller. Inter-stage cooling of the gas stream can be done after each impeller discharge. The combination of these features allows for high volume flows, outstanding energy efficiency even under part load, all in a compact design.

For small to medium size compressors, Siemens Energy offer a package design. The package can include the compressor, driver, process gas coolers, lube oil console, process piping, and all tubing and wiring. The package design leads to significantly reduced on-site installation time. For large-size units all main train components are delivered separately to site to be installed on a concrete foundation.

The technology applied for steam compression is integrally geared compressors. Read more in the article here. Decarbonizing industrial process heat through steam compression
Turbo Heater The Turbo Heater technology is specifically designed to deliver high-temperature process heat at industrial scale without combustion of fossil fuels.
Rotating Olefins Cracker (ROC)

The Rotating Olefins Cracker (ROC), jointly developed by Siemens Energy and Technip Energies, introduces a brand-new approach to olefins production - a game changing approach to decarbonize the olefin production process.
Mechanical Vapor Recompression (MVR) cycles open a new pathway for decarbonization

Looking for an efficient and cost-effective way to recover waste heat in industrial processes? For waste heat temperature levels from approximately 70°C (i.e. mid-temperature levels), MVR cycles provide an alternative to closed loop heat pumps for recovering waste heat, to produce low, medium, or high-pressure steam.

MVR cycles use advanced compression technology to extract heat from industrial processes and convert it into usable energy. This technology is particularly useful for the downstream oil and gas, chemicals, pulp and paper, food and beverage, and aluminum industries, where waste heat is a byproduct of many processes.

With MVR cycles, thermal energy from a mid-temperature waste stream is used to directly evaporate feedwater. The steam is then compressed to the required temperature and pressure level of the process. The entire latent heat for evaporation is provided by the free-of-charge waste heat. Only the sensible heat, which is significantly lower than the latent/evaporation heat, is provided in the form of compression. The steam can then be used for industrial purposes, either as a feedstock or as a heating medium, e.g. in the chemical industry or in pulp and paper.

For application cases in which waste steam is present at lower than desired pressure levels, the steam can simply be compressed up to higher pressure and temperature levels, with the use of our multi-stage integrally geared steam compressors.
Benefits:

items: The MVR cycle can be applied for waste heat sources at temperatures as low as ~70°C and does not require the use of a refrigerant, which is often either fluorinated, flammable, or toxic.

Compared to a closed loop heat pump, the MVR system can be designed in a very lean and compact way – oftentimes eliminating the need for an expansion valve, the flash tank, the refrigerant condenser, and some ancillary piping.

COPs (Coefficients of Performance) of more than 7.0 are possible. This means only one seventh of the final heat output needs to be given in the form of electricity for the compressor drive; the remaining six sevenths are provided in the form of waste heat.
With the use of proven Integrally Geared Compressor (IGC) technology, CAPEX, OPEX and footprint can be optimized.
IGCs can handle large volumetric flows up to 2.4 million m3/hr in one machine, enabling applications with 100+ MWth final heat output with only one machine.
Final steam pressures up to 60 bar and temperatures up to 330°C are possible. Higher temperatures are possible as well with the use of a small downstream superheater.
Siemens Energy has extensive steam know-how and experience inhouse via 10,000+ steam turbine references.

items.h1: Pipeline compressors: compressors for natural gas pipelines
items.description: Siemens Energy offers a wide range of pipeline compressors with a choice of axial intake or conventional horizontally opposed suction and discharge nozzles.

faqs.q: What is a pipeline compressor?
faqs.a: A pipeline compressor is a rotating or reciprocating machine used to increase the pressure of natural gas as it travels through a pipeline. This helps to maintain the flow of gas over long distances and through various terrains.

faqs.q: What is a natural gas compressor station?
faqs.a: A natural gas compressor station is a facility that houses pipeline compressors and other equipment such as gas scrubbers, filters, dehydrators and cooling systems. These stations are strategically located along a pipeline to remove moisture and contaminants and boost the pressure of the natural gas, ensuring it continues to flow efficiently to its destination.

faqs.q: What is natural gas compression?
faqs.a: Natural gas compression is the process of increasing the pressure of natural gas to facilitate its efficient and economical transportation through pipelines from production sites to end users. Compression is necessary to overcome the pressure loss mainly from friction and elevation changes as the gas flows through the pipeline.

items.title: Reciprocating compressor valves and capacity control
items.h1: Reciprocating compressor valves and capacity control
items.description: Reciprocating compressor capacity control systems give operators the ability to adjust compressor capacity to demand, eliminating recycle.

faqs.q: What is a compressor valve?
faqs.a: A compressor valve controls the flow of gas into and out of the compression chamber, ensuring efficient operation and pressure regulation.

faqs.q: How much of a difference can a compression valve make?
faqs.a: A well-designed valve can significantly improve compressor efficiency, reduce energy consumption, and extend equipment life.

faqs.q: What is the role of valves in reciprocating compressors?
faqs.a: Valves manage the intake and discharge of gas during each piston stroke, directly affecting performance and reliability.

faqs.q: What are the key factors to consider when selecting a valve type?
faqs.a: Consider operating pressure, temperature, gas composition, flow rate, and maintenance requirements.

faqs.q: What types of valves are used in reciprocating compressors?
faqs.a: Common types include plate valves, poppet valves, and reed valves, each suited to specific operating conditions.

faqs.q: How do the valve materials impact their performance?
faqs.a: Material choice affects durability, resistance to corrosion and wear, and suitability for high-pressure or high-temperature environments.

faqs.q: What are the common issues with compressor valves and how to prevent them?
faqs.a: Issues include wear, sticking, and leakage. Prevention involves regular maintenance, proper material selection, and operating within design limits.

faqs.q: What is valve maintenance best practice?
faqs.a: Inspect regularly, clean components, replace worn parts, and monitor performance indicators to avoid unexpected failures.

faqs.q: What are the suction and discharge valves in a reciprocating compressor?
faqs.a: Suction valves allow gas into the cylinder; discharge valves release compressed gas into the system.

faqs.q: What causes the suction and discharge valves to open and close in a reciprocating compressor?
faqs.a: Valve movement is driven by pressure differences during the piston’s cycle—suction opens on intake, discharge opens on compression.

body.text: Capacity control and compressor valve mechanisms are essential for optimizing the efficiency and functionality of reciprocating compressors. body.text: Valve performance and reliability is key to compressor performance. By paying careful attention to reliability in every aspect of the design, Siemens Energy has created a valve that in many applications can run more than 50 percent longer than other valves before needing service. The company has proven it in thousands of hours of tests, many at high speeds and high temperatures, with a wide range of gases. The engineers select the most appropriate valve based on their extensive experience as well as tools such as the Dynamic Valve Analysis (DVA) program.
Variable capacity control systems

Most compressors produce more capacity than needed to allow for process control. The excess capacity is typically recycled to the inlet of the compressor to meet demand. The energy required to recycle the excess capacity is wasted.

Variable capacity control systems give operators the ability to adjust compressor capacity to demand, eliminating recycle. This reduces energy usage and operating costs.Variable capacity control devices are becoming more prevalent in the process market because of increased energy costs and the desire to save energy and related expenses whenever possible.

faqs.q: What is a reciprocating compressor?
faqs.a: A reciprocating compressor is a type of positive displacement compressor that uses pistons driven by a crankshaft to deliver gases at high pressure.

faqs.q: What is the difference between centrifugal and reciprocating compressors?
faqs.a: Centrifugal compressors use a rotating impeller to add velocity to the gas and then convert this velocity into pressure (dynamic compression). In contrast, reciprocating compressors use pistons to compress the gas in a cylinder (positive compression).

faqs.q: How does a reciprocating compressor operate?
faqs.a: A reciprocating compressor operates by using a piston within a cylinder to compress the gas. The piston moves back and forth, driven by crankshaft, drawing in gas during the intake cycle then compressing the gas when piston changes direction.

faqs.q: What opens and closes the valves in a reciprocating compressor?
faqs.a: The valves in a reciprocating compressor operate automatically in response to pressure differences and are designed to open and close at precise times during the piston's movement.

faqs.q: What maintenance and modernization services does Siemens Energy provide for reciprocating compressors?

items.title: Single-Shaft Centrifugal Compressors
items.description: From standard processes to high-pressure applications, single-shaft compressors are the solution for a wide range of industries and process applications.

faqs.q: What are single shaft compressors?
faqs.a: Single shaft compressors are a type of centrifugal compressors that uses a rotating impeller to increase the pressure and velocity of a gas. It is characterized by having one or more impellers mounted on a single shaft, which is supported by bearings at both ends. Single shaft compressors are a reliable and efficient solution for various gas compression applications, particularly those requiring high flow rates and low to moderate pressure ratios. Their compact design, high efficiency, and cost-effectiveness make them a popular choice in many industries. They can be applied in a wide range of industrial applications, including decarbonization and high-pressure processes.

faqs.q: What are the limitations of a single shaft compressor?
faqs.a: Single shaft compressors are not a good fit for very low flow applications and can have lower efficiency at part load operation. They are also more sensitive to applications in which the process gas has widely varying mole weights. In such applications a positive displacement type compressor could be a better fit.

faqs.q: What is the pressure ratio for a single shaft compressor?
faqs.a: The pressure ratio for single shaft compressors can vary widely depending on the specific design and application. For example, horizontally split single-shaft compressors can achieve discharge pressures up to 100 bar (1,450 psi), while vertically split single-shaft compressors can reach up to 1,000 bar (14,500 psi) 56.

faqs.q: What are the common prime movers used for single-shaft centrifugal compressors?
faqs.a: Our single-shaft compressors can be driven by electric motors (both fixed and variable speed), gas turbines or steam turbines depending on the application and energy source availability. We also have designs that can have both motor and gas turbine drivers that can be switched based on grid and fuel availability.

faqs.q: What industries and applications are Siemens Energy single-shaft centrifugal compressors suitable for?
faqs.a: Single shaft compressors are a flexible product used in upstream (onshore/offshore), pipelines and LNG, chemicals (including ammonia and methanol) and petrochemicals, refining, hydrogen, CO2 and decarbonization projects.

faqs.q: How does Siemens Energy ensure ease of maintenance for single-shaft centrifugal compressors?
faqs.a: Our compressors are designed for easy maintenance with our modular cartridge designs which allow fast and easy swapping of compressor internals without removing piping. Remote diagnostics and predictive maintenance services are also available to monitor the health of the compressor.

faqs.q: What support services does Siemens Energy offer to optimize single-shaft centrifugal compressors operation?
faqs.a: We can analyze the existing compressors performance to evaluate the benefit of revamping which could offer an efficiency, range or flow advantage. Materials and subcomponents can also be evaluated for upgrades, offering improved mechanical properties without modifying operating performance. We can upgrade control systems using our proprietary anti surge protection systems, load sharing technology, and continuous monitoring technologies such as remote diagnostics

body.text: From standard processes to high-pressure applications, Siemens Energy single-shaft compressors are the ideal solution for a wide range of industries and process applications. They are designed to customer specifications and API 617 standards. Compression solutions can be supplied in a variety of configurations from skid mounted, combining the compressor with its driver and auxiliaries, to single lift process modules with fully integrated compressors, drivers and process equipment such as coolers, scrubbers, separators, piping, and wiring. Module fabrication can be done in a Siemens Energy location or contracted out to qualified yards in destination countries to fulfill local content requirements.
Horizontally split casings

Covering a wide performance range in terms of pressure ratio and volume flow, the horizontally split single-shaft compressors can compress gases with suction temperatures as low as required for LNG boil-off gas service (-160 °C / -256 °F).

Several process stages can be housed in each casing depending on process requirements. These include straight-through, back-to-back or double flow configurations while side streams and intercooling can be accommodated as well. Up to three casings can be arranged in line to be driven by a single prime mover. The horizontal casing split allows for easy access to the compressor internals for inspection and maintenance without the need to remove the casing from the base plate or to detach process gas piping. Depending on process specifics, optional adjustable inlet guide vanes in front of the first impeller can optimize energy efficiency under part load conditions.

items.title: Single stage radial compressors
items.description: We offer a comprehensive range of single-stage radial compressors for applications in the metallurgical, oil and gas and chemical industries.

faqs.q: What is a single stage compressor?
faqs.a: A single-stage compressor is a type of compressor where the gas is compressed in a single step or stage. This means that there is only one impeller inside the unit and all the pressure is developed in one stage before it is discharged to the next process.

faqs.q: What is the difference between single stage and multi-stage compressors?
faqs.a: The main difference between single stage and multi-stage compressors is the number of times the gas is compressed. In a single stage compressor, the gas is compressed once, while in a multi-stage compressor, the gas is compressed multiple times in different stages (by multiple impellers) to achieve higher pressure.

items.h1: Fatigue Monitoring System: proactive protection for your boiler assets
items.description: Discover Siemens Energy`s Fatigue Monitoring System that empowers you to take control of boiler reliability and performance.

faqs.q: What is Fatigue Monitoring?
faqs.a: Fatigue monitoring is the process of continuously tracking the condition of critical equipment—such as boiler components—in industrial plants to detect signs of material fatigue caused by temperature, pressure, and cyclic mechanical stresses over time.

faqs.q: What is the Fatigue Monitoring System (FMS)?
faqs.a: FMS is an advanced digital solution from Siemens Energy that continuously monitors the fatigue and creep status of critical boiler components in real time, helping operators optimize maintenance, extend asset life, and prevent unexpected failures.

faqs.q: How does FMS assess fatigue in boiler components?
faqs.a: FMS uses real-time temperature and pressure data from the plant’s Distributed Control System (DCS), applies EN 12952 Parts 3 & 4 standards, and calculates creep and low-cycle fatigue through proven algorithms.

faqs.q: Which boiler components can FMS monitor?
faqs.a: FMS typically monitors high-pressure drums, separators, superheater/reheater manifolds and headers, branches, spray water injectors, gate valves, and can easily scale to cover up to 88 components per boiler.

faqs.q: Is Fatigue Monitoring System compatible with any boiler type?
faqs.a: Yes, FMS is versatile and supports vertical/horizontal HRSGs (with or without supplementary firing), conventional fired steam generators, and biomass boilers, using drum-type or Benson once-through evaporator designs.

faqs.q: Does Fatigue Monitoring System require a plant shutdown during installation?
faqs.a: No. FMS installs on a technology server, supports hot commissioning in as little as six months, and does not require unit disassembly or lengthy outages.

faqs.q: Is Fatigue Monitoring System certified for compliance?
faqs.a: Yes, FMS is TÜV-SÜD certified out-of-the-box, providing verifiable, standard-compliant calculations and full transparency for regulatory or audit requirements.

faqs.q: Can Fatigue Monitoring System help save costs on maintenance?
faqs.a: Absolutely. FMS supports early detection of fatigue risks, enables cost-effective inspection planning, reduces unnecessary downtime, and helps prevent expensive repairs—often delivering ROI in under three years.

faqs.q: Can I integrate Fatigue Monitoring System with other digital systems or platforms?
faqs.a: Yes, FMS integrates with Siemens Energy’s Omnivise ecosystem, supports MEP.Core, OPC UA, and cloud-based platforms like AWS IoT, ensuring secure interoperability and unified monitoring.

faqs.q: How do I get started with Siemens Energy’s Fatigue Monitoring System?
faqs.a: Contact Siemens Energy’s experts for a consultation, demo, or site assessment. They will guide you through implementation, customization, and ongoing support to ensure maximum plant reliability and value.

Siemens Energy offers a lifecycle management solution for following up the plant during the whole lifecycle.
One solution for process, safety, electrical and marine systems acts to optimize the OPEX including maintenance costs.
The Oil & Gas industry has been hit by many challenges the last years due to heavy price fluctuations and change in market demand. This has led to changes in the industry.

The focus on cost has always been a priority but new technology availability has enabled new ways of reducing operational cost. The introduction of digital tools and functionalities has the power to transform the way the oil gas industry works.

Typically an ambition is to move from calendar based to condition based maintenance, thus reducing the overall operational cost in the plant. Further operational optimization can be achieved by development of modern remote operated facilities and a focus on reducing time spent on offshore task, which in turn contributes to lower staffing or unmanned facilities. This will also drive the safety aspect but will also challenge the industry related to IT security.

Further it is important to deliver an ICSS solutions in compliance with requested standards and regulations. Seamless integration of power generation and distribution systems including efficient and optimized power management into the ICSS system is an important pre requisite in a modern plant.
Operator systems will be based on accepted standards for human interface providing an easy and intuitive operation of the process plant.

We deliver an ICSS systems providing event driven high quality data to the data repository used for digital data processing, with low bandwidth and high resolution. This enables advanced and reliable condition monitoring of all instrumentation and process equipment as well as enabling necessary work process changes in the plant.
We believe that a full concept E-A-D (Electrical, Automation, Digitalization) with its seamless integration of data represents the best choice for any future offshore production facility.
Digital solutions to reduce maintenance costs
Omnivise for Offshore is a fully scalable digitalization platform from Siemens Energy with the objectives to

items: Improve Production Efficiency of the asset and higher overall ROI
Improve Safety

body.text: The solution has four main components: gateway, historian, analytics and dashboard. The gateway can connect to several generations of control systems and third-party systems for collecting data. The historian will hold high resolution event-based plant data for the lifetime of the plant. Analytics will do condition-based monitoring of equipment and alarm/maintenance/production/safety-reporting. The dashboard features live trending, process pictures, dashboards, KPI displays, playback and much more. The solution can be used either as a local only solution or a cloud-based solution.

Assets are a central part of the Omnivise for Offshore solution. An asset can be a pump, motor, valve and other field equipment, but also switches, routers and IT equipment. Asset templates contains both the condition/performance monitoring to be performed in by analytics framework and the layout of the equipment in the Omnivise for Offshore dashboard. The results of each condition monitored will be output to a time series tag value. There will also be written a health state for each condition, indicating normal, warning or alert. These values can be visualized in customer dashboard as traffic lights or charts. The template is typically created once and then it's quick to configure multiple instances. In Omnivise for Offshore dashboard each equipment will have its own homepage.
Remote Monitoring and Analytics

Predictive Maintenance is an important function to reduce the maintenance effort and to move the maintenance planning to the onshore organization. The main SOGO philosophy is to push data upwards in the hierarchy and store the data in a Historian or Cloud system. SOGO Analytics runs on top of the Historian and thus has all data sources available (such as ICSS data, vibration data, IoT, engineering data ++).
Event based updates

All data collecting from the PCS 7 controllers are event based. This means that data is updated on change and not pulled/polled at an interval from the controllers. At the end of each logic sequence, the controllers will send a snapshot of a selection of values to the gateway if the value is changed outside the dead band configured in the controllers. This has several benefits like high resolution data when it matters: like monitoring of critical temperatures on equipment. Values that are rarely changed don't have to store duplicate values that have to be cleansed in the historian at a later stage. The network traffic is also kept at a bare minimum since only update values are sent. The PLC is pushing the data, so there is no need for a lot of computing power doing polling of all tags on the gateway.
Valve example:

items: Monitor movement time for maintenance purposes
Verify correct operation according to Cause & Effect
Rapid changing process value – all transients picked up

body.text: Remote operation and normally unmanned installation (NUI) concept

The flexible and scalable ICSS solution, its data acquisition and supporting architecture provides the backbone for facilitating NUI operation and maximizing maintenance efficiency. The ICSS and supporting infrastructure for such facilities is an enhancement of existing designs and practices rather than a fundamental change.
The base requirement for NUI operation is facilitation of remote control and operation of the ICSS and supporting infrastructure to be highly integrated.

The complete integration will enable the fully redundant ICSS to provide enhanced data acquisition and serve as the main conduit for data transfer to additional support software, such as Condition Based Monitoring and predictive maintenance tools. Subsea monitoring and/or control can also be facilitated and integrated into the same system.
The Electrification, Automation, and Digitalization Concept (EAD)

Siemens Energy as a leading electrical equipment manufacturer and power solution provider is able to integrate electrical solutions with Omnivise Digital to provide digital benefits to the electrical system.

For the Electrical equipment, all measurement values and alarms feed into the ICSS and conditioning monitoring is performed in the IMS. The Engineering Station handles configuration and is used for detailed diagnosis. The electrical system fully conforms to offshore industry standards.
Figure gives an overview of the interfaces for the main electrical equipment. Via the Intelligent Electronic Devices (IED), optimal communication to PCS 7 system is ensured.
We deliver a fully integrated solution based on common libraries with data consistency in the full EAD line of plant operations and maintenance.

The electrical system is designed for easy expansion and flexibility. It is built on a network structure with a high degree of integration of all systems for operation and maintenance, and is designed to support remote operation from onshore. All main electrical equipment is enabled for condition-based monitoring, making it easier to carry out necessary maintenance without extensive manpower.
Brownfield digital solutions
In addition to greenfield solutions, Siemens Energy implements solutions on existing facilities.

Such solutions enable efficient decision making and proactive operational management on existing facilities, via access to timely data, data visualization, monitoring/alerting capabilities and access to relevant systems and supporting documentation.
For brownfield solutions, please get in touch to discuss your needs.

faqs.q: What is Power Plant Performance Monitoring?
faqs.a: Performance Monitoring is a digital solution that combines data monitoring with expert analysis to optimize power plant performance by recovering power lost to thermodynamic degradation.

faqs.q: How does Omnivise Performance Monitoring improve power plant efficiency?
faqs.a: It improves efficiency by identifying performance deviations, optimizing fuel consumption, reducing emissions, and enhancing reliability to maximize power output and profitability.

faqs.q: What types of power plant performance issues can Omnivise Performance Monitoring detect?
faqs.a: It detects issues such as thermodynamic degradation, operational inefficiencies, increased fuel consumption, and conditions that lead to higher emissions and downtime.

faqs.q: How does the Thermodynamic Digital Twin work?
faqs.a: The Thermodynamic Digital Twin compares your plant’s actual performance against an optimal expected output under the same conditions, helping to identify and quantify performance gaps.

faqs.q: What benefits can my power plant expect from using Omnivise Performance Monitoring?
faqs.a: Benefits include reclaimed power, improved fuel efficiency, reduced CO2 and NOx emissions, increased plant reliability, better merit order positioning, and higher revenue.

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy experts support the power plant performance monitoring?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy performance experts analyze your plant data, provide actionable insights, make recommendations, and conduct monthly reviews to support continuous improvement.

faqs.q: How can I obtain a power plant performance testing software ?
faqs.a: You can contact Siemens Energy directly. For more information or to schedule a demo, please fill out the contact form you will find in this website and a representative will contact you.

faqs.q: Can I access my power plant’s condition monitoring data remotely?
faqs.a: Yes, Siemens Energy’s Omnivise Power Monitoring solution offers secure, cloud-based access to detailed power plant performance reports anytime and anywhere via a web-based application.

faqs.q: Who is currently using Siemens Energy’s Omnivise Performance Monitoring?
faqs.a: Over 800 power units worldwide utilize Siemens Energy’s monitoring and optimization expertise to enhance reliability and output.

faqs.q: How can I get started with Omnivise Performance Monitoring for my power plant?
faqs.a: You can contact Siemens Energy directly to explore tailored solutions and discover how Omnivise can unlock your power plant’s full potential.

faqs.q: Are there any plant configuration requirements?
faqs.a: Omnivise Performance Monitoring is offered for all large combustion and steam turbines in the Siemens Energy fleet. We recommend Gas Turbine only for simple cycle units and combined cycle power plants with the objective of thermal degradation visibility on their gas turbines only. Total Plant is recommended for steam and combined cycle power plants with large number of operating hours per year, and for plants that require maximum capacity and efficiency.

faqs.q: What services are included with Omnivise Performance Monitoring?
faqs.a: The solution comes with a digital thermal twin tailored to your specific power plant. It also includes a web application for data visualization, scheduled reports, and access to Siemens Energy performance experts to review the recommendations. The scope can be tailored to the total plant monitoring or the gas turbine only.

body.text: Optimizing power plant performance is crucial for operators seeking to reduce costs, lower emissions, and maximize profitability in today's rapidly evolving energy landscape. Performance monitoring is at the core of optimizing power plant performance.

Siemens Energy has developed Omnivise Performance Monitoring: a digital solution that combines data monitoring with expert analysis to provide actionable recommendations for recovering thermodynamic degradation.
What sets Omnivise Performance Monitoring apart?

Omnivise Performance Monitoring aids your margin by ultimately assisting you in generating more power, improving fuel efficiency, optimizing emissions, advancing merit order positioning and overall reliability and availability for increased revenue.
Power degradation recovery: reclaim power lost to operational degradation
Advance merit order: your plant can move up in dispatch order
Improve fuel efficiency: reduce fuel consumption and heat rate
Improve reliability: optimize operational process activities and minimize downtime
Minimize emissions: reduce CO2 and NOx emissions
Increase profits and revenues: recovering power and increasing efficiency directly contribute to higher revenues

Explore the capabilities of Omnivise Performance Monitoring in enhancing power recovery, and hear a success story from a satisfied customer, demonstrating the practical benefits of our innovative digital solution.
Video: Omnivise Performance Monitoring combines data monitoring with expert analysis to recover thermodynamic degradation.
How plant performance monitoring works

Power plant performance monitoring works by continuously collecting and analyzing data on various operational parameters, such as temperature, pressure, and power output, using sensors and control systems.

Thermodynamic degradation is monitored using a Thermodynamic Digital Twin and comparing the actual performance of your plant assets against their expected optimal output. Using the digital application, performance gaps are identified by analyzing deviations under the same operating conditions between the plant and the Digital Twin output.
Siemens Energy performance experts will review this information to develop actionable insights and recommendations to recover the degradation.
Plant performance monitoring enables power recovery

Siemens Energy's advanced digital solution is designed to boost power recovery by detecting and addressing performance deviations. By utilizing their thermodynamic digital twin, Siemens Energy identifies thermodynamic degradation and implements solutions to correct it, ensuring power plant operations are maintained at optimal efficiency.
Siemens Energy experts provide actionable insights to recover degraded power, leading to improved resulting in enhanced energy output.
This video features a performance monitoring expert who will explain everything to you.
Power plant condition monitoring expertise is included

Siemens Energy includes power plant condition monitoring expertise in its Managed Services. The company provides advanced analytics software and leverages the expertise of seasoned Performance Engineers through its Power Diagnostics® Services group. The solution delivers early issue detection, downtime reduction through the use of analytics and diagnostics tools, as well as actionable insights and recommendations to help optimise your assets.

Siemens Energy experts will assess the actual performance of your power plant against the expected optimal output and hold one-on-one consultations to review and explain your power plant performance data from the previous month. You will receive a detailed report through a web-based application. The cloud-based service ensures that you can access your performance data at any time.
With Siemens Energy solution you benefit from:
bold: With Siemens Energy solution you benefit from:

items: 24/7 early detection of issues before they become costly problems
Reduced downtime, enabled by continuous analytics and diagnostic insights
Custom recommendations and monthly one-on-one reviews with performance experts
Secure, cloud-based access to your plant's performance data and detailed web-based reports any time, anywhere
