items.description: Omnivise T3000 is a reliable and scalable control system with enhanced cybersecurity and seamless integration for optimized power generation and industrial processes.
items.tags: Digital services;;;Renewable power;;;Control systems;;;Conventional power;;;Instrumentation and control

faqs.q: What is Omnivise T3000?
faqs.a: Omnivise T3000 is a control system for power plants and industrial processes, developed by Siemens Energy. It is is a scalable and future-proof system that supports both conventional and renewable energy sources as well as real-time monitoring, cybersecurity, and lifecycle support. Designed for the specific requirements of the energy market, it can manage both the complexity of large power plants and the aggregation of simpler automation requirements.

faqs.q: What types of power generation plants is Omnivise T3000 suitable for?
faqs.a: Omnivise T3000 supports all types of generation units, from conventional power plants to decentralized or renewable sources. It controls and integrates combined and simple (open) cycle plants, hybrid systems (including PV and CSP), offshore wind farms, geothermal, biomass and waste-to-energy facilities, carbon capture units, power-to-x plants, synchronous condensers, as well as substations – to name but a few.

faqs.q: How does Omnivise T3000 enhance plant efficiency and operator training?
faqs.a: Omnivise T3000 integrates control solutions for optimized plant operations, enabling automatic adjustments in response to changes in load, fuel quality and fuel feed. It connects assets on a single platform for centralized, remote control. The Omnivise T3000 system's integrated simulator supports operator training in realistic conditions, ensuring preparedness for real-world scenarios.

faqs.q: What cybersecurity features does Omnivise T3000 offer?
faqs.a: Omnivise T3000 uses a defense-in-depth strategy with multilayered security measures to protect power plants and other critical infrastructure. It meets international cybersecurity standards like IEC 62443 and reflects global requirements and legislation. It includes malware protection, security event monitoring, configuration change management, application whitelisting and other cybersecurity capabilities.

faqs.q: Does Omnivise T3000 support integration with other systems and communication protocols?
faqs.a: The Omnivise T3000 control system is built for seamless connectivity and interoperability, supporting a wide range of systems and communication protocols. It incorporates standards like IEC 61850 to integrate third-party systems and ensures secure operations through VPNs and data encryption.

faqs.q: Can Omnivise T3000 be remotely accessed and controlled?
faqs.a: The Omnivise T3000 system supports easy remote access for remote operation and maintenance. Its SCADA functionality connects various components through a single platform in a centralized view, allowing users to monitor and manage data with maximum flexibility. This enables the operation of multiple remote plants from a central control center, supported through secure, cyber-secure connections.

faqs.q: What kind of support and services are available for Omnivise T3000 users?
faqs.a: To maintain optimal performance and cybersecurity levels for Omnivise T3000, a comprehensive range of services is available, addressing both system- and cybersecurity-related aspects. These services range from system support via our expert tech line to system updates and on-site support, as well as system and software maintenance and patching.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of Omnivise T3000 compared to other power plant control systems?
faqs.a: Omnivise T3000 stands out with its integrated platform, broad application range, seamless renewable integration, and user-friendly HMI. It offers superior cybersecurity, fast diagnostics, and strong regulatory compliance. Scalable and future-ready, it ensures easy maintenance and long-term cost savings—making it a top choice for power plants focused on flexibility, efficiency, and protection.

faqs.q: Can Omnivise T3000 support digital transformation and future energy market requirements?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy’s Omnivise T3000 supports digital transformation with cloud-based analytics, digital twins, and IoT integration. Its scalable, flexible architecture adapts to renewable energy, hydrogen, and storage systems, meeting future energy market demands. Advanced diagnostics and cybersecurity ensure efficiency and compliance, future-proofing operations for evolving grids.

body.text: New markets, new rules, new concepts: The energy landscape is changing faster than ever before. In this dynamic environment, Omnivise T3000 remains a constant for you. SPPA-T3000, which has proven itself for decades, offers more than you expect from a control system.
bold: New markets, new rules, new concepts:

body.text: The latest release of Omnivise T3000 supports you with innovations you need to build a bridge to the energy system of tomorrow. For conventional power plants as well as decentralized power generation with renewable energy sources, for any plants and any size – perfectly tailored to our digital solution portfolio. Control the energy system of tomorrow with Omnivise T3000.
Your bridge into the future

Omnivise T3000 is your bridge into the future of intelligent energy control. As Siemens Energy's advanced Distributed Control System (DCS), it empowers operators to seamlessly manage hybrid energy systems, integrate renewables, and ensure cybersecurity - all from a unified platform. With its scalable architecture and proven reliability across thousands of installations, Omnivise T3000 transforms complexity into clarity, helping you navigate the energy transition with confidence and control.
Video: Omnivise T3000 - your future-proof integrated control system
Proven technology of today with the innovations of tomorrow
Omnivise T3000 combines decades of proven control system reliability with cutting-edge innovations tailored for the evolving energy landscape.
Expert Talks about the new features in Omnivise T3000

Our expert talks provide you with specific insights how Omnivise T3000 allows you to boost efficiency for your plant. Just click on one of the videos below to learn more on the SCADA functionalities, cybersecurity and simulation with our proven control system.
The answer to challenging times

Omnivise T3000 is not just the most advanced control system, equipped to meet the challenges facing both the traditional and the new power generation landscape. More than anything else, it will continue to fulfill the important task of running your plant in the future – efficiently, safely and reliably.
Future-proof, pioneering, secure, supported
Identify and exploit opportunities

Flexible, scalable, and cost-efficient, Omnivise T3000 is the control system unlike anything in the textbooks. It's designed for ever-changing markets, upcoming requirements and endless new opportunities. For conventional power generation plants and a wide range of new applications like wind, solar, hydrogen, and storage using SCADA functionalities. With the latest technology, at any scale, and for any challenge posed by a dynamic energy market. Choose today – and choose long-term success.
Your goals, our innovations

We designed Omnivise T3000 as a future-proof platform for digital solutions that will open up new possibilities for you. A simulation function that works as a digital twin of your plant, enabling you to digitally test new configurations and train the operators without incurring actual costs. And let's not forget the remote access to data – at any time and with maximum flexibility. Or the use of cutting-edge software technology and the cyber-secure connection.
Secure today and tomorrow

With Omnivise T3000, you are opting for reliable operation of your automation and control system both today and in the future. The defense-in-depth concept, already proven in thousands of applications, and certification according to the latest international standards, make Omnivise T3000 the perfect control system to transform your ideas into reality – with the precise level of security that meets your requirements.
Understanding is the beginning

Your success is what drives us. Understanding your needs is the basis of our collaboration. This is something you will quickly notice when you talk to us about new pathways to success, what the future holds for the energy business, and how you can shape it individually for energy projects of any size. We draw on our experience from nearly 4,000 installations worldwide. We're here for you worldwide, and we'll support you with efficient project management as well as short implementation phases. Naturally, we also offer long-term service and continously improve and maintain your control system according to your needs.
Experience more technical details on Omnivise T3000 in our interactive brochure
Omnivise T3000 combines a multitude of innovative features with proven functionality. Explore them!

The requirements for reliability, cybersecurity and flexibility are constantly growing in the energy markets. At the same time, they are becoming increasingly diverse, requiring rapid decision-making to take advantage of opportunities. Omnivise T3000 helps you make the right decisions by allowing you to virtually test changes before you implement them. This allows you to break new ground without incurring large costs. Control technology that is your bridge to the future must offer all of this – and much more.
Cybersecurity
Built-in security for your plant

As part of the critical infrastructure, plants in the energy market have to fulfil more stringent requirements than ever before. With the risk of cyber attacks, this means looking beyond operational concerns and protecting plants against hacker attacks – and documenting compliance according to all legal requirements. Thanks to built-in security and our comprehensive cybersecurity portfolio, Omnivise T3000 is ideally suited to help operators protect their plant.

The defense-in-depth concept strengthens your system to withstand external attacks. Omnivise T3000 is officially certified by TÜV SÜD according to IEC 62443, the leading standard for IT security for industrial communication networks. This is just one example of the numerous internationally recognized standards for which the Omnivise T3000 system as well as our development process is certified for. We provide long-term support so you can rely on a system that is always up-to-date. We support current hardware on a long-term basis and provide tried and tested security patches for the software at any time during operation. For you, this means long-term security – with no downtime. In addition, our Cybersecurity Operations Center (cSOC) helps you defend against or resolve cyberattacks 24/7.
T3000 SCADA
Be prepared for future opportunities
Fostering renewable energy production is crucial to enable decarbonization. Thanks to its latest SCADA functionalities, Omnivise T3000 is a key enabler to control renewable operation and production.

Today, operators don't have to manage just conventional or renewable power generation. The trend is moving clearly towards virtual power plants with mixed generation fleets. Omnivise T3000 is the scalable and future-proof system for the entire lifecycle. It can manage both the complexity of large power plants as well as the aggregation of simpler automation requirements. But most important, it can combine all types of generation units by centralized process control. In addition, a scalable SCADA system enables you to prepare for future opportunities and requirements like direct marketing or integration of hydropower. Discover the offshore wind controls website
T3000 Simulator
Safety net for reliable operations

Train operators, test engineering, commission virtually, optimize plants – there are numerous reasons to have a simulation tool of your I&C system. The fully integrated T3000 Simulator expands the system's possibilities. It is not a separate tool, it is part of Omnivise T3000 and thus provides immediate and direct simulation in the T3000 HMI and runs on T3000 hardware. This sets the foundation for perfectly trained and highly-qualified operators who can master fault event conditions reliably and are specifically prepared for critical situations.
This brings you practical benefits for the reliable operation of your assets:

items: Better basis for decision-making – know what the consequences of a planned change will be before making a decision
Optimal development possibilities – detailed testing of the effects of measures in engineering, retrofits or replacement of plant components, changes or adjustments in Omnivise T3000, etc.
Non-reactive simulation – the digital twin of Omnivise T3000 shows you the real plant behavior before any real change is made
Keep plant know-how in-house – ideal for staff training by your experienced colleagues, hands-on, with the actual control system
Cost security – no additional software or hardware required

body.text: Service
Support you can rely on

We support customers from more than 900 plants worldwide with high-quality remote and local services. Our Remote Expert Centers (REC) are home to more than 50 trained experts worldwide equipped with the latest data communication systems and direct secure access to the engineering data of your plant.
We are ready to step in at critical moments via remote connection in order to quickly find a solution – 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
Service along the entire lifecycle

Our experts support you with know-how and expertise. Our regular inspections as part of periodic plant maintenance activities, clever spare parts concepts, long-term solutions to extend service life and our intelligent diagnostics solutions bring a genuinely preventive element to plant maintenance and detect faults before they can trigger costly failures.

Our global training network with highly experienced and qualified instructors can provide a wide range of training options with cutting edge technology, designed specifically for various plant personnel positions. Many of our courses can be customized to meet your schedule and budget requirements. Let us transform your plant performance with knowledge transfer to your staff.
Omnivise Digital
Digital transformation is more than just technology
bold: Digital transformation is more than just technology

body.text: Changing markets require in-depth data analysis, interpretation, and advice to make an impact on the bottom line. As a result, knowing that digital transformation entails more than just technology, we do offer a broad portfolio of digital services, but also a collaborative approach to boost your performance with custom solutions. It is a business model born out of our expertise and domain know-how that helps you profit from digitalization, experience, and highly skilled manpower.

Omnivise Digital Services Portfolio offers you a data-supported, collaborative approach to optimize your power plant operations and maintenance with customized solutions – all based on Omnivise T3000 as data platform.

Together, we analyze your data, provide you with advice on making smarter decisions, and finalize tasks to improve asset-, unit- and fleet operations. Manage the performance of your energy assets with real time data analysis, lower operational and maintenance costs, mitigate risks and achieve higher return on investment.
Highlights that will take you further

A control system is only as good as the benefits it offers you. Once you start working with Omnivise T3000, you will immediately notice how good it is. The intuitive user interface, the integrated simulator, system operation that is not tied to a specific hardware, the ability to remotely access your data, all combined with a comprehensive cybersecurity concept: Omnivise T3000 offers you every opportunity for long-term success in the energy market. Not to mention our experienced project teams, who support you worldwide with their wealth of expertise.

Get answers: FAQs on Omnivise T3000 system
What is Omnivise T3000?

Omnivise T3000 is a control system for power plants and industrial processes, developed by Siemens Energy. It is is a scalable and future-proof system that supports both conventional and renewable energy sources as well as real-time monitoring, cybersecurity, and lifecycle support. Designed for the specific requirements of the energy market, it can manage both the complexity of large power plants and the aggregation of simpler automation requirements.
What types of power generation plants is Omnivise T3000 suitable for?

Omnivise T3000 supports all types of generation units, from conventional power plants to decentralized or renewable sources. It controls and integrates combined and simple (open) cycle plants, hybrid systems (including PV and CSP), offshore wind farms, geothermal, biomass and waste-to-energy facilities, carbon capture units, power-to-x plants, synchronous condensers, as well as substations – to name but a few.
How does Omnivise T3000 enhance plant efficiency and operator training?

Omnivise T3000 integrates control solutions for optimized plant operations, enabling automatic adjustments in response to changes in load, fuel quality and fuel feed. It connects assets on a single platform for centralized, remote control. The Omnivise T3000 system's integrated simulator supports operator training in realistic conditions, ensuring preparedness for real-world scenarios.
What cybersecurity features does Omnivise T3000 offer?

Omnivise T3000 uses a defense-in-depth strategy with multilayered security measures to protect power plants and other critical infrastructure. It meets international cybersecurity standards like IEC 62443 and reflects global requirements and legislation. It includes malware protection, security event monitoring, configuration change management, application whitelisting and other cybersecurity capabilities.
Does Omnivise T3000 support integration with other systems and communication protocols?

The Omnivise T3000 control system is built for seamless connectivity and interoperability, supporting a wide range of systems and communication protocols. It incorporates standards like IEC 61850 to integrate third-party systems and ensures secure operations through VPNs and data encryption.
Can Omnivise T3000 be remotely accessed and controlled?

The Omnivise T3000 system supports easy remote access for remote operation and maintenance. Its SCADA functionality connects various components through a single platform in a centralized view, allowing users to monitor and manage data with maximum flexibility. This enables the operation of multiple remote plants from a central control center, supported through secure, cyber-secure connections.
What kind of support and services are available for Omnivise T3000 users?

To maintain optimal performance and cybersecurity levels for Omnivise T3000, a comprehensive range of services is available, addressing both system- and cybersecurity-related aspects. These services range from system support via our expert tech line to system updates and on-site support, as well as system and software maintenance and patching.
What are the advantages of Omnivise T3000 compared to other power plant control systems?

Omnivise T3000 stands out with its integrated platform, broad application range, seamless renewable integration, and user-friendly HMI. It offers superior cybersecurity, fast diagnostics, and strong regulatory compliance. Scalable and future-ready, it ensures easy maintenance and long-term cost savings—making it a top choice for power plants focused on flexibility, efficiency, and protection.
Can Omnivise T3000 support digital transformation and future energy market requirements?

Siemens Energy's Omnivise T3000 supports digital transformation with cloud-based analytics, digital twins, and IoT integration. Its scalable, flexible architecture adapts to renewable energy, hydrogen, and storage systems, meeting future energy market demands. Advanced diagnostics and cybersecurity ensure efficiency and compliance, future-proofing operations for evolving grids.

faqs.q: What is a disconnector (disconnect switch) and how does it work?
faqs.a: Disconnectors are mechanical switching devices to guarantee safety for the people working in the high voltage network, providing visible gap isolation of line section. Earthing switches ensure absolute de-energization of high voltage components in a circuit or switchgear.

faqs.q: What are the different types of disconnectors available?
faqs.a: centre break disconnectors, knee-type disconnectors, double-side-break disconnectors, vertical break disconnectors, pantograph, freestanding earthing switches, built-on earthing switches

faqs.q: What criteria should be considered when choosing a disconnector switch?
faqs.a: Providing an isolating distance between substation parts, they grant a safe, reliable and visible interruption of the current flow.

faqs.q: What are common industrial applications of disconnectors?
faqs.a: Disconnectors are an essential part of electrical power substations, AIS as well as GIS. They indicate a visible isolating distance in an isolated gap.

faqs.q: Are disconnectors operated manually or automatically?
faqs.a: disconnectors are equipped with a motor drive; however, the motor operating mechanism can also be operated manually with a hand crank.

faqs.q: What is the purpose of an earthing switch?
faqs.a: Earthing switches ensure absolute de-energization of high voltage components in a circuit or switchgear. They serve to protect people working in a substation and make sure that after switching actions there is no voltage potential left at the substation parts.

faqs.q: What voltage range do Siemens Energy disconnectors and earthing switches cover?
faqs.a: Voltage level from 40.5 kV up to 1200 kV, rated current up to 5000 A, rated short circuit current up to 80 kA, ambient temperature - 60 ... + 55°C.

items.title: Flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS)
items.description: Explore Siemens Energy’s flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) to enhance AC grid reliability, boost power quality, and increase transmission capacity.

faqs.q: Why do we need grid stabilization?
faqs.a: Since power is produced on demand, it's critical to ensure that the power system frequency and voltage remains within nominal ranges. Maintaining this balance is necessary to keep the power grid stable and efficient.

faqs.q: What are flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) and its application?
faqs.a: FACTS are power electronic based devices used to improve the controllability and increase the power transfer capability of AC transmission systems by absorbing and providing of reactive power.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of FACTS?
faqs.a: FACTS can provide high dynamic reactive power to respond to voltage fluctuations caused by load changes or faults in the grid.

faqs.q: What are the main types of FACTS devices?
faqs.a: The main types of flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) devices include STATCOM (SVC PLUS®), E-STATCOM (SVC PLUS® FS), synchronous condenser, fixed series capacitor (FSC), and mechanically switched capacitors (MSC and MSCDN). These devices are integral to enhancing grid stability and efficiency.

faqs.q: How do FACTS support renewable energy integration?
faqs.a: FACTS devices support the integration of renewable energy sources like wind and solar by enhancing grid stability, adaptability, and resilience. They manage the variability and intermittency of renewables by dynamically controlling voltage and reactive power, allowing for efficient power flow management. This ensures seamless integration into the grid, maintaining balance between supply and demand as renewable penetration increases, ultimately contributing to a more reliable and responsive power system.

faqs.q: Can FACTS increase the capacity of existing transmission lines?
faqs.a: Yes, FACTS can significantly increase the capacity of existing transmission lines. FACTS devices enhance grid performance by absorbing or providing reactive power, which improves the power transfer capability and efficiency of AC transmission systems. By optimizing the flow of electricity through the existing infrastructure, FACTS devices enable higher power transfer capabilities, reducing the need for constructing new transmission lines. This optimization allows for more efficient use of current assets, ultimately increasing the overall capacity of the transmission network.

faqs.q: How is Siemens Energy advancing FACTS technology?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy advances FACTS technology by constantly optimizing existing solutions and developing new features. Our commitment to innovation ensures that FACTS devices continue to meet evolving grid demands, enhancing performance and reliability in modern power systems.

faqs.q: Why do grids need power factor correction?
faqs.a: Without power factor correction the power lines and other equipment would be utilized with reactive power which limits utilization with active power and will not operate at optimal condition.

faqs.q: What is grid-forming?
faqs.a: Grid-forming FACTS devices can operate on very weak grids, while grid-following devices require a more stable grid. Grid-forming devices use their built-in active power source to respond inherent to grid events.

faqs.q: Which additional features can be provided by FACTS?
faqs.a: Main additional features are: active harmonic filtering up to four different harmonics simultaneouslyload balancing (negative phase sequence control)POD (power oscillation damping)

body.text: The accelerating global energy transition, driven by the increasing integration of decentralized renewable energy sources, presents significant challenges in maintaining reliable and stable grid operations. Flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) are crucial in modernizing and stabilizing power grids, offering comprehensive solutions to enhance grid reliability, stability, and transmission efficiency.

Siemens Energy, a global leader in power transmission, operates across all continents and possesses extensive experience in addressing global environmental challenges. body.text: SVC PLUS® (STATCOM)

The cutting-edge SVC PLUS® offers a cost-effective, space-efficient, and flexible solution for reactive power compensation. Utilizing advanced multilevel voltage-source converter (VSC) technology, it enhances dynamic stability and power quality within the grid.
SVC PLUS FS® (E-STATCOM)

The SVC PLUS® frequency stabilizer emulates system inertia by injecting high active power into the grid when necessary. Additionally, it provides voltage support through reactive power compensation, ensuring enhanced grid stability and performance.
Synchronous condenser

Synchronous condensers enhance grid stability, particularly in transmission systems with significant renewable energy input. They deliver short-circuit power, inertia, and reactive power compensation, ensuring robust and reliable grid performance.
Fixed series capacitor (FSC)
The fixed series capacitor (FSC) is a key component of the series compensation portfolio, utilizing capacitors to enhance transmission system stability and increase power transmission capacity.
Mechanically switched capacitors (MSC and MSCDN)

Mechanically switched devices (MSC/MSCDN) are the most economical reactive power compensation devices. MSCs provide a robust solution for voltage control and network stabilization under steady-state conditions. The MSCDN additionally includes a damping network to prevent resonance conditions in the electrical system.
Dynamic power flow control

The dynamic power flow control solution manages power flow within milliseconds, stabilizing the AC grid even in critical situations (Grid code N-1). It maximizes the use of existing grid capacity while ensuring maximum protection.
Grid resilience

Our high-voltage solutions, products, and services facilitate the efficient, loss-minimal transportation of renewable energy to global cities and hubs. By leveraging cutting-edge digital technologies, we optimize grid performance, effectively managing large volumes of fluctuating energy and ultra-short-term renewable energy storage.
Grid-forming

Grid-forming technology enables stable grid voltage without relying on external references. It reduces dependence on external influences and maintains voltage and frequency during disturbances and load changes.

Get answers: FAQs on flexible AC transmission systems
Why do we need grid stabilization?

Since power is produced on demand, it's critical to ensure that the power system frequency and voltage remains within nominal ranges. Maintaining this balance is necessary to keep the power grid stable and efficient.
What are flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) and its application?
FACTS are power electronic based devices used to improve the controllability and increase the power transfer capability of AC transmission systems by absorbing and providing of reactive power.
What are the benefits of FACTS?
FACTS can provide high dynamic reactive power to respond to voltage fluctuations caused by load changes or faults in the grid.
What are the main types of FACTS devices?

The main types of flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) devices include STATCOM (SVC PLUS®), E-STATCOM (SVC PLUS® FS), synchronous condenser, fixed series capacitor (FSC), and mechanically switched capacitors (MSC and MSCDN). These devices are integral to enhancing grid stability and efficiency.
How do FACTS support renewable energy integration?

FACTS devices support the integration of renewable energy sources like wind and solar by enhancing grid stability, adaptability, and resilience. They manage the variability and intermittency of renewables by dynamically controlling voltage and reactive power, allowing for efficient power flow management. This ensures seamless integration into the grid, maintaining balance between supply and demand as renewable penetration increases, ultimately contributing to a more reliable and responsive power system.
Can FACTS increase the capacity of existing transmission lines?

Yes, FACTS can significantly increase the capacity of existing transmission lines. FACTS devices enhance grid performance by absorbing or providing reactive power, which improves the power transfer capability and efficiency of AC transmission systems. By optimizing the flow of electricity through the existing infrastructure, FACTS devices enable higher power transfer capabilities, reducing the need for constructing new transmission lines. This optimization allows for more efficient use of current assets, ultimately increasing the overall capacity of the transmission network.
How is Siemens Energy advancing FACTS technology?

Siemens Energy advances FACTS technology by constantly optimizing existing solutions and developing new features. Our commitment to innovation ensures that FACTS devices continue to meet evolving grid demands, enhancing performance and reliability in modern power systems.
Why do grids need power factor correction?
Without power factor correction the power lines and other equipment would be utilized with reactive power which limits utilization with active power and will not operate at optimal condition.
What is grid-forming?

Grid-forming FACTS devices can operate on very weak grids, while grid-following devices require a more stable grid. Grid-forming devices use their built-in active power source to respond inherent to grid events.
Which additional features can be provided by FACTS?
Main additional features are:

items: active harmonic filtering up to four different harmonics simultaneously
load balancing (negative phase sequence control)
POD (power oscillation damping)

faqs.q: What are Converter Controlled Series Capacitors (CCSC PLUS)?
faqs.a: CCSC PLUS is Siemens Energy's platform-based dynamic series compensation solution for high-voltage AC transmission grids. It combines a fixed series capacitor with a converter branch based on voltage source converter (VSC) and modular multilevel converter (MMC) technology, providing real-time bidirectional impedance control and advanced power flow control without a high-voltage transformer. It belongs to Siemens Energy's FACTS portfolio and replaces the UPFC concept with a simpler, more cost-competitive architecture.

faqs.q: How does CCSC PLUS differ from a Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC)?
faqs.a: A TCSC controls an inductor in parallel with a capacitor. CCSC PLUS uses an MMC-based voltage source converter, which injects a clean voltage with minimal harmonics and can operate in both the capacitive and the inductive direction – a wider and more flexible control range than TCSC.

faqs.q: How does CCSC PLUS compare to modular SSSC solutions?
faqs.a: Modular static synchronous series compensators perform well at moderate line ratings, but their per-phase module count makes them costly and physically large at high line currents. CCSC PLUS is designed for line ratings up to 4,000 A and delivers equivalent or better impedance control at those power levels, with a lower cost per unit of compensation and a smaller footprint.

faqs.q: What is power oscillation damping, and does CCSC PLUS support it?
faqs.a: Power oscillation damping (POD) suppresses inter-area electromechanical oscillations that can destabilize interconnected AC grids, a growing concern as synchronous generation is displaced by converter-interfaced renewables. CCSC PLUS includes a dedicated POD control loop that modulates series impedance in response to detected oscillations, improving transient stability without additional hardware.

faqs.q: Can CCSC PLUS mitigate sub-synchronous resonance (SSR)?
faqs.a: Yes. SSR, SSTI (sub-synchronous torsional interaction) and SSCI (sub-synchronous control interaction) can cause mechanical damage to generator shafts and instability in inverter-based plants on series-compensated corridors. CCSC PLUS uses active dynamic impedance control to counteract sub-synchronous currents as an integrated function of the control system, removing the need for separate SSR filters.

faqs.q: What happens during a grid fault (N-1 event)?
faqs.a: CCSC PLUS includes an emergency dispatch mode that can be activated automatically or by the TSO on detection of an N-1 contingency, such as the loss of a parallel line. In this mode the system maximizes power flow on the remaining circuit within its thermal rating, maintaining supply security and reducing the risk of cascading outages.

faqs.q: Is CCSC PLUS part of Siemens Energy's FACTS portfolio?
faqs.a: Yes. CCSC PLUS sits within Siemens Energy's Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) portfolio, alongside SVC PLUS® (STATCOM), SVC PLUS® FS (E-STATCOM), Fixed Series Capacitors (FSC), synchronous condensers and mechanically switched capacitors (MSC/MSCDN). The converter technology is derived directly from the SVC PLUS® platform.

faqs.q: What voltage and current levels does CCSC PLUS support?
faqs.a: The current platform is designed for line voltages up to 400 kV and line current ratings up to 4,000 A, covering the majority of high-voltage transmission applications. Applications at higher line voltages can be discussed with the Siemens Energy engineering team.

body.text: Converter Controlled Series Capacitors (CCSC PLUS) provide dynamic series compensation and advanced power flow control for high-voltage AC transmission grids. CCSC PLUS is part of Siemens Energy's Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) portfolio. It combines proven series capacitor technology with a converter branch – drawn from Siemens Energy's SVC PLUS® and HVDC expertise – to deliver dynamic power flow control directly in series with the transmission line, with no high-voltage transformer required. The platform is designed for transmission corridors operating at up to 400 kV and line current ratings up to 4,000 A.
Why transmission grids need dynamic power flow control

Three forces are converging on transmission networks at the same time: demand is rising faster than new lines can be built, generation is moving further from load, and power flows are becoming harder to predict. The result is congestion on some circuits while parallel paths run below their thermal limit.

Growing demand is straining existing infrastructure. Transmission system operators (TSOs) are facing a sharp increase in electricity demand, driven by additional loads from data centers, the electrification of industrial processes, and EV charging. Much of this demand lands on infrastructure that was planned for a different load profile.

The construction of new power lines, or the refurbishment of existing ones, is very costly and time-consuming. Therefore, improving the utilization of existing infrastructure can help mitigate investment costs. Permitting, land rights and construction span years rather than months, so TSOs increasingly need to release capacity from the corridors they already own before committing to new build.
Uncontrolled power flows create congestion and cost
Congestion is no longer an occasional peak-hour event – it is a structural condition of networks carrying large volumes of variable generation:

items: As more decentralized and renewable generation enters the grid, power flows become less predictable and harder to manage
Thermal overloads on individual lines coexist with underutilized parallel paths – a structural inefficiency of conventional devices cannot be solved.
Redispatch interventions are costly and becoming more frequent; TSOs need tools that manage congestion automatically and in real time.

body.text: The limits of conventional series compensation

Fixed Series Capacitors (FSC) and Phase Shifting Transformers (PST) remain key assets in modern grid infrastructure, but neither delivers fast dynamic series compensation: FSC impedance is set at commissioning and cannot respond to changing conditions, and a PST responds in seconds to minutes.
Thyristor Controlled Series Compensation (TCSC) adds controllability, but injects harmonic content that requires filtering and offers only a limited inductive range.

A new class of grid enhancing technology is needed: one that combines the reliability of series capacitors with fast, converter-based control, and that stays cost-effective at the line ratings where modular series compensators become impractical.
What is CCSC PLUS?

CCSC PLUS is Siemens Energy's platform-based solution for dynamic series compensation in AC transmission grids. It builds on the proven foundation of Fixed Series Capacitor (FSC) technology – adding a converter branch in parallel with the capacitor bank to enable real-time, bidirectional impedance control, in both the capacitive and the inductive direction.

Side view of the CCSC PLUS substation connection. The CCSC PLUS is installed in series with the transmission line; the containerized converter branch (VSC) is installed in parallel with the capacitor bank on the same platform

CCSC PLUS is the successor to the Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) concept. Where a UPFC required a high-voltage shunt transformer and a back-to-back converter arrangement, CCSC PLUS is installed directly in series with the line. Removing the transformer removes the single largest cost and footprint driver, while delivering comparable dynamic control capability.

Because no high-voltage transformer is required, CCSC PLUS offers a shorter lead time, a competitive installed cost and a smaller substation footprint than transformer-coupled alternatives – while providing full dynamic control capability.
Key positioning points:

items: Part of Siemens Energy's FACTS portfolio, alongside SVC PLUS® (STATCOM), SVC PLUS® FS (E-STATCOM), FSC, and Synchronous Condensers.
Platform-based: benefits from containerized SVC PLUS® (Prefab) converter technology.
Designed for line voltages up to 400 kV and line current ratings up to 4000 A (higher voltage available on request).

body.text: How CCSC PLUS works

CCSC PLUS combines two well-established Siemens Energy building blocks on a single line-voltage platform: a series capacitor bank and a containerized voltage source converter. The sections below cover the system architecture, the two control modes, and the additional grid-support functions the converter branch enables.
System architecture: proven components, new combination
CCSC PLUS has two main elements installed on a single platform:

items: Fixed capacitor branch: installed directly in series with the transmission line. Provides capacitive compensation via fixed impedance, increasing the power flow capability of the line.

Converter branch (VSC): installed in parallel with the capacitor bank on the same platform. A containerized Voltage Source Converter (VSC) based on Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) technology controls the voltage across the capacitor, dynamically adjusting the effective impedance seen by the line.

body.text: No high-voltage transformer is required. The platform design draws directly on Siemens Energy's FSC and containerized SVC PLUS® experience, both of which are in service in transmission networks worldwide.
Control modes
The converter branch enables two primary control modes:

items: Impedance control mode: the system maintains a constant impedance setpoint regardless of changes in line current. This redistributes power flow between parallel transmission paths.
Line current control mode: the system adjusts impedance compensation continuously to maintain a target line current setpoint, enabling precise power flow management.

body.text: Additional grid-support functions
Beyond steady-state power flow control, CCSC PLUS provides:

items: Power Oscillation Damping (POD): an additional control loop acts against inter-area power oscillations, improving dynamic stability across the transmission corridor.

Sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) mitigation: dynamic impedance control counteracts SSR and SSTI (sub-synchronous torsional interaction), which can damage generator shafts, as well as SSCI (sub-synchronous control interaction) between series compensation and inverter-based resources such as wind and solar plants.

Emergency Dispatch: in N-1 fault scenarios (loss of a parallel line), the system can be commanded to maximize power flow on the remaining line, supporting grid resilience and N-1 security requirements.
Line overload management: impedance adjustment redistributes flow away from thermally constrained circuits in real time, without operator intervention.

body.text: Use cases for CCSC PLUS

CCSC PLUS is applied wherever a transmission corridor is limited by how power distributes itself rather than by the physical rating of the conductors. The four scenarios below are the most common starting points for a system study.
Typical CCSC PLUS use cases, including congestion management on parallel corridors, renewable integration, grid stabilization, and deferring grid reinforcement.
Use case: Congestion management on parallel transmission corridors

Where two or more lines run in parallel, power flow naturally concentrates on the lower-impedance path – leaving the higher-impedance path underutilized. CCSC PLUS redistributes flow dynamically between parallel circuits, eliminating overloads without new infrastructure. This directly reduces redispatch frequency and cost.
Use case: Integrating renewables into constrained grids

Large offshore wind farms and solar hubs often connect into grid corridors with limited dynamic control capability. CCSC PLUS enables higher renewable penetration by redirecting power flows away from bottlenecks in real time, improving hosting capacity without line upgrades.
Use case: Grid stabilization and contingency response

items: POD (Power oscillation damping): CCSC PLUS damps inter-area oscillations that can destabilize interconnected grids – a function critical as synchronous generation declines and grid inertia falls.

SSR/SSTI (Sub-Synchronous Resonance / Sub-Synchronous Torsional Interaction) mitigation: Particularly relevant for grids with long radial lines and thermal generation, and for corridors with high shares of inverter-based generation, where sub-synchronous interactions pose a risk to generator shafts and to converter controls.
Emergency dispatch after N-1 faults: Following the loss of a parallel line, CCSC PLUS can immediately maximize power transfer on the remaining circuit, maintaining supply security.

body.text: Use case: Deferring costly grid reinforcement

By extracting more capacity from existing lines, CCSC PLUS enables TSOs to defer or avoid capital-intensive grid reinforcement programs – delivering the economic case for grid enhancing technology investment at a fraction of the cost of new construction.
Benefits of CCSC PLUS for grid operators

The business case for CCSC PLUS differs by audience. Grid operations teams value the speed of response, planning teams value the deferred capital expenditure, and engineering teams value the smaller civil scope. The groups below summarise each.
For Transmission System Operators (TSOs)

items: Maximize existing grid capacity without new line construction
Reduce redispatch costs through automated, millisecond-speed power flow redistribution
Improve N-1 security with emergency dispatch capability built into the control system
Mitigate grid instabilities – POD and SSR mitigation in a single platform solution
Defer capital expenditure – a fraction of the cost of new transmission infrastructure

body.text: For grid development and engineering teams

items: No HV transformer required – smaller substation footprint, simpler civil works
Platform-based design – factory-tested, site-assembled, reduced commissioning time
Proven technology building blocks – VSC and MMC technology proven in Siemens Energy's SVC PLUS® and HVDC projects worldwide
Freely programmable control – MMC technology allows control modes and setpoints to be updated as grid conditions and grid codes evolve, without hardware modification

body.text: For energy transition objectives

items: Enables higher penetration of renewable generation by removing transmission bottlenecks
Supports grid decarbonization by deferring fossil-fueled redispatch
Contributes to grid code N-1 compliance without new infrastructure

items.title: Gas-insulated switchgear and busduct
items.description: Siemens Energy offers SF6-free gas-insulated switchgear with clean air insulation and digital tech for efficient, eco-friendly, and reliable power transmission.

faqs.q: What is gas insulated switchgear (GIS)?
faqs.a: Gas-insulated Switchgear (GIS) integrate functions like switching, disconnecting, earthing, measurement and surge protection in a very compact and highly compatible way.

faqs.q: How does gas insulated switchgear (GIS) work?
faqs.a: HV switchgear are stations of a transmission system (grid) where voltage is transformed from high to low or the reverse using transformers. In a GIS substation the switching products are installed in metal-enclosed gas compartments.

faqs.q: What is gas insulated switchgear (GIS) used for?
faqs.a: GIS transform voltages from high to low or the reverse in a grid. Electric power may flow through several substations between generating plant and consumer, and may be changed in voltage in several steps.

faqs.q: What is SF6 gas insulated switchgear (GIS)?
faqs.a: SF6 (Sulphur Hexafluoride) is the most commonly used insulation gas in GIS over the last decades, which is the most climate hostile greenhouse gas in the world.

faqs.q: What is the alternative to SF6 gas in switchgear?
faqs.a: To reduce the CO2 footprint in switchgear there are being new technologies developed using alternative gases, such as clean air, CO2, Fluoronitrile-mix, etc.

faqs.q: What are the main components of GIS?
faqs.a: Each circuit-breaker bay includes the full range of disconnecting and earthing switches, instrument transformers, control and protection equipment, and interlocking and monitoring facilities.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of Gas-Insulated Switchgear?
faqs.a: Minimum space requirements compared to AIS substation; metal compartments ensure full protection against contact with live parts and protection against pollution

faqs.q: Are there environmental and regulatory considerations for GIS?
faqs.a: All regulations related to SF6 or other F-gases

faqs.q: What is the difference between GIS and GIB?
faqs.a: GIS = gas-insulated switchgear; GIB = gas-insulated busduct containing one or more busbars (cable connection)

faqs.q: What is the difference between GIS and AIS?
faqs.a: GIS = gas-insualted switchgear; AIS = air-insulated switchgear; same function but different types of installation

body.text: With the energy sector having a greater carbon impact than every other industry combined, the urgent need for decarbonization to combat climate change cannot be overstated. Renewable energy sources are only part of the solution; at Siemens Energy we understand how essential it is to achieve Zero Global Warming Potential (GWP) in the transmission of power as well as in its generation.

Most switchgear still uses SF6 for insulation – a gas 24,300 times more climate-hostile than CO2 and one which stays in the atmosphere for up to 1,000 years. Even the new F-gas alternatives are still harmful to the environment when released. That's not sustainable, as recognized by the new EU-F-gas regulation. And it's why we've developed our Zero-harm Blue portfolio, including gas-insulated switchgear and gas-insulated busduct.
The new net-zero switchgear

Get answers: FAQs on insulated switchgears (GIS)
What is gas insulated switchgear (GIS)?
Gas-insulated Switchgear (GIS) integrate functions like switching, disconnecting, earthing, measurement and surge protection in a very compact and highly compatible way.
How does gas insulated switchgear (GIS) work?

HV switchgear are stations of a transmission system (grid) where voltage is transformed from high to low or the reverse using transformers. In a GIS substation the switching products are installed in metal-enclosed gas compartments.
What is gas insulated switchgear (GIS) used for?

GIS transform voltages from high to low or the reverse in a grid. Electric power may flow through several substations between generating plant and consumer, and may be changed in voltage in several steps.
What is SF6 gas insulated switchgear (GIS)?
SF6 (Sulphur Hexafluoride) is the most commonly used insulation gas in GIS over the last decades, which is the most climate hostile greenhouse gas in the world.
What is the alternative to SF6 gas in switchgear?
To reduce the CO2 footprint in switchgear there are being new technologies developed using alternative gases, such as clean air, CO2, Fluoronitrile-mix, etc.
What are the main components of GIS?
Each circuit-breaker bay includes the full range of disconnecting and earthing switches,
instrument transformers, control and protection equipment, and interlocking and monitoring facilities.
What are the advantages of Gas-Insulated Switchgear?
Minimum space requirements compared to AIS substation; metal compartments ensure full protection against contact with live parts and protection against pollution
Are there environmental and regulatory considerations for GIS?
All regulations related to SF6 or other F-gases
What is the difference between GIS and GIB?
GIS = gas-insulated switchgear; GIB = gas-insulated busduct containing one or more busbars (cable connection)
What is the difference between GIS and AIS?
GIS = gas-insualted switchgear; AIS = air-insulated switchgear; same function but different types of installation

faqs.q: What is a gas turbine and how does it work?
faqs.a: A gas turbine is an internal combustion engine that converts fuels like natural gas or hydrogen into mechanical energy. It compresses air, mixes it with fuel, and ignites the mixture in a continuous process. The resulting high-pressure gases spin turbine blades to generate power, used in power plants, industry, aircraft, and ships.

faqs.q: What are gas turbines used for?
faqs.a: Gas turbines are used in various applications, including: • Power generation: Producing electricity in power plants • Industrial use (e.g., oil and gas): Driving compressors, pumps, and generators • Aviation: Powering jet engines in aircraft • Marine propulsion: Driving ships and submarines

faqs.q: Who makes gas turbines?
faqs.a: • Siemens Energy • GE Vernova • Mitsubishi Power • Rolls-Royce • Ansaldo Energia • Solar Turbines (a Caterpillar company) • Kawasaki Heavy Industries • Capstone Green Energy • MAN Energy Solutions • OPRA Turbines These companies are leaders in the industry, providing advanced and efficient gas turbines for various applications.

faqs.q: How efficient are gas turbines?
faqs.a: Gas turbines are highly efficient, achieving thermal efficiencies of 30–40% in simple-cycle configurations. In combined-cycle systems, where waste heat is reused, efficiency can exceed 60%. Performance depends on design, size, and operating conditions. Due to their high efficiency, flexibility, and low maintenance requirements, gas turbines are a reliable choice for power generation and industrial applications.

faqs.q: Where are gas turbines most commonly used in the process industries?
faqs.a: Gas turbines are widely used in process industries for: • Driving compressors: Essential for various industrial processes • Power generation: Providing electricity for on-site needs • Pump drives: Common in the oil and gas industry These applications enhance operational efficiency, reliability, and energy performance in industrial operations.

faqs.q: What are the biggest problems with gas turbines?
faqs.a: Gas turbines face several challenges. High temperatures can cause thermal stress, material fatigue, and failure. Vibrations can damage rotors and bearings. Fouling – the buildup of dirt and particles – reduces efficiency. Poor lubrication can lead to wear and overheating.To ensure safe, efficient operation, these issues require high-quality materials, regular maintenance, and monitoring.

faqs.q: What are aeroderivative gas turbines?
faqs.a: Aeroderivative gas turbines are lighter, more flexible versions of gas turbines originally designed for aircraft engines. They are adapted for use in power generation and industrial applications.

faqs.q: What are the main applications of Siemens Energy's gas turbines?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy's gas turbines are used in various applications, including: • Power generation: For utilities, independent power producers, and industrial users • Oil and gas industry: Powering upstream, midstream, and downstream operations • Mechanical drive applications: Driving compressors and pumps in industrial processes These applications demonstrate the versatility and reliability of Siemens Energy's gas turbines.

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy's gas turbines compare to those of other gas turbines manufacturers?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy’s gas turbines are known for their high efficiency, reliability, and fuel flexibility, including hydrogen readiness. Their broad portfolio supports diverse applications, from power generation to industrial use. How the fast-ramping 9000HL gas turbine supports your path to net-zero

There is not just one solution which will produce enough power and meet net zero emissions targets. A mix of new technologies, including high output and fuel-flexible options like the SGT-9000HL, are paving the way to sustainable energy. Whether you're switching from coal to gas, to higher efficiency solutions, or to low- and no-carbon fuels, we're with you on this journey. Integrating with renewables and carbon capture storage technologies are also ways the SGT-9000HL can help you drive the energy transition.
TÜV SÜD Certification for power plants with SGT-9000HL gas turbines

In October 2023, we have received the TÜV SÜD certificate for the hydrogen readiness concept covering combined cycle plants, simple cycle plants and combined heat and power plants equipped with the SGT-9000HL. With this certificate, TÜV SÜD validates the readiness concept for main systems and components with exception of the gas turbine package for hydrogen readiness up to 100% hydrogen. The gas turbine package itself is rated as H2 ready for up to 50%Vol, based on current rig test results.

This is an important milestone in the 9000HL's hydrogen journey as TÜV SÜD is an internationally recognized certifier, and this certificate is evidence that we meet the requirements to offer hydrogen-ready power plants in line with regulatory requirements, customer expectations and transformation roadmaps. We are aiming to have all gas turbines capable of burning 100% hydrogen by 2030, to help our customers meet their demands of the energy transition.

body.text: The Siemens Energy SGT-300 gas turbine is a reliable and proven solution for power generation and combined heat and power applications. With a single-shaft configuration providing an electrical power output of 8.0 MW, and a twin-shaft version delivering either 8.4 MW or 9.1 MW, the SGT-300 offers versatile power generation capabilities.

Its compact design, on-site maintainability, and inherent reliability, combined with its ability to operate with a wide range of gaseous and liquid fuels and to burn up to 30 vol% of hydrogen (H2), make it an efficient and flexible gas turbine for various applications. To date, over 200 units have been sold, contributing to a combined fleet experience exceeding of over 10 million equivalent operating hours, which demontsrates a class-leading reliability rate of 99.5%.
Key benefits of the SGT-300 gas turbine technology
The SGT-300 offers low maintenance requirements and reduced emissions. It is available in a single-shaft configuration for power generation and a twin-shaft version for mechanical drive applications.
Excellent steam-raising capability and efficiency

In cogeneration configuration, with its excellent efficiency and high steam-raising capability, the SGT-300 forms the core of reliable, efficient and powerful combined heat and power plants. For industrial cogeneration, the high steam-raising capability of more than 18 tonnes per hour contributes towards achieving overall plant efficiencies of 80% or higher.
Dry Low Emissions (DLE)

For compliance with stringent environmental legislation, the SGT-300 gas turbine is equipped with a Dry Low Emissions (DLE) combustion system, providing low NOₓ emission levels with liquid and gaseous fuels. Emissions on gas fuel, corrected to 15% O₂ dry: NOₓ: < 10 ppmvd CO: < 10 ppmvd
Fuel flexibility matters

The SGT-300 operates on a wide range of gases, covering an extensive Wobbe fuel range. The engine, equipped with DLE burners, is capable to burn up to 30 vol% of hydrogen (H2). It also supports numerous liquid fuels and features dual-fuel operation. Automatic switching between primary and secondary fuels is possible at any load.
Rapid core engine exchange minimizes downtime
The SGT-300 can be maintained on-site. Furthermore, the option of rapid core turbine exchange will minimize the downtime of the gas turbine.

The SGT-300 is available for a wide variety of power generation applications, including:

body.text: Robust, flexible and high performing industrial gas turbine
The single-shaft SGT-300 consists of a single twin-bearing rotor with heavy-duty casing. Quick core engine exchange is possible, which significantly cuts your maintenance-related downtime.

The SGT-300 twin-shaft has a 2-stage gas generator turbine and a 2-stage power turbine. The core turbine is designed for high reliability with powerful performance and quick load following. Its modular design approach allows turbine module exchanges to be carried out on-site as an alternative to a gas generator or power turbine service exchange.
Both versions of the SGT-300 gas turbine are equipped with a Dry Low Emissions (DLE) combustion system, providing low NOₓ emission levels with liquid and gaseous fuels and dual-fuel capability.
SGT-300 core engine: single-shaft version
SGT-300 core engine: twin-shaft version
SGT-300 packages

The compact SGT-300 gas turbine packages for power generation and mechanical drive applications comprise factory-tested modules, and offer a high power-to-weight ratio. The packages incorporate gas turbine, gearbox (where applicable), drive unit and all factory-tested fluid modules, all of which are mounted on an underbase. This makes them easy to transport, install and maintain on-site.
The shop-tested and certified fluid system modules are the same for design across the SGT-100 to SGT-400 range and come fully wired into the package control systems:

items: Auto drains module
Gas fuel module

body.text: The health and safety of the operation and maintenance staff are paramount. This is why our SGT-300 packages are designed with a special emphasis on, e.g., walkways and handrails, noise suppression, access doorways, and safety interlocks.
Power generation package
The SGT-300 package for power generation is suitable for simple cycle, combined cycle and cogeneration.

High steam-raising capability, compact arrangement, on-site maintainability, and an inherent reliability make it an ideal choice for many applications, including applications in the demanding oil and gas industry.
Mechanical drive package

The mechanical drive package is very compact, with a small footprint and a high power-to-weight ratio. The twin-shaft configuration offers excellent speed and load turndown characteristics to allow maximum flexibility of operation.
Cogeneration plants

With its excellent efficiency and steam-raising capability of more than 18 tonnes per hour, the SGT-300 forms the core of reliable, efficient and powerful combined heat and power plants (CHP). This contributes towards achieving overall plant efficiencies of 80% or higher.
When compared with conventional energy supplies, a cogeneration plant based on the SGT-300 will provide electrical power, heating and/or cooling with the benefit of:

items: Significant reductions in energy costs
Security of energy supplies
Reductions in total emissions of carbon dioxide
Improved flexibility

body.text: Powering a cogeneration plant

The SGT-300-based CHP plant was required to help provide for the energy needs of 13,000 people living and studying at an university campus, in an efficient and cost-effective manner. The plant runs predominantly at part load, with various load adjustments, and provides trigeneration: heating, cooling, and electrical power.
Comprehensive portfolio of customer service activities

The comprehensive portfolio of services provides low life cycle cost and optimum performance throughout the turbine's life cycle: Long Term Programs (LTP), overhaul service, field service, spare parts, service exchange, remote diagnostic service, and modernization and upgrades.
Siemens Energy specialists offer on-site support all over the world.

body.text: Rapid core exchange option for minimized downtimes
The core engine maintenance can be performed on-site or off-site.
Axial blade attachment
The first stage rotor blades can be axially removed for quick and easy on-site exchange, maximizing availability.
Easy combustor maintenance
For minimized downtimes and maximized availability, the combustion chambers, flame tubes and ignitors are easily accessible for inspection.
Borescope holes
Multiple borescope ports are used to inspect the engine. They allow visual inspection of the interior of the engine without disassembly. The borescope inspections prevent unnecessary maintenance.
Coverage of a wide Wobbe range

The single-shaft SGT-300 operates on a wide range of gases, including gas fuels outside of standard pipeline quality. It covers a Wobbe fuel range from approximately 50 MJ/m³ down to 17.5 MJ/m³, which include, e.g., gas fuels available in LNG liquefaction plants, wellhead gas and minimally processed, weak wellhead gas, biogas from ethanol, industry waste, or landfill gas. The engine, equipped with DLE burners, is capable to burn up to 30 vol% of hydrogen (H2).
The SGT-300 is also able to burn a large number of liquid fuels and offers dual-fuel capability, with automatic changeover from primary to secondary fuel at any load.
Robust combustion with high fuel flexibility
For high fuel flexibility, the SGT-300 uses a robust can annular combustion system with six reverse-flow tubular chambers, and a high energy igniter in each combustor.
Clean, flexible operation
The SGT-300 DLE combustor burns a great variety of gaseous and liquid fuels and offers clean combustion with low emissions.
Low emissions despite rugged industrial design
The proven and reliable Dry Low Emissions (DLE) combustor offers clean combustion with low emissions over a wide operating range.

The SGT-300 uses six reverse-flow tubular combustion chambers positioned around a high-pressure casing. Each burner contains its own ignition source and is capable of gas-only, liquid-only or dual-fuel operation. Fuel is controlled by both a pilot and a main burner, with the control system providing for smooth changeover across the power range.
With the DLE combustion system, emission compliance at lower operating loads down to 50% or lower is possible.

items: NOₓ emissions: ≤ 15 ppmvd (corrected to 15% O₂ dry)

body.text: Clean combustion for stringent emission compliance
The SGT-300 DLE combustion system provides NOₓ and CO emission compliance with the most stringent environmental legislations.
NOₓ limitation with lean premix of air and fuel

NOₓ emission increases exponentially with temperature. Therefore, it is critical to ensure that air and fuel are optimally mixed. The Siemens DLE combustion system achieves low emissions over a wide load range by a lean air/fuel premix flame with multiple fuel-injection points.

faqs.q: What is the power range of the Siemens Energy SGT-400 gas turbine?

faqs.q: Can the SGT-400 turbine burn different fuel types, including hydrogen?

faqs.q: What advantages does the SGT-400 offer for emissions compliance?

body.text: The Siemens Energy SGT-400 is a durable twin-shaft gas turbine suitable for power generation and mechanical drive applications in the 13 – 15 MW power band, suitable for all climates, onshore and offshore. It boasts operational and fuel flexibility, low emissions, and overall efficiency, with enhancements to rotors and blades as well as a 33% increase in time between overhauls. To date, more than 450 units have been sold, collectively achieving over 11.7 million hours of operation, which demontsrates a class-leading reliability rate of 99%.

With its can-annular design and single-stage combustion system, it efficiently burns a wide variety of fuel types at any load, consistently meeting strict emissions standards—even at low loads—while providing seamless, true dual-fuel operation. Additionally, it is capable of burning up to 65 vol% hydrogen (H2), making it a flexible and efficient gas turbine for diverse applications.

body.text: Get answers: FAQs on SGT-400
What is SGT-400?
SGT-400 is a durable twin-shaft gas turbine suitable for power generation and mechanical drive applications in the 10 – 15 MW power band.
What is the power range of the Siemens Energy SGT-400 gas turbine?
The SGT-400 operates in the 10–15 MW power band, making it suitable for both power generation and mechanical drive applications in diverse climate and site conditions.
Can the SGT-400 turbine burn different fuel types, including hydrogen?

Yes. The SGT-400 features true dual-fuel capability and can burn a wide variety of gaseous and liquid fuels, including hydrogen blends—up to 30% H₂ with DLE burners and up to 65% H₂ with diffusion burners.
What advantages does the SGT-400 offer for emissions compliance?
The SGT-400's DLE combustion system enables compliance with the most stringent NOx and CO emissions regulations, delivering ultra-low emissions across a wide load range—even at loads down to 30%.
How does the SGT-400 ensure high operational reliability and flexibility?

It features robust design qualities including durable rotors and blades, extended service intervals, and the ability to efficiently operate across a broad load and speed range, plus seamless fuel changeover capability.
What industries and locations are best suited for the SGT-400?

The SGT-400 is ideal for offshore and onshore oil & gas production, refinery applications, LNG plants, combined heat and power (CHP), and mechanical drive uses such as direct-drive compressors and pumps.
What are the service and maintenance features of the SGT-400?

Core engine maintenance can be performed on-site or off-site, with quick access to burner modules and rotor blades for rapid exchange. Remote diagnostic and support services optimize uptime and lifecycle costs.
How does Siemens Energy support SGT-400 owners and operators?
A global team of field service technicians, 24/7 help desks, and remote monitoring ensure owners receive comprehensive lifecycle support, including long-term programs and modernization options.
What is the efficiency profile of the SGT-400 in various applications?
The turbine delivers best-in-class efficiency for simple cycle, combined cycle, and CHP uses, and offers high steam-raising capability and compact dimensions for maximum site adaptability.
Is the SGT-400 gas turbine proven in real-world installations?
Yes - over 390 units have been deployed globally, logging more than 5 million operating hours across diverse industries and geographies.
Where can I find technical documentation and request support about SGT-400?

Brochures, technical papers, and case studies are available in the product's download section. Dedicated support is available 24/7 in English, Spanish, and German for technical, operational, or marketing inquiries.

body.text: Ingenious design to the core

The SGT-800 industrial gas turbine blends a robust, simple design for reliability and easy maintenance with high efficiency and low emissions. Its continuous evolution, based on fleet experience and proven design solutions, guarantees optimal performance and a long operational lifetime for your gas turbine.
The gas turbine features a robust dual-fuel DLE system for clean combustion, without the complexity of burner of burner staging.
The single-shaft engine is composed of a 2-bearing rotor with a 15-stage compressor and a 3-stage turbine.
Classic or single-lift?
Two different package solutions are available for increased flexibility in order to meet your individual requirements. Both are available for 50 Hz and 60 Hz markets.
Standard options for hot and cold climates are available for operation at extreme ambient temperatures.
SGT-800 classic package

items: The classic package comprises preassembled modules with the gas turbine and gearbox on a single base frame.
Mechanical auxiliary systems are mounted on a separate skid within the enclosure.
A modular package allows for easy transportation and straightforward on-site installation.
On-site maintenance, inspections, and overhauls are conveniently performed within the enclosure, providing added ease and efficiency.

body.text: SGT-800 single-lift package

items: The single-lift package is a preassembled unit available in two configurations: as a single-lift driver unit(i.e. gas turbine, gearbox and mechanical auxiliary systems on a single base frame) with the generator on the foundation, or as a complete skid-mounted train for 3-point mount installations, e.g. for power barges (SGT-800 SeaFloat).
It offers a small footprint and the potential for a 48-hour core engine exchange.
The single-lift operation of the driver unit or complete train results in a short installation and commissioning time on site.
A special US-adapted option is available for specific requirements.

Flexibility and efficiency are key for your power plant solutions. The excellent efficiency and steam-raising capability of the SGT-800 gas turbine make it outstanding in cogeneration – also called combined heat and power (CHP) – and combined cycle installations.

Siemens Energy offers a wide variety of power plant configurations, based on one or more SGT-800 gas turbines. The standard plant configurations offer a high degree of flexibility. This allows for the optimization of plants to suit specific requirements, such as island-mode operation or multiple power blocks.

body.text: Designed for flexible operation

Our SGT-800-based power plants offer the flexibility required in today's volatile energy landscape: quick starts, fast load following and low emissions on low plant part-load operation. Designed for frequent starts and stops, they are the perfect match to back up renewable power sources in the grid.
Excellent combined cycle and combined heat and power efficiency

One or multiple SGT-800 gas turbines provide the core of a powerful combined cycle plant: In a 2x1 combined cycle configuration, the power output is up to 180 MW(e) at a net plant efficiency of more than 60%. In a combined heat and power (CHP) cycle, the efficiency is more than 92% with supplementary firing.
Flexible maintenance – high availability
The comprehensive service portfolio ensures low life cycle costs and optimal performance throughout the turbine's life cycle, including:

items: Long Term Programs (LTP)
Overhaul service

Modernization and upgrades The SGT-800 offers high operational availability, providing up to 60,000 equivalent operating hours (EOHs) between major overhauls, and offering flexible, standardised maintenance concepts based on either time or cycles. Package solutions offer on-site maintenance or modular overhaul, while the single-lift package provides off-site maintenance and the option of a 48-hour core engine exchange. Designed for easy maintenance, the compact and modular setup of the SGT-800 allows for convenient access. The vertically split compressor casing enables straightforward on-site component replacement, and the burners can be swiftly removed for maintenance inspections.

body.text: Fuel flexibility matters

The SGT-800 offers gas-only, liquid-only (diesel No. 2) or dual-fuel (gas/liquid) options, with on-load fuel-changeover capability. Its excellent fuel flexibility allows for a high content of inert gases, hydrogen and heavy hydrocarbons in the gas fuel composition with no impact on maintenance. The engine, which is equipped with DLE burners, can burn up to 75 vol% hydrogen (H₂).
The low gas supply pressure requirement (27–31 bar(a)/390–450 psi(a)) reduces the need for a gas compressor on site.
Best-in-class NOₓ and CO emission levels

All SGT-800 units are equipped with a robust dual-fuel Dry Low Emission (DLE) combustion system to minimize NOₓ and CO emissions. The combustor and burner designs offer world-class emission performance over a wide load range with single-digit CO emission levels and capable of down to 9 ppm NOx emissions. With this gas turbine you will comply with both global and regional regulations.
H2-Readiness - TÜV SÜD certificate

TÜV SÜD has developed a guideline for defining the “H2-Readiness” of power plants and is offering an independent certification to original equipment manufacturers and engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) companies. The certification increases investment security for utilities. Siemens Energy is the first company worldwide to receive this certification for its “H2-Ready” power plant concept for the SGT-800. The guideline for obtaining certification was developed in collaboration with subject matter experts from Siemens Energy.

body.text: Get answers: FAQs on SGT-800
What is SGT-800?

The SGT-800 is a powerful and flexible industrial gas turbine from Siemens Energy with a power output of up to 62 MW, designed for a wide range of applications like industrial power generation, oil and gas operations, and combined cycle plants.
What are the main applications of the SGT-800 gas turbine?

The SGT-800 is ideal for both industrial power generation and oil and gas applications. It supports combined cycle, cogeneration (CHP), and grid support functions—whether for base, intermediate, or peaking loads.
How efficient is the SGT-800 in combined cycle and CHP plant configurations?
In a 2x1 combined cycle setup, the SGT-800 achieves a net plant efficiency of over 60%. In CHP (cogeneration) cycles with supplementary firing, efficiencies greater than 92% are attainable.
What makes the SGT-800 environmentally friendly?

It features world-class low emission levels, with single-digit CO emissions and NOx as low as 9 ppm. Low emissions are possible with both gas and liquid fuels, without water injection, and the system meets stringent global and regional regulations.
How reliable is the SGT-800 gas turbine fleet?
The average fleet reliability of core engine and auxiliary systems is 99.1% (2024), attributed to its simple, robust technical solutions and long-proven record worldwide.
What fuels can the SGT-800 use?

The SGT-800 offers maximum flexibility, running on natural gas, Diesel No.2, or dual fuel (with on-load fuel changeover). It's also capable of burning up to 75% hydrogen by volume and supports high biofuel content.
What maintenance options are available for the SGT-800?
A modular, compact design ensures easy maintainability, with long intervals between overhauls and robust service concepts—including 48-hour core engine exchange to maximize uptime.
Is the SGT-800 “H2-Ready”?

Yes, Siemens Energy is the first manufacturer to receive TÜV SÜD's independent “H2-Ready” certification for a power plant concept based on the SGT-800, ensuring hydrogen integration and investment security for the future.
How does the SGT-800 perform in extreme climates?
There are standard options for both hot and cold environments, ensuring reliable performance and efficiency even in harsh ambient conditions.
What successful projects feature the SGT-800?

Examples include the Leipzig CHP plant in Germany (2 x SGT-800 with SIESTART battery storage) and the SeaFloat barge-mounted plant for Seaboard Corporation, which combines SGT-800 turbines, an SST600 steam turbine, and battery storage.
What support and services are offered for SGT-800 operators?
Siemens Energy provides a comprehensive, global service portfolio, including preventive maintenance, fast core swaps, and expert support, with teams available 24/7 in English, Spanish, and German.

faqs.q: Fits all climates and environmental conditions
faqs.a: The SGT-A05 is proven to operate in various challenging conditions and locations around the world, including the North Sea, West Africa, Siberia, Brazil, Alaska, Southeast Asia and the desert regions of the Middle East. The SGT-A05 engine has been shock-qualified to Mil-S-901C, which makes it particularly suitable for areas with frequent or severe seismic activity.

faqs.q: Excellent fuel flexibility
faqs.a: The SGT-A05 is known for its high fuel flexibility, which will accommodate a wide variety of possible application scenarios and requirements. Fuels include, but are not limited to natural gas, liquid fuel (or both) and mid to low BTU gas fuels. Fuel system options include dual fuel, steam and water injection. Dry Low Emissions (DLE) technology is also available.

faqs.q: Fast start-up
