body.text: A possible use case: the combined production of hydrogen and heat

Whenever enough renewable energy is available, it can be used to produce hydrogen. The hydrogen can be easily stored for times when there is a shortage of renewable energy. At the same time, the heat pump uses the waste heat from the electrolyzer to produce heat at temperatures suitable for district heating. In times of renewable energy surplus, thermal power plants can be shut down because they are not needed for electricity or heat production. When heat production is higher than heat demand, the excess heat from the heat pump can be stored in thermal storage facilities.

The heat from the thermal storage covers periods of high heat demand but low electricity demand. The integration of renewable energy in heat production helps to decarbonize district heating. The integrated electrolyzer and heat pump solution lowers the levelized cost of energy for both hydrogen production and heat production for district heating by minimizing energy losses.

items.title: Medium-voltage direct current (MVDC PLUS®)
items.description: Discover how MVDC PLUS® can transform your grid infrastructure with flexible, efficient, and sustainable medium-voltage DC transmission technology.

faqs.q: What is medium voltage?
faqs.a: Medium voltage refers to the range of voltages typically between 1 kV and 35 kV used in electrical power systems for distribution and sub-transmission. It is crucial for efficiently transmitting electricity over moderate distances and connecting regional grids.

faqs.q: What is MVDC PLUS® and what makes it different from traditional AC transmission systems?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® is Siemens Energy advanced medium-voltage direct current technology that offers enhanced grid transmission capabilities. Unlike traditional AC systems, MVDC PLUS® provides improved efficiency, flexibility, and reliability by combining the benefits of DC transmission with the adaptability of AC networks.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® improve grid stability?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® enhances grid stability by managing complex power flows and reducing transmission losses. Its ability to control voltage and power quality ensures consistent and reliable energy delivery, even in challenging conditions.

faqs.q: Can MVDC PLUS® be integrated with renewable energy sources?
faqs.a: Yes, MVDC PLUS® is designed to seamlessly integrate with renewable energy sources, facilitating efficient power transmission and supporting the transition to sustainable energy systems.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® handle power quality issues?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® addresses power quality issues by providing precise voltage control and harmonic filtering, ensuring stable and high-quality power delivery across the grid.

faqs.q: What new features or technologies could be added to the MVDC PLUS® system?
faqs.a: Future enhancements to MVDC PLUS® may include advanced grid management features, improved scalability, and integration with emerging technologies to further optimize grid performance and adaptability.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® improve environmental compatibility?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® improves environmental compatibility by reducing transmission losses and enabling the efficient integration of renewable energy sources, contributing to lower carbon emissions and a more sustainable energy ecosystem.

faqs.q: Can MVDC PLUS® be integrated with existing AC grids?
faqs.a: Yes, MVDC PLUS® can be integrated with existing AC grids, providing a flexible solution that enhances overall grid performance and supports the modernization of energy infrastructure.

faqs.q: What are the typical applications of MVDC PLUS®?
faqs.a: Typical applications of MVDC PLUS® include regional grid interconnections, renewable energy integration, and enhancing the efficiency of medium-voltage distribution networks.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® contribute to economic efficiency?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® contributes to economic efficiency by reducing transmission losses, optimizing power flow, and minimizing the need for extensive infrastructure investments, resulting in cost savings and improved energy delivery.

faqs.q: What is the power transmission capacity of MVDC PLUS®?
faqs.a: The power transmission capacity of MVDC PLUS® varies based on system configuration and application, but it is designed to handle significant power loads efficiently, supporting medium-voltage grid demands.

faqs.q: How does MVDC PLUS® handle bidirectional power flow?
faqs.a: MVDC PLUS® efficiently manages bidirectional power flow, allowing for dynamic energy exchange between interconnected grids and supporting the integration of distributed generation sources.

body.text: The future of flexible, efficient grid transmission: unlocking the grid connector potential of medium-voltage DC for modern energy ecosystems - an economic, flexible, and powerful solution for medium-voltage transmission, designed to transform modern energy ecosystems.

As energy systems evolve with increasing distributed generation and renewable integration, regional high-voltage (HV) and medium-voltage (MV) grids face unprecedented challenges in power transmission. The omnidirectional power flows characteristic of modern energy ecosystems demand innovative solutions to ensure stability and efficiency.

Siemens Energy medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) technology, specifically MVDC PLUS®, offers a cutting-edge solution to these challenges. By combining the reliability and efficiency of DC transmission with the flexibility of AC networks, MVDC PLUS® empowers grid operators to manage complex power flows and meet both current and future energy demands. This technology unlocks the potential of MVDC for modern energy ecosystems, providing a powerful tool for enhancing power transmission capabilities and supporting sustainable energy development.
MVDC PLUS®: A comprehensive solution

The increasingly complex energy landscape presents numerous challenges to regional transmission and distribution grids. Siemens Energy's MVDC PLUS® emerges as the innovative universal solution, adept at addressing these issues with ease and efficiency:

items: High-quality power output
Bidirectional power flow
Reactive power compensation and load flow control
STATCOM operation capabilities

body.text: Several factors contribute to the increasing interest in medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) systems, as they offer innovative solutions to modern power transmission challenges:
Increased transmission distances
As markets become more liberalized, the need for longer transmission distances grows, requiring efficient solutions to maintain power quality and grid stability.
Distributed generation
The rise of distributed power generation units introduces power quality and grid stability issues, necessitating advanced technologies to manage these complexities.
Grid expansion and upgrades
To accommodate the volatile demand for flexible electricity supply, grid infrastructure must be expanded, upgraded, and reconnected, ensuring reliable energy delivery.
Demand for transmission autonomy
Distribution system operators (DSOs) require greater transmission autonomy to address the expanded range of tasks in today's energy landscape.
Find out how MVDC PLUS® can help to tackle your grid challenges

Siemens Energy MVDC PLUS® is the solution to transmission challenges. It is the efficient, robust, reliable, and compact solution designed to tackle the challenges faced by regional high-voltage transmission networks and medium-voltage distribution grids. By integrating the advantages of DC technology into AC networks, MVDC PLUS® enhances transmission capabilities, strengthens grid infrastructure, minimizes losses, and provides reactive power compensation and load flow control. This technology empowers grid operators to meet the demands of modern energy systems, supporting sustainable and flexible electricity supply.
MVDC PLUS® overview
Key features and benefits of MVDC technology

MVDC PLUS® is engineered with Siemens Energy proven multilevel voltage-sourced converter technology, available in three standardized type ratings. This ensures universal applicability and delivers numerous benefits across diverse power transmission applications.
Improved connectivity
MVDC PLUS® excels in grid coupling, effectively connecting or re-connecting islanded grids with independent frequencies to larger supply structures, enhancing overall grid integration.
Increased capacity
It enables substantial and sustainable capacity improvements, helping to avert or delay costly network expansions by optimizing existing infrastructure.
Enhanced environmental compatibility

MVDC PLUS® requires minimal space and supports the use of less visually intrusive MV overhead transmission lines (OHLs), facilitating the transmission of up to 150 MW with reduced environmental impact compared to traditional AC solutions.
Greater economic efficiency

Offering an exceptional price/performance ratio, MVDC PLUS® covers a wide performance spectrum, eliminating the need for multiple individual measures and delivering cost-effective solutions for modern energy systems.
Applications of MVDC technology
MVDC technology is versatile and suitable for a wide range of applications, enhancing efficiency and reliability across various sectors:

items: Offshore wind power generation: MVDC technology facilitates efficient transmission of power from offshore wind farms to onshore grids, optimizing renewable energy integration.
Microgrids: MVDC technology enhances the performance and reliability of microgrids, enabling decentralized energy solutions and supporting local energy independence.
Transportation: It plays a crucial role in electrifying transportation systems, offering efficient power transmission for railways and electric vehicle infrastructure.
Subsea loads: MVDC technology is ideal for powering subsea equipment, ensuring reliable energy delivery in challenging underwater environments.
Marine vessels: It supports onboard power systems, providing stable and efficient energy management for marine vessels.
Data centers: It provides efficient power management for data centers, supporting high-demand operations with stable and reliable energy supply.
Oil and gas rigs: MVDC technology ensures efficient power transmission to offshore oil and gas rigs, enhancing operational reliability and safety.
Connecting small communities: It enables the connection of small, remote communities to larger power grids, improving access to reliable electricity.
Backup power: MVDC technology offers robust backup power solutions, ensuring continuity of energy supply during outages or emergencies.

body.text: Technical aspects of MVDC PLUS®

MVDC PLUS® utilizes a symmetrical monopole layout, a streamlined version of the HVDC topology, offering a smart combination of AC and DC transmission advantages. Based on our modular multilevel voltage-sourced converter (VSC) technology, MVDC PLUS® has demonstrated its efficiency and performance in numerous HVDC PLUS® and SVC PLUS® applications.
AC transmission benefits
MVDC PLUS® incorporates the simplicity, robustness, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of common AC technology, allowing for easy integration into existing transmission networks.
DC transmission advantages
It leverages the long-distance transmission capabilities, high transmission capacity, active power flow control, reactive power compensation, and STATCOM properties of HVDC PLUS® technology.

At the core of MVDC PLUS® are rugged and powerful multilevel voltage-sourced converters (VSCs), which produce an almost ideal sinusoidal waveform, ensuring consistent power quality. The converter stations facilitate bidirectional power flow and can operate as STATCOMs, enhancing grid stability and efficiency. MVDC PLUS® represents our commitment to delivering advanced solutions for modern power transmission challenges.
MVDC PLUS® in the context of the energy transition

Siemens Energy is dedicated to advancing the global energy transition by empowering grids to integrate renewable energy sources and operate with greater efficiency. MVDC PLUS® plays a pivotal role in this transformation by:
Supporting renewable integration
MVDC PLUS® offers flexible grid management solutions that facilitate the seamless integration of renewable energy, enhancing grid adaptability and performance.
Reducing grid losses
By improving transmission efficiency, MVDC PLUS® minimizes grid losses, ensuring more effective energy delivery and reducing operational costs.
Facilitating decarbonization
MVDC PLUS® contributes to the development of reliable and resilient power networks, supporting the shift towards sustainable, low-carbon energy systems.
Aligning with Siemens Energy strategies
MVDC PLUS® complements Siemens Energy broader strategies for creating sustainable energy solutions, reinforcing the commitment to a cleaner, greener future.
Get answers: FAQs on medium-voltage direct current (MVDC PLUS®)
What is medium voltage?

Medium voltage refers to the range of voltages typically between 1 kV and 35 kV used in electrical power systems for distribution and sub-transmission. It is crucial for efficiently transmitting electricity over moderate distances and connecting regional grids.
What is MVDC PLUS® and what makes it different from traditional AC transmission systems?

MVDC PLUS® is Siemens Energy advanced medium-voltage direct current technology that offers enhanced grid transmission capabilities. Unlike traditional AC systems, MVDC PLUS® provides improved efficiency, flexibility, and reliability by combining the benefits of DC transmission with the adaptability of AC networks.
How does MVDC PLUS® improve grid stability?

MVDC PLUS® enhances grid stability by managing complex power flows and reducing transmission losses. Its ability to control voltage and power quality ensures consistent and reliable energy delivery, even in challenging conditions.
Can MVDC PLUS® be integrated with renewable energy sources?
Yes, MVDC PLUS® is designed to seamlessly integrate with renewable energy sources, facilitating efficient power transmission and supporting the transition to sustainable energy systems.
How does MVDC PLUS® handle power quality issues?
MVDC PLUS® addresses power quality issues by providing precise voltage control and harmonic filtering, ensuring stable and high-quality power delivery across the grid.
What new features or technologies could be added to the MVDC PLUS® system?

Future enhancements to MVDC PLUS® may include advanced grid management features, improved scalability, and integration with emerging technologies to further optimize grid performance and adaptability.
How does MVDC PLUS® improve environmental compatibility?

MVDC PLUS® improves environmental compatibility by reducing transmission losses and enabling the efficient integration of renewable energy sources, contributing to lower carbon emissions and a more sustainable energy ecosystem.
Can MVDC PLUS® be integrated with existing AC grids?
Yes, MVDC PLUS® can be integrated with existing AC grids, providing a flexible solution that enhances overall grid performance and supports the modernization of energy infrastructure.
What are the typical applications of MVDC PLUS®?
Typical applications of MVDC PLUS® include regional grid interconnections, renewable energy integration, and enhancing the efficiency of medium-voltage distribution networks.
How does MVDC PLUS® contribute to economic efficiency?

MVDC PLUS® contributes to economic efficiency by reducing transmission losses, optimizing power flow, and minimizing the need for extensive infrastructure investments, resulting in cost savings and improved energy delivery.
What is the power transmission capacity of MVDC PLUS®?

The power transmission capacity of MVDC PLUS® varies based on system configuration and application, but it is designed to handle significant power loads efficiently, supporting medium-voltage grid demands.
How does MVDC PLUS® handle bidirectional power flow?
MVDC PLUS® efficiently manages bidirectional power flow, allowing for dynamic energy exchange between interconnected grids and supporting the integration of distributed generation sources.
Is MVDC PLUS® scalable for different grid sizes and demands?
Yes, MVDC PLUS® is scalable and can be customized to meet the specific needs of different grid sizes and demands, ensuring optimal performance and adaptability across various applications.

body.text: Integrating renewable energy sources and decarbonizing existing electricity infrastructure are key to meeting society's energy needs while fighting climate change. Yet, these contributions to more carbon-neutral energy take place in remote areas often hundreds or even thousands of kilometers away from the centers of consumption. Effective solutions are vital to connecting all distributed power generation sources to the grid to make electricity available where it is really needed.
Connections to a secure, reliable, and more decarbonized world of energy
Siemens Energy supplies a comprehensive range of reliable, efficient, and proven transmission systems as grid access solutions that meet and master these challenges.
Offshore renewables

Renewables such as wind power (on- and offshore) play an increasingly important role in the energy mix and contribute considerably to the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions. Siemens Energy supplies the entire range of products and services to turnkey solutions required for efficiently harnessing the power of offshore renewables and getting the energy to the end consumer. This includes wind turbines and complete grid access solutions in HVAC and HVDC technology as well as monitoring and control solutions and operation and maintenance services.
Offshore electrification

Worldwide lowest emissions in offshore oil and gas production with offshore electrification solutions. Increasingly also Oil & Gas companies are energizing their offshore installations by the means electrical energy. Our HVDC and HVAC solutions supply industrial offshore sites efficiently with clean and reliable power. Siemens Energy's HVDC and HVAC grid access and power supply solutions have proven their superior performance, reliability and availability in numerous projects all over the world - in the harshest climates.
Floating substations

Floating offshore wind opens the door to larger and deeper offshore areas with higher wind potential. Siemens Energy offers optimum floating substation solutions for the connection of floating offshore windfarms to the grid or floating power from shore to open the next frontier for renewables. From small modular HVDC power from shore applications, or floating HVAC substations, up to full-scale +1 GW floating HVDC solutions, Siemens Energy can offer a lean and innovative floating substation solution for the most challenging environments, based on long-term proven high-voltage technology, and optimized for minimal environmental impact. With clean air GIS solutions, ester-insulated transformers and closed cooling systems, the Siemens Energy floating OSS offers a valuable and sustainable grid connection for the future of floating windfarms.
Meeting the challenges of the renewable energy era

There are many challenges to be faced in today's energy world that is fundamentally changing at a rapid pace. Electricity must come from renewables such as wind and solar power. Power generation must be as carbon-neutral as possible. The distance between power producers and consumers is increasing because renewables resources like offshore wind farms are further away from consumer centers. Grid capacity is growing as fossil power generation is gradually shutting down.

This swiftly-advancing energy transition demands major changes to power grids, making it crucial to stabilize existing, strained grids to ensure continuously reliable operation. Guaranteeing security of power supply and consequently the security of reliable operation of such critical infrastructure is a matter of utmost priority. And while digitalization enables new technologies and solutions, it comes with the burdens of cybersecurity.
Zero-subsidy renewables

As a pioneer in offshore power transmission technologies and reliable partner for implementing high-voltage direct current (HVDC) and high-voltage alternating current (HVAC) solutions as well as flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) and a comprehensive range of related services, we support you with our in-depth, long-standing experience in the field of power transmission and distribution.

With our holistic approach to the entire electricity transmission system, our experts drive continuous development in terms of both technology and economy. Collaborating with our customers, we deliver significant savings in the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) while further improving transmission system reliability and ensuring grid code compliance. And our expertise supports the zero-subsidy initiative for offshore projects.

faqs.q: THYRIPOL®-S & THYRIPOL®-6RV90 (static excitation systems)
faqs.a: The static excitation system (SES) is a tried-and-tested solution for synchronous machines (generators, motors and synchronous condensers). SES can be used as a stand-alone system or as a compact system in combination with a start-up frequency converter. Our solution adapts perfectly to the conditions in both newly built or upgraded power plants, regardless of the space conditions, generator type, power supply or control system and regardless of whether the control system is also being replaced at the same time, as well as whether there is a hard-wired or bus connection.

faqs.q: THYRIPART®-S (compound excitation systems)
faqs.a: The compound excitation system (CES) is a tried-and-tested solution for synchronous generators of any manufacturer and can be used both as a static excitation system for generators and for excitation of rotating excitation machines. Over 300 installations in operation have demonstrated the unconditional reliability and robustness for years. Our solution adapts to the conditions in each individual power plant regardless of the available footprint, which generator is used and which power supply and control system is available.

faqs.q: DIGUREG 2 (digital voltage regulator)
faqs.a: DIGUREG is a compact voltage regulator, designed and tested in accordance with the relevant IEEE 421.5 standards and has an integrated power module. It is intended for synchronous machines with exciter sets and rotating diodes. DIGUREG is suitable for being used in steam turbine, gas turbine and hydroelectric power plants.

body.text: Aging equipments can be challenging, especially when they no longer meet operational demands. After years in operation, long-serving excitation equipment is often no longer up to the task. Components of the excitation system may have been discontinued, the frequency of outages becomes unacceptable and grid operators impose new demands on control dynamics. Issues such as shortages of spare parts, excessive outages, and increasing grid requirements can hinder reliable and efficient continuous operation, which is crucial for maintaining the availability of the power plant.

Siemens Energy offers a comprehensive modernization solution for synchronous generators through advanced excitation systems that are compatible with any make or brand. Our turnkey solutions include all necessary components and services, tailored to each power plant's specific needs, ensuring efficient installation and grid compliance, making reliability non-negotiable in today's energy landscape.
Reliable operation, stability and fast transient response for synchronous generators and synchronous motors

Excitation systems play a major role in ensuring the reliable continuous operation of synchronous generators. They have a direct impact on generator readiness, dynamic response, and the regulation of reactive power. Modern generator excitation systems are essential for meeting today's demands for performance, flexibility, and grid compliance - especially in power plants where reliablity is non-negotiable.

Our excitation systems are engineered to meet the highest demands of modern power generation - offering maximum grid stability, flexible system integration, and full compliance with international standards. Whether for new installations or retrofit projects, they combine proven technology with advanced digital control to ensure reliable performance, seamless connectivity, and long-term operational security.

The right excitation system for every application
No matter your footprint, power supply or generator output, Siemens Energy can offer the right excitation system for any application in any power plant.

items: Static excitation systems (SES) employ the most advanced technology for synchronous generators and synchronous condensers, and are compatible with generators from any manufacturer. SES are suitable for low to high performance classes, from 1 to over 1200 MVA generator output, mainly in hydroelectric, gas, steam and nuclear power plants. These systems are characterized by absolute reliability and maximum efficiency.

Compound excitation systems (CES) are excitation systems for synchronous generators and emergency diesel generators. They are suitable for lower and upper performance classes with a generator power of up to approximately 50 MVA in hydroelectric, gas, steam and nuclear plants (emergency diesel) and are characterized by maximum safety and absolute availability. CES are available as load dependent static and brushless versions.

Automatic voltage regulators for brushless excitation systems (BES) are for generators with (brushless) exciters, and use cutting-edge technology. They are suitable for all performance classes from 1 to over 1000 MVA generator output in gas, hydroelectric and steam power plants and are characterized by absolute reliability and maximum efficiency.

items.title: Grid ancillary solutions
items.description: Power stations equipped with black start capabilities and synchronous condensers supplying short circuit power ensure permanent dynamic voltage and reactive power control.

body.text: Modern energy systems are being impacted by the reduction of nuclear and fossil power generation as well as the increase of renewable power generation. These factors can cause stability problems in the HV-grid (reduction of short circuit power/ inertia and voltage dip stability) which might result in a blackout. In order to prevent this, power stations with black start capabilities are required, while synchronous condensers can supply power during short circuits, and ensure permanent dynamic voltage and reactive power control.

Siemens Energy offers a Synchronous condenser to stabilize the frequency and support the voltage also for long distances. They could generate electricity during dynamic peak demands and have the capability to build up the grid after black-out. The solution allows to utilize existing assets and therefore offers a very short Return on Investment (ROI)
bold: stabilize the frequency and support the voltage

body.text: Synchronous condenser

A synchronous condenser is a generator without a prime mover from a gas or steam turbine. It stabilizes the grid in changing reactive power demands. The rotating mass and the dynamic generation of reactive power stands for the high advantages of this product. The main benefits of a synchronous condenser are frequency stabilization and power supply during short circuits.

Any existing power plant generator type can be converted into a synchronous condenser. It can supply the grid with short circuit power and ensure permanent dynamic voltage and reactive power control. Synchronous condensers are designed to stabilize frequency and maintain voltage even over long distances.

They can generate electricity during dynamic peak demands and are able to build up the grid after a black-out. The project time for converting a plant is usually less than 12 months. The solution allows the use of existing assets and offers a very short return on investment (ROI).

items.title: Electrostatic precipitators
items.description: High efficiency electrostatic precipitators for power plants deliver reliable dust removal and flue gas particulate control to support strict emission limits.

body.text: Power plants face numerous challenges, including stringent environmental regulations, the need for efficient emissions control, and the pressure to reduce operational costs while maintaining performance. One significant issue is the management of particulate matter emissions, which can harm air quality and public health.

Electrostatic precipitators (ESPs) play a crucial role in addressing this challenge by collecting dust from the flue gas produced by boilers and other components. They support air pollution control not only at thermal power plants but also at various industrial facilities.

Siemens Energy offers suitable technologies tailored for plant applications and operations, combining compact design with high efficiency. By implementing ESP technology, Siemens Energy helps power plants minimize their environmental impact while enhancing operational efficiency, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable energy future.
Advanced inverter technology for ESP power supply

A high voltage is applied to the discharge electrode, generating a corona discharge that produces negative ions. The electrically charged dust is accumulated on the collecting electrode by an electrical field. The accumulated dust is removed by rapping hammer (dry ESP), scraping brush (dry ESP), or flushing water (wet ESP). The most important consideration in ESP for coal-fired boiler applications is to maintain and increase the collection of high-resistivity dust.
View of the Iskenerdrun steam power plant in Turkey

items.h1: Expansion turbines: integrally geared radial expanders
items.description: Integrally geared radial expanders (expansion turbines) are applied where energy can be recovered from off-gas or process gas streams from chemical and other industrial processes.

faqs.q: What is an expansion turbine?
faqs.a: An expansion turbine is a device that converts the energy of high-pressure gas into mechanical work by expanding the gas through a turbine.

faqs.q: How does an expansion turbine work?
faqs.a: It works by allowing pressurized gas to expand through a turbine, causing the turbine to spin and generate power, while cooling the gas in the process.

faqs.q: What is the efficiency of a expansion turbine?
faqs.a: Efficiency typically ranges from 70% to 90%, depending on design, operating conditions, and application.

faqs.q: What are the different types of expansion turbines?
faqs.a: Common types include: Radial or axial expandersOil-bearing or magnetic-bearing expandersGenerator-loaded or compressor-loaded expanders

faqs.q: What is the difference between turbine and turbo expander?
faqs.a: A turbine generally extracts energy from steam or combustion gases, while a turbo expander is specifically designed to recover energy from expanding gases, often in cryogenic or high-pressure applications.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of using Siemens Energy’s expansion turbines compared to traditional solutions?
faqs.a: We offer: High efficiency and reliabilityAdvanced digital monitoringCustom engineering for diverse applicationsReduced operational costs and emissions

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy expansion turbines contribute to carbon capture and decarbonization?
faqs.a: They enable energy recovery and cooling in gas separation processes, supporting carbon capture, natural gas processing, and low-emission operations.

faqs.q: What industries benefit most from the integration of expansion turbines?

body.text: Integrally geared radial expanders are applied where energy can be recovered from medium to high temperature off-gas or process gas streams from chemical and other industrial processes. The design is based on Siemens Energy's integrally geared centrifugal compressor concept invented more than 70 years ago.

Energy in the hot gas stream is converted directly to mechanical energy which can then be used to drive a compressor or generator respectively. While improving the overall energy balance of the plant, this also saves operating expenses as well as capital cost because there is no need for additional heat exchangers and steam generation equipment otherwise required for heat transfer.

Radial expanders can be configured as stand-alone units with up to three expansion stages arranged around a central bull gear, or they can be integrated into the casing of an integrally geared compressor transferring power directly to the compressor bull gear by a pinion shaft.

items.title: Fixed Series Capacitor (FSC)
items.description: Discover a cost-effective way to increase transmission capacity and enhance grid stability on both new and existing AC transmission lines.

faqs.q: What is fixed series compensation?
faqs.a: Fixed series compensation is a technology used in power transmission systems to enhance capacity and stability by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines. It involves the use of capacitors connected in series with the line to improve voltage regulation and power flow.

faqs.q: What are the fixed series compensation solutions?
faqs.a: Fixed series compensation solutions include the use of fixed series capacitors (FSC) to increase transmission capacity, reduce voltage drops, and improve system stability. These solutions are tailored to meet specific grid requirements and operational needs.

faqs.q: What is a fixed series capacitor (FSC) and how does it work?
faqs.a: A fixed series capacitor (FSC) is a device used in power transmission systems to increase capacity and stability by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines. It works by connecting a capacitor bank in series with the line, enhancing voltage regulation and power flow.

faqs.q: How does FSC improve transmission system capacity?
faqs.a: FSC improves transmission system capacity by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines, allowing for increased power flow and reduced voltage drops, thereby maximizing the utilization of existing infrastructure.

faqs.q: What are the main benefits of using Siemens Energy FSC technology?
faqs.a: Our FSC technology offers benefits such as increased transmission capacity, enhanced grid stability, reduced voltage drops, and improved power flow efficiency. It provides a cost-effective alternative to building new transmission lines.

faqs.q: How does FSC contribute to grid stability?
faqs.a: FSC contributes to grid stability by improving voltage regulation and reducing the transmission angle, which helps maintain a stable voltage profile and prevents voltage sags and swells.

faqs.q: Can FSC be used on both new and existing transmission lines?
faqs.a: Yes, FSC can be applied to both new and existing transmission lines, enhancing their capacity and stability without the need for extensive infrastructure modifications.

faqs.q: What protection mechanisms are included in Siemens Energy FSC?
faqs.a: Our FSC includes protection mechanisms such as metal-oxide varistors (MOV) and triggered spark gaps to safeguard against overvoltage conditions and ensure reliable operation.

faqs.q: Are Siemens Energy FSC components manufactured in-house?
faqs.a: Yes, Siemens Energy manufactures all major FSC components in-house, ensuring superior quality control and supply chain security.

faqs.q: How does FSC compare to building new transmission lines in terms of cost and time?
faqs.a: FSC is a cost-effective and time-efficient alternative to building new transmission lines, as it maximizes the capacity of existing infrastructure without the need for extensive construction and investment.

faqs.q: What customization options are available for FSC solutions?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offers customized FSC solutions tailored to specific grid requirements and site conditions, ensuring optimal performance and reliability.

faqs.q: How long has Siemens Energy been providing FSC technology?

body.text: What is fixed series compensation?

Innovative series compensation technology offers a cost-effective solution for increasing transmission capacities of existing long-distance AC transmission lines, enhancing grid stability without the need for new infrastructure. Siemens Energy fixed series capacitor (FSC) technology has been a cornerstone in improving grid stability and optimizing transmission line utilization for decades.

Transmission system operators worldwide have reaped the benefits of our tailored fixed series compensation solutions, designed to meet specific requirements. Key advantages of FSC include reducing line voltage drops, limiting load-dependent drops, and decreasing the transmission angle. These improvements contribute to a more efficient and reliable power transmission system, supporting the global energy transition and sustainable development goals.
Key benefits of Siemens Energy fixed series capacitors

Fixed series capacitors offer a range of advantages that enhance power transmission efficiency and grid stability. By integrating these advanced solutions, transmission system operators can significantly increase capacity and reliability without the need for costly new infrastructure.
Maximized transmission capacity

Fixed series capacitors effectively expand transmission capacity by compensating for the impedance of overhead lines. This cost-efficient solution allows for larger transmission capacities without the need for constructing new lines, optimizing existing infrastructure and enhancing power flow.
Enhanced grid stability and reliability

Fixed series compensation plays a crucial role in ensuring grid stability and reliability. By reducing voltage drops at the connection point, it provides system stability for bulk power transmission and long-distance lines, thereby strengthening overall grid resilience and performance.
Cost-efficient and scalable solution

Fixed series capacitors offer the most economical solution for transmission system operators. Their simple, proven, and robust technology optimizes power transmission and increases capacity. With all major components sourced in-house, Siemens Energy guarantees superior quality and reliability, underscoring its commitment to excellence in power transmission solutions.
How does our fixed series capacitor (FSC) work?

The amount of power that can be transferred through long overhead transmission lines is often limited by impedance, which can lead to voltage drops. For decades, fixed series compensation has been the proven solution to maintain a minimum voltage profile and maximize the utilization of transmission lines. Siemens Energy fixed series capacitor (FSC) technology addresses these challenges by increasing voltage at the connection point, reducing transmission angle and line voltage drops, and improving power transfer capability and system stability.

FSC works by connecting a capacitor bank in series with the transmission line to partially compensate for the inductive impedance of the line. This setup increases the voltage at the point of connection, enhancing the overall efficiency of power transmission. The capacitors are protected by metal-oxide varistors (MOV) and, in case of a fault, the FSC is tripped and the bypass breaker is closed. For instant protection, a triggered spark gap bypasses capacitors and MOVs within less than 1 ms. Gap-less solutions are also possible, provided that local requirements match.

Due to the complexity and precision required, Siemens Energy recommends and offers individually designed solutions with fixed series capacitors, ensuring optimal performance tailored to specific grid needs.
Applications of FSC

Long-distance high-voltage AC lines
Grid modernization and stability enhancement projects
Renewable energy integration requiring voltage support and reactive power control
Industrial power systems demanding reliable and efficient transmission

What is fixed series compensation?

Fixed series compensation is a technology used in power transmission systems to enhance capacity and stability by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines. It involves the use of capacitors connected in series with the line to improve voltage regulation and power flow.
What are the fixed series compensation solutions?

Fixed series compensation solutions include the use of fixed series capacitors (FSC) to increase transmission capacity, reduce voltage drops, and improve system stability. These solutions are tailored to meet specific grid requirements and operational needs.
What is a fixed series capacitor (FSC) and how does it work?

A fixed series capacitor (FSC) is a device used in power transmission systems to increase capacity and stability by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines. It works by connecting a capacitor bank in series with the line, enhancing voltage regulation and power flow.
How does FSC improve transmission system capacity?

FSC improves transmission system capacity by compensating for the inductive impedance of transmission lines, allowing for increased power flow and reduced voltage drops, thereby maximizing the utilization of existing infrastructure.
What are the main benefits of using Siemens Energy FSC technology?

Our FSC technology offers benefits such as increased transmission capacity, enhanced grid stability, reduced voltage drops, and improved power flow efficiency. It provides a cost-effective alternative to building new transmission lines.
How does FSC contribute to grid stability?
FSC contributes to grid stability by improving voltage regulation and reducing the transmission angle, which helps maintain a stable voltage profile and prevents voltage sags and swells.
Can FSC be used on both new and existing transmission lines?
Yes, FSC can be applied to both new and existing transmission lines, enhancing their capacity and stability without the need for extensive infrastructure modifications.
What protection mechanisms are included in Siemens Energy FSC?
Our FSC includes protection mechanisms such as metal-oxide varistors (MOV) and triggered spark gaps to safeguard against overvoltage conditions and ensure reliable operation.
Are Siemens Energy FSC components manufactured in-house?
Yes, Siemens Energy manufactures all major FSC components in-house, ensuring superior quality control and supply chain security.
How does FSC compare to building new transmission lines in terms of cost and time?

FSC is a cost-effective and time-efficient alternative to building new transmission lines, as it maximizes the capacity of existing infrastructure without the need for extensive construction and investment.
What customization options are available for FSC solutions?
Siemens Energy offers customized FSC solutions tailored to specific grid requirements and site conditions, ensuring optimal performance and reliability.
How long has Siemens Energy been providing FSC technology?
Siemens Energy has been providing FSC technology for decades, leveraging extensive experience and expertise to deliver reliable and innovative solutions for power transmission systems.

faqs.q: Why are integral natural gas engines important today?
faqs.a: Natural gas compression is a critical component of the oil and gas industry, enabling the efficient transportation, processing, and storage of natural gas across upstream, midstream, and downstream sectors. Among the various types of compressors used, the natural gas-driven integral engine compressor stands out for its unique design and operational advantages. These systems, which combine the engine and compressor into a single unit sharing a common crankshaft, have been a mainstay in pipeline infrastructure since the mid-20th century. Integral engine compressors are designed for mechanical simplicity and long life, which translates into high reliability and efficiency. Unlike separable packages—where the engine and compressor are distinct units connected via couplings—integral compressors feature a single frame and crankshaft, reducing the number of moving parts and potential failure points.

items.description: Discover Siemens Energy's innovative grid connectivity solutions for efficient, reliable, and secure energy integration worldwide.

body.text: Power grids are essential as they form the backbone of electricity transmission, connecting sources of power generation to end users, including homes, businesses, and industries. A well-functioning power grid is crucial for ensuring a stable supply of electricity, reducing the risk of blackouts, and integrating renewable energy sources, such as wind or solar.
Connecting energy systems and bringing power from where it's generated to where it's needed

Power grids aren't ready yet for tomorrow's energy landscape. Aging infrastructure, increasing energy demand, and the need to optimize grid utilization, along with the integration of renewables, require modernization and expansion of power grids worldwide.

With a broad portfolio of innovative transmission products, systems, solutions, and services, Siemens Energy supports customers on their energy transition journeys and makes sure to bring power from where it is generated to where it is needed.
Driving positive change through innovative solutions

At Siemens Energy, we offer solutions that enable an efficient energy transfer between regions, helping to cover the increasing energy demand, and securing energy access and electrification, for example of industries and data centers.
Integration of renewable energy

To reach climate neutrality by 2050, more renewable energy sources need to be integrated into the power grid. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), 3.000 GW of renewable power projects are waiting to be connected. In total, the grid is estimated to double in size by 2040 (IEA), resulting in an increasing demand in corresponding grid technologies.

We enable the transmission of renewable power, reducing dependance on fossil fuels and promoting a clean energy mix. Our innovative solutions, including offshore grid connections and high-voltage direct current systems, facilitate the seamless integration of renewable energy sources, such as offshore wind farms and solar power plants, into the electrical grid.
Covering increasing electricity demand

Infrastructure facilities, industry, and private households around the world require more and more electrical energy. As electricity demand continues to rise, it is essential to ensure a reliable power supply that can meet these needs.

Our high-voltage substations solutions, including our product offerings, such as transformers, gas-insulated switchgear, circuit breakers, surge arresters and disconnectors and earthing switches, serve as critical node points within today's intricate power transmission infrastructure, playing a vital role in safely and reliably meeting this demand.
Energy access & electrification of industries and data centers
We help to bring reliable energy to remote and underserved areas, thus facilitating energy access and electrification.

Our pre-assembled micro substation offers a one-step transition from high voltage to low voltage, enabling fast deployment and versatile applications. And with a comprehensive range of products and solutions, we ensure that industries and data centers can quickly adapt to changing needs and remain at the forefront of technological advancements.
Our solutions for an interconnected, reliable power grid

We enable transmission grids to cope with growing demands, the shift from traditional fossil-fuel based energy systems to renewable sources, and increasing system complexity with our products, solutions, digital offerings, and services. Step by step, we're making power grids ready.
High-voltage substations

High-voltage substations, the node points of today's complex power transmission infrastructure, play a key role in meeting the increasing electricity demand safely and reliably. We provide the entire range of services, technologies, and components that are required for the successful construction and operation of a high-voltage substation of any type.
High-voltage direct current (HVDC)

HVDC is ideal for bridging the distances between large-scale renewable power generating installations such as offshore wind farms and the load centers they serve. In a multi-terminal configuration, the collecting of renewable power can be combined with pan-continental integration of power transmission systems, such as for interconnecting multiple regional or national AC grids.
Offshore grid connections

Integrating renewable energy sources is key to meeting society's energy needs while fighting climate change. Yet, these contributions to more carbon-neutral energy take place in remote areas often hundreds or even thousands of kilometers away from the centers of consumption. We provide reliable and efficient transmission systems to connect remote renewable energy sources to the grid.
Data center power solutions

Data centers face significant challenges as power demand soars. We understand the unique requirements of data centers and offer a comprehensive range of products and solutions, ensuring that data centers can quickly adapt to changing needs and remain at the forefront of technological advancements.
Micro substations

Our pre-assembled micro substation offers a one-step transition from high voltage to low voltage for fast deployment in various applications, including remote electrification and EV charging. Key benefits include quick installation, transportability, scalability, cost-effectiveness for underserved areas, a sustainable SF₆-free Blue portfolio, and reliable power access in regions without MV/LV grids.

body.text: Why choose iSER™ Actuators?

Many steam turbines are controlled by antiquated mechanical hydraulic control (MHC) systems resulting in control issues, unplanned outages due to failures and wear, and high maintenance costs. In addition, the experienced personnel required to operate and maintain these systems are rapidly disappearing and finding replacement parts is increasingly difficult. The main barrier to upgrading to a modern electrohydraulic control (EHC) system is the exceptionally large capital investment in the demolition of the old system, installation of the new system, and updates to the plant control system. The single largest expense when modernizing a control system is typically the installation of new welded high-pressure piping for the hydraulic system.

body.text: The Siemens Energy iSER™ Actuators solve these challenges at a significantly lower cost. Their self-contained design of these electrohydraulic actuators eliminates the main costs of piping installation while providing the precision control needed for operation and increasing the reliability, safety, and flexibility that turbine owners desire. In addition, Siemens Energy iSER Actuators offer advantages over modern EHC systems, including eliminating virtually all leak points, greatly improved diagnostic capabilities, and enabling of predictive instead of reactive maintenance.

The iSER™ Actuator – how it works

The patented Siemens Energy iSER™ Actuator is a linear actuator providing precise position control of valves based on a 4-to-20 mA input current signal. The actuator was designed for the demanding application of steam turbine control and the pumping system was developed by Siemens Energy to provide optimal flow and precise motion control of the actuator, all while offering the redundancy needed for reliable and safe operation.
bold: designed for the demanding application of steam turbine control

body.text: Siemens Energy iSER™ Actuator is a self-contained hydraulic system. This means that all the pumps, motors, valves, and other components necessary to operate the hydraulic cylinder are attached to the cylinder itself and there is no separate hydraulic power unit or associated piping. It is also a hydrostatic system, so when the actuator has reached the desired position, the motors turn off and the valve is held in position.

The iSER™ Actuator design has been specifically built to provide hassle free operation and full redundancy of critical components. Internally it has a 2-out-of-2 (2oo2) fluid pumping design with two dedicated motors/pumps for forward stroke and two for backward stroke, ensuring fault tolerant operation during its service. The actuator will continue to operate with the loss of 1 motor in either forward or backward stroke.

body.text: Industrial Power distribution
Comprehensive power distribution for paper mills

Our system ensures stable, efficient power across your entire process, including black starts and emergency modes. Intelligent controls and seamless communication guarantee high availability and power quality.
From transformers to HV, MV, and LV switchgear and protection systems, we deliver everything for a complete, future-proof distribution solution.
Power control technology for a transparent energy flow
Industrial power distribution gives you real-time insight into all electrical processes and provides key service data at a glance.
Intelligent monitoring to avoid costly peaks:

Using smart protection relays, direct online motor starters and energy-efficient frequency converters with fiber-optic networks. The system tracks every switching operation, predicts load trends, and helps avoid costly peak demand charges or blackouts through proactive control.
Cost-optimized planning from experienced specialists
Our industrial power distribution offers end-to-end power supply solutions from a single source – fully integrated across all voltage levels and lifecycle phases.

We analyze all relevant mill data – from power demands to short-circuit capacities – to design a resilient, efficient network. Emergency concepts, availability targets, and grid requirements are factored in from the start. Dynamic fault simulations ensure fast recovery and optimal performance in any scenario.
Get the performance you need – with Power Intelligence

Power Intelligence is a comprehensive portfolio of digital products and solutions. These are designed to enable power utilities and industries to unlock the full potential of their electrical infrastructure. They provide insightful data for decision-making, enhance asset management, improve reliability and efficiency, and reduce operational costs.
Energy Management

The pulp and paper industry has already taken a leading role in the closed-cycle economy by making optimal use of resources, integrating waste products into processes, optimizing energy requirements, transforming into a self-sufficient energy cycle, and using digitalization tools.
Managing the water steam cycle in the pulp and paper industry

We know the importance of a flexible steam turbine design and customization. That is why we provide steam turbines with various uncontrolled and controlled extraction options adapted to the steam flow in your process. We can offer the precise number of extractions indicated by your process requirements.
Implementation of a gas turbine in tissue drying process

The Yankee drying process is the most common drying method. Small gas turbines are desirable for use in the Yankee process because the demand for hot air is lower compared with the Through Air Dryer (TAD) process. TAD uses heat to dewater the product instead of the conventional mechanical pressing. This produces a much softer paper and reduces the demand for raw material from 8% to 30%, but dramatically increases the drying load. The high demand of hot air means that the implementation of gas turbines up to 10 MW is profitable for the TAD process.
Innovative services for the digital future of industry

faqs.q: What are the key benefits of using a wind control system for offshore wind energy?
faqs.a: Omnivise T3000 connects wind turbines, substation automation, auxiliaries and direct marketing through a single platform in a centralized view. It enables easy operation of multiple remote plants from a Central Control Center over the entire lifecycle of your wind farm.

faqs.q: Can different renewable energy sources be integrated into a single offshore wind control system?
faqs.a: Yes, the Siemens Energy Omnivise T3000 control system is designed to integrate multiple renewable energy sources into a single, integrated platform. This flexibility allows operators to manage not only offshore wind energy but also other sources such as solar, battery storage (BESS) and hydroelectric power. Omnivise T3000 is equipped to meet the challenges facing both the traditional and the new power generation landscape. By utilizing the Omnivise T3000, energy producers can optimize their operations, enhance grid stability, and improve overall energy management. This capability makes the Omnivise T3000 an ideal solution for modern, multi-source energy systems, ensuring efficient and sustainable energy production.

faqs.q: What are the primary use cases and applications of offshore wind control systems?
faqs.a: The Siemens Energy Omnivise T3000 control system is essential for enhancing the efficiency and security of offshore wind energy operations. It implements robust cybersecurity measures to protect against threats and ensure compliance with regulations like the NIS Directive and NERC CIP. Additionally, the Omnivise T3000 supports proactive maintenance and condition-based monitoring, optimizing the lifecycle of wind farms while reducing costs. Its ability to integrate energy storage, solar PV, and green hydrogen production enables hybridization, improving reliability and opening new revenue streams. Overall, the Omnivise T3000 enhances offshore wind energy operations, supporting a sustainable clean energy future.

faqs.q: Which offshore wind parks can utilize the Omnivise T3000 control system?
faqs.a: Our Omnivise solutions can be utilized in a wide range of offshore wind parks, regardless of their size or configuration. It is compatible with various turbine models and can be tailored to meet the specific needs of different projects. Whether for new installations or existing wind farms, Siemens Energy provides a robust and flexible solution for managing offshore wind energy operations. Its adaptability makes it an ideal choice for both large-scale offshore wind farms and smaller, localized projects, ensuring efficient energy production across diverse environments.

As wind power grows so does their risk of cyber attacks, making strong cybersecurity measures vital to prevent financial losses, power outages, and reputational damage.

Wind farms must comply with strict cybersecurity regulations like the NIS Directive, NERC CIP, and KRITIS due to their critical role in national power supplies. A secure-by-design approach, considering cybersecurity from the earliest design stages through ongoing operations, is essential. Standardizing equipment and configurations simplifies monitoring and maintenance, while clear responsibility for cybersecurity at each lifecycle phase ensures integrated, site-wide defenses.

items.title: Benson technology
items.description: Steam is an essential element in the energy supply system. Siemens Energy offers steam generation based on Benson® technology or drum-type steam generators.

body.text: Benson technology is a proven process for large-scale steam generation in power plants. The heart of this process is the once-through principle. Combined with sliding pressure operation, this allows for highly efficient, flexible, and reliable power plant operation. Our Benson technology and our associated Benson license will improve your specific steam generator and, consequently, benefit your power plant performance.
Experience and expertise

Since 1933, leading steam generator manufacturers worldwide have built Benson steam generators under licence from Siemens Energy. Benson technology is widely used in fired steam generators for steam power plants, with over 1,300 units commissioned worldwide.
Today, the company is focusing on deploying Benson technology in heat recovery steam generators (HRSGs) for highly efficient combined cycle power plants to support the energy transition.

items: Benson HRSGs in combined cycle power plants
Research and development

body.text: Superior technology for the latest power plant applications
Today's combined cycle power plants must be more efficient and flexible than ever before. They need to:

items: Cover peak loads
Serve as backup reserves for renewables

body.text: This is where Benson HRSGs make an important contribution. Benson HRSGs can be constructed either horizontally or vertically and will fit into any power plant architecture.
Benefits compared with drum-type steam generators
bold: Benefits compared with drum-type steam generators

items: Steam parameters can be increased because there is no pressure limitation
Increased efficiency in part-load operation and at high ambient temperatures, thanks to reduced attemperator flows compared with a drum-type HRSG
Increased operational flexibility: no limit on gas turbine load transients during startup and load changes, and no limit on load transients for possible duct firing

body.text: The first combined cycle power plant with a Benson heat-recovery steam generator (HRSG) – the 390-MW Cottam CDC, located in Great Britain – was successfully commissioned in 1999. More than 130 Benson heat-recovery steam generators have been commissioned to date or are currently under construction.
Start with something good – and make it even better

Thanks to continuous research and development, Benson steam generators are recognised for their excellent operating characteristics and high reliability. Depending on the specific boundary conditions of your project, we refine and optimise the design of your Benson evaporator. Another priority is developing Benson-specific control concepts, which play a key role in ensuring your system operates at its best.

From 1975 to 2023, Siemens Energy operated a dedicated Benson test rig for conducting thermohydraulic investigations of two-phase flows in evaporator tubes. These campaigns generated an extensive database on heat transfer and pressure drop in Benson evaporator tubes. The Benson test rig was also used to investigate the physical phenomena of dynamic instabilities. All of these findings support the development and validation of Siemens Energy's Benson design software.
History of the Benson Licence

In 1925, Siemens acquired the right to use Benson's patent, and in 1926–27 the first large Benson boiler in Berlin-Gartenfeld was built. Siemens improved the technology and developed it as an internationally acknowledged standard for large steam generators. In 1933, Siemens decided that it would no longer manufacture steam generators in its facilities, but would instead award licenses based on its own patents and expertise. body.text: Siemens Energy is meeting the growing demand for efficient and sustainable power generation. Our Combined Cycle Power Plants (CCPP) integrate advanced gas and steam turbines to achieve efficiencies in excess of 64%, significantly lower emissions and the flexibility to match output to demand.
With innovative single and multi-shaft configurations, Siemens Energy provides reliable and environmentally friendly power generation for both 50 Hz and 60 Hz markets.
What is a combined cycle power plant?
A combined cycle power plant is a highly efficient type of power plant that uses both gas turbines and steam turbines to generate electricity.

But how does it work? By using both a gas turbine and a steam turbine, these plants can generate more electricity from the same amount of fuel compared to a simple cycle gas plant, because it combines two thermodynamic cycles: the Brayton cycle (gas turbine) and the Rankine cycle (steam turbine).
Combined cycle power plant diagram
The diagram shows a typical combined cycle plant layout and process.
The plant burns natural gas to produce hot gases. These gase spin the rotor of a gas turbine driving a generator to produce electricity.
The hot exhaust gases are used in a heat recovery steam generator to produce steam.
The steam drives a steam turbine generator producing additional electricity.
Fuels for gas turbines

While natural gas is the most common fuel, combined cycle power plants can also use a variety of other fuels including hydrogen, biogas, syngas, diesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), or other gaseous or liquid fuels.
Benefits of combined cycle power plants

Siemens Energy combines technology, experience, and workforce to provide cutting-edge combined cycle power plants. These technologies aim to deliver a low lifecycle cost of converting fuel into electricity.
Higher efficiency
By utilizing both gas and steam turbines, CCPPs can achieve efficiencies of over 64%.
Lower carbon emissions
The efficient use of fuel results in reduced greenhouse gas emissions.
Operational flexibility
CCPPs can quickly ramp up or down, making them ideal for balancing renewable energy sources.
Low electricity costs
High performance with low power generation costs to help reduce the levelized cost of energy (LCOE).
Our scope of supply for CCPP solutions

At Siemens Energy, we are pioneering sustainable power generation with our advanced gas and steam turbines. Our combined cycle power plants, ranging from about 40MW up to 1,800MW, provide unmatched reliability and efficiency for both 50 and 60Hz markets, tailoring single-shaft and multi-shaft configurations to your specific needs. Choose Siemens Energy for fast, precise power plant development.

Our combined cycle power plants (CCPP) are engineered for high efficiency and cost-effective electricity generation, catering to both 50Hz and 60Hz markets with options for single- and multishaft designs.

A single-shaft configuration entails a gas turbine that is directly coupled to a steam turbine, with both sharing a single common generator. Conversely, in a multishaft configuration, each turbine - gas and steam - operates with its own dedicated generator.
Single-shaft configuration
In a single-shaft configuration, the gas and steam turbines are on one shaft line with a common generator, reducing the number of components.
The single-shaft setup offers cost savings of 3-5%, higher efficiency, and a smaller footprint due to fewer mechanical connections and simplified BOP systems.
Multi-shaft configuration
Multi-shaft configurations use separate generators for each turbine.
Multi-shaft configurations are chosen for specific requirements or when the gas turbine operates before the combined cycle development.
Power output for combined cycle configurations
Combined cycle plants are highly efficient and maximize power output by utilizing both gas and steam turbines to convert excess heat into additional electricity.

items.description: Decarbonize your independent power supply while ensuring cheap, available energy with a hybrid power solution from Siemens Energy.

faqs.q: What are hybrid power solutions?
faqs.a: Hybrid power solutions integrate multiple energy sources—such as renewables, energy storage, and traditional generators—into a single intelligent system to ensure reliable, efficient, and sustainable electricity supply.

faqs.q: What are hybrid power systems?
faqs.a: A hybrid power system is an integrated energy setup that combines multiple power sources—typically renewable technologies like solar and wind with energy storage and sometimes conventional generators—to deliver reliable, efficient, and often grid-independent electricity supply while reducing reliance on fossil fuels and improving resilience.

faqs.q: Why are hybrid power solutions important for remote or off-grid locations?
faqs.a: Hybrid power systems help overcome limited or unreliable grid access by combining sources like solar, wind, batteries, and generators, guaranteeing stable and cost-effective energy even in challenging environments.

faqs.q: How do hybrid power solutions support decarbonization?
faqs.a: By maximizing the use of renewable energy and reducing reliance on fossil fuels, these systems lower emissions and help customers meet their sustainability targets.

faqs.q: What is the role of intelligent control in hybrid power systems?
faqs.a: "Advanced control platforms, such as Siemens Energy’s Omnivise Hybrid Control, continuously optimize energy dispatch, balance fluctuations, and coordinate all assets for maximum efficiency and reliability.​"

faqs.q: What are the main components of Siemens Energy hybrid power solutions?
faqs.a: Core components may include solar panels, wind turbines, battery energy storage systems, electrolyzers, heat pumps, and smart controllers—customized to each site’s needs.

faqs.q: Can hybrid power solutions integrate hydrogen technologies?
faqs.a: Yes, Siemens Energy offers systems that combine green hydrogen production and storage for additional flexibility, clean fuel generation, and re-electrification.

faqs.q: How do hybrid power solutions improve grid stability
faqs.a: Energy storage and smart dispatching smooth out variability from renewables, provide backup power, and enable better load management, resulting in higher grid reliability and fewer outages.

faqs.q: What are the advantages of battery energy storage in a hybrid system?
faqs.a: Batteries store excess renewable power, supply electricity when demand is high or generation is low, back up critical loads, and help balance the grid efficiently.

faqs.q: Are Siemens Energy hybrid power solutions customizable?
faqs.a: Yes, solutions are tailored to client requirements, site conditions, and decarbonization goals through modular designs, scalable components, and digital control.

faqs.q: How can I learn more or get started with Siemens Energy hybrid power solutions?
faqs.a: Visit the Siemens Energy website, watch solution videos, review technical white papers, or contact their experts for an in-depth consultation or cost-optimized project design.

Battery Energy Storage System

Integrated electrolyzer and heat pump solution

Boost the efficiency of hydrogen production while decarbonizing district heating: For the production of green hydrogen, typically 70-80% of the electrical energy is used to split water into hydrogen and oxygen, while the rest is converted into waste heat. With our integrated electrolyzer and heat pump solution, we combine the production of hydrogen and heat: The heat pump dissipates the waste heat from the electrolyzer, raises its temperature to a higher level and makes it available for other processes, such as district heating. By removing waste heat, the heat pump also provides cooling for the electrolyzer, minimizing the need for other cooling equipment. Batteries store excess renewable power, supply electricity when demand is high or generation is low, back up critical loads, and help balance the grid efficiently.

Yes, solutions are tailored to client requirements, site conditions, and decarbonization goals through modular designs, scalable components, and digital control.

Visit the Siemens Energy website, watch solution videos, review technical white papers, or contact their experts for an in-depth consultation or cost-optimized project design.

faqs.q: How much does a modular data center cost?
faqs.a: The cost of a modular data center can vary widely depending on factors such as size, capacity, and specific requirements. Siemens Energy and Eaton provide customizable solutions that can be tailored to fit different budgetary constraints.

faqs.q: How to design modular data centers?
faqs.a: Designing modular data centers involves assessing the specific needs of the organization, selecting appropriate modules, ensuring efficient power and cooling systems, and planning for scalability and flexibility to accommodate future growth. Siemens Energy and Eaton offer design services and solutions that help optimize the layout and efficiency of modular data centers.

faqs.q: What firms manage rapid-deployment modular data centers?
faqs.a: Several firms specialize in rapid-deployment modular data centers, including Siemens Energy and Eaton. These companies provide solutions that can be quickly deployed to meet urgent data center needs, leveraging their expertise in engineering and technology.

faqs.q: Why are modular solutions preferred for fast-growing data centers?
faqs.a: Modular solutions are preferred for fast-growing data centers because they offer scalability, flexibility, and speed of deployment. Siemens Energy and Eaton’s modular solutions allow organizations to quickly expand their data center capacity without the long lead times associated with traditional construction.

faqs.q: How large is the modular data centers market?
faqs.a: The modular data center market is experiencing rapid growth, driven by the need for scalable, energy-efficient, and quickly deployable infrastructure.

faqs.q: What are the main benefits of modular data centers?
faqs.a: The main benefits of modular data centers include quick deployment, scalability, energy efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and the ability to customize solutions to meet specific needs. Siemens Energy and Eaton provide solutions that offer reduced construction time and lower initial capital expenditure compared to traditional data centers.

body.text: Siemens Energy and Eaton have partnered to offer a cutting-edge solution that focuses on flexible and repeatable power, enabling the design of data center campuses to meet hyperscaler lifecycle requirements. This innovative approach features modular design, supporting power needs ideal for data centers exceeding 100MW, and is adaptable to various types of data centers, including Cloud, LLM, and AI. Additionally, the power-to-chip solutions cater to diverse customer requirement, allowing for the replication of designs in other locations and countries.
Siemens Energy's data center power solutions ensure efficient and reliable energy supply, significantly reducing deployment times and enabling rapid scalability.
Tackling the challenges of next-generation data centers

The digital world is expanding, with AI, cloud computing, and hyperscale services driving the rapidly growing demand for data center services. Meeting the substantial electricity demand of data centers presents a major challenge, as grid bottlenecks, rising costs, and environmental concerns pose significant obstacles.

The joint initiative offers a competitive and future-proof solution: an industry-first integrated, on-site power generation system paired with modular data center construction. This approach enables data centers to go live faster, reducing deployment timelines by up to two years. The power plant design incorporates redundancy, eliminating the need for backup diesel generators and reducing CO2 emissions by about 50 percent.
bold: reducing deployment timelines by up to two years

body.text: This solution offers investment flexibility and increased ROI by providing a dedicated power supply designed for future upgrades. It adapts to shifts in power density following rack exchanges and employs modular combinations to meet strategic needs, ensuring a future-proof infrastructure.
The modular data center solutions address key strategic priorities:
Efficiency

Grid access delays challenge timely deployment. The solution enables grid-independent, clean on-site power, boosting operational efficiency. With balanced energization, optimized CapEx, and essential equipment, we ensure streamlined deployment and operational independence, maximizing efficiency in both setup and ongoing operations.
Sustainability

Decarbonization is central. Siemens Energy is providing low carbon solutions, including SF6-free power and grid-interactive UPSs, alongside sustainable manufacturing. Hydrogen-ready gas turbines and modular systems reduce emissions, while eco-passport availability and future-ready power options like hydrogen power, HVO, and CCUS help meet company goals and regulations.
Reliability

Siemens Energy ensure 99.99%+ uptime with redundant gas turbines and battery storage, removing the need for diesel backup. The approach includes essential onsite equipment and balanced energization, enhancing operational stability and reducing the need for extensive testing and commissioning, supporting continuous operations and system resilience.
We offer hyperscalers, co-locators and investors a unique package, enabling them to reduce the time-to-market by up to two years in many places, which leads to significant revenue gains.
Global head of sales, Gas Services Business Area, Siemens Energy

items: No dependency on external power: Highly available, flexible, and efficient distributed power generation with gas turbines provides more freedom to choose data center location without relying on external power sources.

Modularized & expandable design: Integrated modular designs allow for fast installation and expansion, providing scalability to meet growing data center demands.

Operational flexibility: The combined power system for data centers includes base load, backup, and storage solutions, offering critical grid services and benefits, including unconditional dispatchable power.

“Pay as you grow” revenue: This approach enables 100% on-site power generation with grid connection later. It supports white space and campus growth as needed, increasing CapEx efficiency. As the campus and ancillary services grow, revenue increases, allowing capacity expansion regardless of grid availability.

Ready for decarbonization: Utilization of advanced power generation technologies, such as green fuel-ready gas turbines and battery energy storage systems, enables the use of available natural gas initially, with a switch to green fuels later, eliminating the need for diesel engines and reducing emissions.
