BlueVault lithium-ion battery systems support all-electric and hybrid power plants by providing energy storage for peak shaving, spinning reserve, and backup power, significantly reducing onboard fuel consumption, emissions, and engine running hours.
What is the SGM shaft generator with motor function and why is it important?

The Shaft Generator with Motor function is a PTO/PTI system (power take-off/power take-in) that can work both as a shaft generator (PTO) and as a shaft motor (PTI) enabling electrical power generation and propulsion boost while reducing fuel consumption and emissions and supporting integration with waste-heat recovery or hybrid concepts.

body.text: Electric pod systems are widely used on diesel-electric-powered vessels where very high levels of maneuverability, efficiency, and reliability are required. With its POD-M (mono propeller) and POD-T (twin propeller), Siemens Eneegy offers a solution in the power range from 5 MW to 23 MW that allows maximum flexibility in vessel design and layout thanks to minimal space requirement on board. The crucial advantage of POD-M/-T is the substantially higher overall efficiency resulting from the combination of a compact, hydrodynamically optimized design and efficient, permanently excited synchronous motor.
Discover efficient diesel-electric propulsion system with twin or mono propellers.

body.text: Podded propulsion solutions at a glance

In the area of electric pod-based systems, we are the only supplier of podded propulsion systems equipped optionally with twin or mono propellers. This means that the propulsion system can be optimally adapted for your needs, all depending on the type of vessel and operating profile. Whether you opt for a twin or mono propeller version, you benefit from an innovative drive system that meets your requirements fully.
POD-M
With the POD-M, we offerr a solution in the power range from 5 MW to 23 MW that allows maximum flexibility in vessel design and layout thanks to minimal space requirement on board.
POD-T
Twin-propeller systems keep space requirements under the stern to an absolute minimum. The POD-T allows for more flexible ship designs and maximizes the payload capacity.
POD Service Container

To be prepared for on-site conditions, which can sometimes be harsh, the fully equipped POD Service Container contains both standard and special-purpose tools, lifting devices, and air-conditioning and heating equipment.
Optimized open water performance with mono propeller

Sailing open waters is an extraordinary task for every vessel. Not only the ship itself, but also its propulsion systems have to operate on the highest level of performance. With the mono-propeller propulsion system POD-M, we offer you a solution for vessels facing performance and efficiency challenges in these waters.
Increased propeller surface and reduced weight with high hydrodynamic efficiency and low noise level

The POD-M is the podded system of choice for vessels with demanding requirements in terms of open water performance and efficiency. The POD-M is equipped with an optimized strut which prevents vibrations and increases course stability. The hydrodynamic efficiency is even further increased thanks to the slim propeller hub and streamlined design. Cruise ships and other large passenger vessels, megayachts, as well as special vessels with specific ice class requirements particularly benefit from the advantages of the POD-M.
Your advantages with POD-M

body.text: Maximum thrust in minimal space due to twin-propeller layout
If you are looking for a high vessel design flexibility and payload capacity at the same time, our POD-T twin-propeller propulsion system is the right choice for you.
Cast off at any time with twin propeller propulsion

Twin propeller systems keep space requirements under the stern to an absolute minimum. The POD-T allows for more flexible ship designs and maximizes the payload capacity. This is an advantage especially for ferries, special vessels, and naval support vessels.

Having electrical properties resembling those of a conventional synchronized motor, the permanently excited motor can be integrated without limitations into conventional drive systems. In the process, the higher level of availability of the diesel-electric outboard drives also leads to a marked increase in operational reliability. No other type of drive system offers comparable flexibility for designing hulls and engine rooms than azimuthing diesel-electric propulsion systems.
Expanded service capability for POD-M/-T

The loss of even one day of vessel deployment due to a breakdown or failure can significantly impact your balance sheet. Like you, we are well aware of these challenges and address them with special offerings such as our fully equipped POD Service Container.
Be prepared for whatever happens

To be prepared for on-site conditions, which can sometimes be harsh, the fully equipped POD Service Container contains both standard and special-purpose tools, lifting devices, air-conditioning and heating equipment. Together with our new logistics concept, this allows us to substantially decrease maintenance times and also better access and reduce any risks while maintenance is being performed.

A material container has recently complemented the Siemens Energy POD workshop container with all necessary tools for podded drive maintenance. This container additionally acts as an extension of the workshop space. It carries empty material boxes for dismounted large components, such as shaft bearings. This ensures safe transportation at the shipyard and beyond, and also protects sensitive parts regardless of the outside conditions. Overall, the POD material container boosts the shipyard's independence.

DigiTRON products
The DigiTRON range of connectors provides world leading trusted quality and long-lasting reliability.
Controls and instrumentation connectors
DigiTRON+ and DigiTRONe

DigiTRON+ and DigiTRONe are the most reliable and advanced subsea connectors used by the subsea industry to date. Qualified to operate in depths of up to 4,000 meters, a MTBF (Mean Time Between Failure) of 400,000 years and an enviable track record; The DigiTRON range of connectors are the most technically advanced and reliable subsea connectors on the market.
DigiTRON3

DigiTRON3 has all the benefits you would expect from the world leader in subsea connectors. Our trusted proven track record provides quality and reliability where it's needed most. Our new DigiTRON3 connector has an enhanced design with a voltage rating of 1.8/3 (3.6) kV. With the aim to reduce the size and quantity of connectors required for high voltage control applications this connector is perfect for long step out projects. The compact connector size reduces impact on structures and therefore reducing overall subsea costs.
DigiTRONf

DigiTRONf is a compact 12-way optical fibre wet mate connector, from the trusted DigiTRON range. DigiTRONf offers excellent optical performance and has been designed and qualified with a focus on reliability and quality. The 12-line connector offers excellent system flexibility and a greater degree of redundancy, allowing for less connectors being required. Qualified to the recently published SEAFOM TSD-02, DigiTRONf is a modular product which offers a complete system.
Advanced Cable Termination (ACT, ACT3) and Advanced Fibre Termination (AFT)

body.text: SpecTRON products
A world leading range of subsea wet-mate and dry-mate subsea electrical connector systems for subsea power distribution.
Subsea medium and high voltage electrical connector systems

SpecTRON offers the most comprehensive range of technically advanced and reliable subsea power connectors on the market. With an enviable track record and an extensive range of HV power connectors SpecTRON can be used on a wide range of subsea applications in subsea oil and gas and renewable energy.
SpecTRON 8

SpecTRON 8 is Siemens Energy's solution for small multiphase pumping, electro-submersible pumps (ESPs), tidal/wave energy machines, and long step-out control systems. It is a compact, three-phase connector solution which can be connected by remotely operating vehicles (ROVs) as well as application specific “Stab” plates. The product range includes umbilical termination units, high pressure penetrators and a feed-through system for in-well single and dual ESP systems.
The SpecTRON 8 dual penetrator solution has been specifically designed and developed for subsea ETH projects. The product consists of the following:-
A Dual Penetrator - 3.8/6.6(7.6)kV, 120A, 300bar rated bi-directional Dual Penetrator assembly system utilising metallic sealing.
The penetrator assembly is utilised to penetrate the annulus in PiP ETH systems.
Cold Splice - 3.8/6.6(7.6)kV, 120A rated splice assembly utilised to terminate the inboard side of the Dual Penetrator assembly to the ETH cables.

Hot Splice - 3.8/6.6(7.6)kV, 120A rated splice system used to splice the ETH cables along the length of the PiP. Utilises triple layer elastomeric moulding for electric field control and allows for quick and reliable splicing operations.
SpecTRON 10

Siemens Energy's SpecTRON 10 connector system is designed to support the needs of modern subsea pumping and compression systems such as water injection, wet and dry gas compression, single phase pumping, and multiphase pumping. SpecTRON 10 is a single-phase connector system which can be mated by ROV and “Stab” tooling. Through continuous development, the SpecTRON 10 product family has provided innovative solutions for subsea pumping since 2000 as well as 10 kV DC applications in tidal renewable applications.
SpecTRON 45

SpecTRON 45 is Siemens Energy's new high-voltage connector for subsea power distribution applications. Through incorporating several innovative technologies, SpecTRON 45 provides high electrical integrity and a truly modular design. This offers flexibility in layout for a broad range of applications, including subsea power distribution, very long step outs and high current systems. The SpecTRON 45 is our first connector to feature our Common Module Interface (CMI) and Quick Connect technologies for simple, reliable site termination and improved project execution.
Instrumentation feedthrough subsea connector systems
Instrumentation feedthrough subsea connector systems are designed to convey electrical communication between permanent downhole instrumentation through the Tubing Hanger and Xmas Tree.

Siemens Energy Instrumentation feedthrough subsea connector systems is branded under ElecTRON, which is divided into two main product families: ElecTRONv and ElecTRON, respectively designed for Vertical and Horizontal Xmas Trees.
ElecTRON products have proven reliability and a solid track record, deployed on a wide range of major developments worldwide.

ElecTRON brand offers a range of connector solutions, consisting of penetrator, wetmate connectors pair and drymate connectors pair, rated up to 15,000psi working pressure; tested against the latest industry standards and specifications.

items.title: Subsea solutions
items.description: Products and solutions that ensure systems are connected and energized and that the large amount of data collected subsea is accurately and timely delivered.

body.text: At Siemens Energy's Subsea business unit have a portfolio tailored to support the industry on this journey. From a wide range of connectors and sensors to a large-scale subsea power distribution systems, we deliver the products and solutions that ensure our customers' systems are connected and energized and that the large amount of data collected subsea is accurately and timely delivered to a control room or into a cloud solution.

The end result for the customer is increased production, greater availability of systems, longer uptime and reduced CAPEX and OPEX. Our 40-year track record in serving the subsea oil and gas industry is a solid foundation for also supporting the offshore and subsea renewables industry in the coming energy transition.
Energizing and digitalizing subsea

Decarbonization, digitalization, and electrification are three major trends in the oil and gas industry. These trends will influence the way forward with regard to infrastructure, products and processes across the oil and gas market. In addition, we are seeing the emergence of offshore and subsea renewable power generation and energy production and storage.
Powering installations on the seabed
Enabling large-scale subsea processing by powering the subsea fields of the future – down to 3,000 meters.
Subsea PowerGRID
Subsea Transformer

The subsea transformer is the main interface between a subsea transmission line and a subsea power distribution system. As a hermetically sealed, fluid-filled and pressure-compensated unit the subsea transformer enables long step-outs, providing the right voltage level to a wide range of consumers, like subsea switchgear, subsea compressors and subsea pumps.
Subsea Switchgear
The subsea switchgear is the unit responsible for power distribution and protection of other units in a subsea power grid.
Subsea Variable-Speed Drive

The subsea variable speed drive (VSD) is the unit responsible for supplying power and protecting subsea motors for compressors and pumps. It uses the field proven Siemens Perfect Harmony multi-cell topology with bypass capability, which provides high levels of redundancy and reliability.
Subsea Power Control
The Subsea Power Control system is a very important component of the Subsea Power Grid. It ensures several important functions in the subsea power distribution.
Subsea PowerGRID Digital Twin

The subsea power grid components are “born digital” and equipped with sensors and high-quality data acquisition to enable full operational digital twins of the subsea power units. The data is stored in the cloud and on premise and data analytics is applied to the data to produce a hierarchy of health Key Performance Indicators (KPI's) for the subsea assets. This gives a very high level of transparency into the equipment and enables cost efficient operation and maintenance of the subsea power system.
Subsea DigiGRID
DigiGRID Connect/Control

Subsea DigiGRID is a qualified generic control, safety, and Digital Twin system(s) intended for and used to control any part in a subsea process setup. The main intention for a Subsea DigiGRID implementation is to extend the interfaces for a regular topside Safety and Automation Setup (SAS) and Digital twin system(s) to the seabed. A good example for such an application is a subsea factory setup, including, pumps, water treatment systems, separators, and electrical power distribution.
DigiGRID EDU-3

The main functionality of DigiGRID EDU-3 is to switch several identical and independent power outlets in a controlled manner, and at the same time independently monitor the quality of the power delivered to the outlets.
Products and systems

Our subsea products and systems portfolio covers a broad spectrum of applications. Going far beyond power and distribution, it comprises everything from pioneering technologies for subsea control and surveillance to exemplary service and support based on extensive marinization expertise. As a result, we are able to provide answers over the entire life of the field.

body.text: Siemens Energy high-quality subsea pressure and temperature sensors have an unrivalled performance and excellent long-term stability. For over 30 years the performance and stability of our sensors has been proven on subsea installations worldwide.

In addition to our renowned subsea pressure, temperature and differential pressure sensors, we also offer a wide assortment of proven and tested instruments for a varied range of subsea measurement applications.
WEPS sensors
WEPS-100 series

The WEPS-100 subsea sensor range, first released in 2010 has was designed to be the first commercially available modular subsea pressure and temperature sensor, allowing variants such as function and output protocol to be selected without affecting dimensional envelope size.

The WEPS-100 range is available for digital applications to 15K PSI and 180°C. With over 13,000 WEPS-100 sensors produced to date, this product has an unrivalled pedigree in relation to quality and sets the precedent for next generation sensor products.
WEPS-300 series

The WEPS-300 subsea pressure and temperature sensor is our next generation, competitive, future proofed sensor. It is production optimized, focusing on standardization, with reduced part numbers and less variants.

As with all sensors in the WEPS range it has been engineered and manufactured to the highest quality, and has advanced features allowing compliance with technical specifications. It has the qualities of accuracy, stability, reliability, and performance that Siemens Energy sensors are valued for.
Like the WEPS-100, with the WEPS-300 we offer an extended housing option for insulated applications and a dual hose exit
WEPS-900 HP/HT Subsea Pressure and Temperature sensor

The WEPS‑900 HP/HT sensor is engineered for the most demanding high‑pressure, high‑temperature applications, where reliability and accuracy are critical. Developed through extensive qualification testing, the sensor is built to perform in extreme environments and withstand the mechanical, thermal, and chemical stresses typical of advanced upstream operations. Fully compliant with relevant API standards, the WEPS‑900 offers a robust and validated solution for operators who require dependable monitoring of asset health with precision even under HP/HT extremes.
SES-1 – Subsea Erosion sensor

Building on the proven technology of the WEPS‑300 platform, Siemens Energy introduces a fully intrusive erosion‑monitoring sensor designed for high‑accuracy, real‑time detection. By directly measuring physical material loss caused by erosive flow conditions, the sensor delivers rapid response to early‑stage erosion events. This enables operators to identify changing flow regimes quickly and take timely corrective action, helping to protect critical equipment and avoid costly unplanned downtime.
WEPSiTRON – Dry mate coupler

The WEPSiTRON is a dry‑mate coupler specifically engineered for seamless integration with the WEPS‑300 and SES‑1 erosion‑monitoring sensors. Designed to be installed in the workshop, the WEPSiTRON enables full topside disconnectability, simplifying installation and maintenance activities. This approach supports split delivery of the sensor and wiring harness, improving logistics and reducing installation complexity. By eliminating the need for a traditional wet‑mate connector pair, the WEPSiTRON delivers significant cost savings while maintaining robust, reliable performance in demanding environments.

What is a high-voltage substation?
faqs.a: A high voltage substation transforms and distributes electricity, stepping up or down voltages for efficient transmission and safe distribution, and manages grid protection and control.

faqs.q: What types of substations does Siemens Energy offer?
faqs.a: They cover air-insulated (AIS), gas-insulated (GIS), hybrid, digital, offshore, mobile, and micro station designs for all voltage levels and environments.​

faqs.q: What is the main benefit of a GIS substation?
faqs.a: A GIS substation offers a compact footprint, lower maintenance, and higher safety - ideal for urban and harsh environments.​

faqs.q: Can Siemens Energy upgrade existing substations?
faqs.a: Yes, they provide modernization of aging equipment, capacity expansion, and digital retrofits without requiring full replacement.​

faqs.q: How do substations support renewable energy?
faqs.a: Modern substations enable efficient integration, control, and transfer of variable renewable sources across the grid.​

body.text: Substations are crucial for energy transmission, ensuring safe and efficient power flow from generation to consumption. As the energy landscape shifts towards renewables and grid modernization, advanced substation technologies help operators maintain grid reliability, protect infrastructure, adapt to changing demands, and integrate renewable energy with flexibility.
Substation solutions for modern power systems​

Explore Siemens Energy's specialized substation technologies designed to address every transmission and distribution challenge - from robust high voltage hubs for major grids to agile, modular solutions for rapid deployment and decentralized energy needs.

Decarbonizing the energy industry is about more than switching to renewable sources. To achieve Zero Global Warming Potential (GWP), it's essential to make the transmission of power as clean and green as its generation. This means eliminating F-gases from electrical switchgear – particularly SF6. The Siemens Energy Blue portfolio uses clean air for insulation with Zero F-gases, Zero toxicity and Zero harm to human health and the environment.

Siemens Energy offers a comprehensive portfolio of substation solutions, including AIS and GIS solutions (also SF6-free), hybrid substations, offshore substations, prefabricated power solutions, mobile substations as a service and micro substations. These solutions are designed to meet the global demand for reliable, efficient, and sustainable electric power. With extensive experience and innovation, Siemens Energy supports utilities (Transmission System Operator - TSOs) and industries (Distribution System Operator - DSOs) in building smarter, safer, and more resilient grids and achieving their decarbonization goals.

Get answers: FAQs on high voltage substations
What is a high-voltage substation?
A high voltage substation transforms and distributes electricity, stepping up or down voltages for efficient transmission and safe distribution, and manages grid protection and control.
What types of substations does Siemens Energy offer?
They cover air-insulated (AIS), gas-insulated (GIS), hybrid, digital, offshore, mobile, and micro station designs for all voltage levels and environments.​
What is the main benefit of a GIS substation?
A GIS substation offers a compact footprint, lower maintenance, and higher safety - ideal for urban and harsh environments.​
Can Siemens Energy upgrade existing substations?
Yes, they provide modernization of aging equipment, capacity expansion, and digital retrofits without requiring full replacement.​
How do substations support renewable energy?
Modern substations enable efficient integration, control, and transfer of variable renewable sources across the grid.​
What is a mobile substation used for?
Mobile substations provide fast, flexible grid support - restoring service after outages or expanding the grid during upgrades or new construction.​
Are Siemens Energy substations suitable for challenging sites?
Absolutely. Their portfolio includes systems designed for deserts, offshore wind, mountains, and remote or temporary locations.​
What services does Siemens Energy provide for substations?
They offer end-to-end solutions: engineering, project management, installation, maintenance, upgrades, digitalization, and financing.​
What's the difference between a substation and a power station?
A power station generates electricity; a substation regulates, transforms, and distributes power but does not generate it.​
How does Pretact enhance resilience?
Pretact combines modular and mobile solutions for rapid deployment and recovery, ensuring grid continuity even during emergencies.​

items.h1: Surge arrester solutions, products and services
items.description: Discover our medium- and high-voltage surge arresters designed for safe and reliable protection of electrical equipment.

faqs.q: What is a surge arrester?
faqs.a: A lightning strike or an electrical surge can cause several irreversible damage to electrical devices, when this lightning strike or electrical surge is above the certain insulation level of devices. The main task of a surge arrester is to limit the overvoltage and protect the valuable equipment. With the help and the correct implementation of surge arresters, lightning strikes and surges cannot damage the system or device.

faqs.q: How does a surge arrester work?
faqs.a: A surge arrester diverts lighting and switching surges by metal oxide varistors inside its housing. Metal oxide varistors (MOVs) are no-linear semiconductors. MOVs work as an insulator at normal voltages and the current cannot pass through it. MOVs start acting as a resistive conductor, while overvoltages occur. The overvoltages will be diverted to the ground.

faqs.q: What are the main types of surge arresters and their applications?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy has been designing and manufacturing different construction types of medium- and high-voltage surge arresters for standard and special applications. Valuable equipment, such as transformers, circuit breakers, generators, motors, capacitors, traction vehicles, bushings and complete switchgear, is ideally protected against overvoltages.

faqs.q: How often should surge arresters be tested and maintained?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy surge arresters are maintenance free and there are no serviceable parts in it. Visual examinations regarding outer damages or extreme pollutions may be carried out at regular intervals. If there is any monitoring device installed the specific rules of the system/device apply.

faqs.q: What are the common signs that a surge arrester needs replacement?
faqs.a: The failure rate of our high voltage surge arresters is estimated to be far lower as 0.1% per year, which corresponds to a mean time between failure (MTBF) of more than 1000 years. More specific figures cannot be given, since the total number of reported arrester failures by our customers is by far too low to perform statistic calculations with sufficient accuracy. The reported and investigated arrester failures were mainly caused by exceeding the electrical specification (e.g. by direct lightning stroke, voltage transfer) or loss of tightness by external stresses (e.g. by transport damage). Consequently, the inherent failure rate of Siemens high voltage surge arresters is virtually zero and can be neglected. Based on service experience as well as inspections and test on surge arresters taken back from service, the life expectancy of our high voltage surge arresters is considered to be at least 40 years.

faqs.q: What types of equipment can Siemens Energy surge arresters protect?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy surge arresters can ideally protect valuable equipment against overvoltages, such as transformers, circuit breakers, generators, motors, capacitors, traction vehicles, bushings and complete switchgear.

faqs.q: Since when has Siemens Energy been manufacturing surge arresters?
faqs.a: In 1925, an exciting journey began at Schaltwerk Berlin: the development of the first surge arrester (cathode arrester) - the beginning of arrester manufacturing at Siemens Energy. Today, 100 years later, our surge arresters are an indispensable core element for a safe and sustainable energy supply worldwide. We are the market leader - and with good reason: quality, innovation and decades of experience.

body.text: Surge arresters are essential in safeguarding valuable electrical equipment from overvoltage incidents, such as those caused by lightning strikes, switching operations, or other transient events. By effectively diverting surge currents, these devices protect transformers, circuit breakers, generators, motors, capacitors, traction vehicles, bushings, and complete switchgear installations from potential damage.

Siemens Energy surge arresters stand out for their superior quality, extended service life, and reliability across diverse operating conditions worldwide. The arrester products not only adhere to international standards but also undergo rigorous certified quality management processes, ensuring optimal safety and performance.
Why choose Siemens Energy surge arresters?
Since 1925, Siemens Energy has been a leader in designing and manufacturing medium- and high-voltage surge arresters for a broad spectrum of standard and specialized applications.
Proven expertise
Nearly a century of experience in surge arrester technology and continuous innovation.
Comprehensive product range
Solutions for medium voltage (MV), high voltage (HV), railway applications, line protection, and station equipment.
Reliability & durability
Engineered for easy installation, minimal maintenance, and prolonged operational life.
Global support
Personalized advice and assistance from Siemens Energy experts worldwide.
Explore the surge arrester products and solutions
To meet the diverse needs of its customers, Siemens Energy offers specialized surge arrester products, each designed for specific applications and environments.
Heavy-duty arresters are designed for high voltage substations, ensuring the protection of critical assets.
Efficient and compact arresters designed for medium voltage networks and equipment.
Surge arresters optimized for overhead lines and distribution networks to protect infrastructure from transient overvoltage.
Robust protection solutions tailored for railway electrification systems, ensuring safe and uninterrupted operations.
How does a surge arrester work?

Surge arresters operate by diverting excess voltage away from sensitive electrical equipment during transient overvoltage events. They use nonlinear resistive elements that remain inactive during normal operation but become highly conductive when voltage surges occur, safely channeling the surge current to the ground.
This protective action prevents insulation breakdown, equipment damage, and service interruptions, thereby enhancing system reliability and reducing maintenance costs.

All Siemens Energy surge arresters are subject to certified quality management and comply with international standards. They are absolutely reliable and characterized by easy installation, low maintenance costs, and an extremely long operating life.
Benefits of Siemens Energy surge arresters
Siemens Energy surge arresters offer numerous advantages, including:

items: Certified quality and compliance: all products meet international standards and undergo stringent quality assurance.
Easy installation and maintenance: designed for straightforward integration and minimal upkeep.
Long operating life: engineered to withstand harsh environmental conditions and electrical stresses.
Cost efficiency: reduces downtime and repair expenses by preventing surge-related failures.
Customized solutions: tailored designs for unique applications and special requirements.

faqs.q: What is a surge arrester?
faqs.a: A lightning strike or an electrical surge can cause several irreversible damage to electrical devices, when this lightning strike or electrical surge is above the certain insulation level of devices. The main task of a surge arrester is to limit the overvoltage and protect the valuable equipment. With the help and the correct implementation of surge arresters, lightning strikes and surges cannot damage the system or device.

faqs.q: How does a surge arrester work?
faqs.a: A surge arrester diverts lighting and switching surges by metal oxide varistors inside its housing. MOVs (metal oxide varistors) are no-linear semiconductors. MOVs work as an insulator at normal voltages and the current cannot pass through it. MOVs start acting as a resistive conductor, while overvoltages occur. The overvoltages will be diverted to the ground.

faqs.q: What is the purpose of a surge arrester?
faqs.a: Line surge arresters (LSA) are designed to prevent ground faults and short circuits in power lines caused by lightning or switching overvoltages. Insulator flashovers, voltage dips and interruptions are prevented by eliminating all lightning and switching overvoltages above the insulator insulation level.

faqs.q: Where should surge arresters typically be installed?
faqs.a: The line surge arresters are installed at recommended locations along the line in accordance with the line simulation, and ensures anhanced overvoltage protection. Selecting the optimum line surge arresters, especially in terms of their quantity and installation locations, significantly improves the reliability of the overall line system and the quality of power that it supplies.

faqs.q: What are line surge arresters and what do they protect against?
faqs.a: Line Surge Arresters (LSAs) are increasingly used to improve the service security of transmission lines and therefore the system stability in cases where the following problems are present: • High ceraunic level (high ground flash density). • Poor earthing conditions of towers. • High switching surges on EHV lines. • Danger of double flashovers (shorts between 2 systems). A cost effective line upgrade is possible without substitution of insulators and without adding shield wires.

faqs.q: Up to what system voltage can Siemens Energy line surge arresters be used?
faqs.a: Siemens Energy offer line surge arresters for system voltages up to 800 kV and an energy discharge capability of 3.6 C.

faqs.q: How does the line surge arrester operate during a lightning event?
faqs.a: Externally Gapped Line Arrester (EGLA) operates above a defined minimum lightning impulse value, but this value is below the flashover (Critical Impulse Flashover) of the insulators. Overvoltage below this level will not lead to any flashover along the line, i.e. they are not relevant. None Gapped Line Arrester (NGLA) operates permanently for all kinds of overvoltage (lightning impuls &switching impuls). If the line is equipped with sufficient LSA (EGLA/NGLA) based on line-study results, it can become foolproof system against all flashover failures.

body.text: Transmission line surge arresters (LSAs) are essential components in modern power systems, designed to protect overhead transmission lines from the damaging effects of lightning strikes and switching surges. Siemens Energy offers a comprehensive range of surge arresters that ensure the reliability, safety, and efficiency of electrical grids worldwide.
Overview of transmission line surge arresters

Transmission line surge arresters are installed on power transmission lines to limit overvoltages caused by lightning or switching operations. By safely diverting excessive surge energy to the ground, these devices prevent flashovers, equipment damage, and power outages.
Key functions:

items: High voltage capability: designed for system voltages up to 800 kV with an energy discharge capacity of 3.6 C.

Lightning protection: externally gapped spark gap flashes over during lightning events, limiting ground fault currents from several kiloamperes to just a few amperes, extinguishing arcs within 10 milliseconds, and avoiding circuit breaker operation.
Enhanced system reliability: Siemens Energy proprietary simulation software, based on Cigré studies, optimizes LSA placement and quantity, ensuring robust lightning protection while minimizing costs.

Reduced power interruptions: LSAs eliminate overvoltages above the insulator's lightning-impulse withstand level (LIWL), preventing insulator flashovers and voltage dips, thereby improving power quality and reducing outages.
Advanced simulation and support: detailed software analysis models customer-specific line conditions, enabling precise LSA selection and placement for maximum effectiveness.

body.text: Siemens Energy transmission line surge arrester portfolio
Siemens Energy offers both medium- and high-voltage surge arresters for transmission lines, covering voltages up to 800 kV and even higher for station applications.
Our portfolio includes:
Non-Gapped Line Arrester (NGLA) – Direct connection to overhead lines

Non-gapped line surge arresters (NGLA) provide exceptional mounting flexibility and high operational reliability. Depending on tower design and insulator arrangements, NGLAs can be installed directly on insulators, conductors, or tower structures. They effectively limit overvoltages to levels below the insulator's withstand voltage, preventing flashovers and equipment damage.
Key benefits:

items: Highly flexible installation: suitable for mounting on conductor, tower, or insulator, adapting to various line configurations.
Superior protection: high energy absorption capacity ensures robust defense against lightning and switching overvoltages.
Thermal overload safety: integrated disconnector isolates the arrester during thermal overload, allowing continued line operation until replacement.
Standards compliance: designed and tested according to the latest IEC 60099-4 standard for surge arresters.

body.text: Externally Gapped Line Arrester (EGLA) – Insulated by series spark gap

Siemens Energy EGLA surge arresters feature an external spark gap in series, which galvanically isolates the arrester's active components from the line voltage under normal conditions. Upon lightning strike, the spark gap flashes over, limiting ground fault current from kiloamperes to amperes and extinguishing the arc within 10 ms. This rapid arc quenching prevents circuit breaker trips and eliminates reclosing operations.

items: Zero leakage current: the series gap disconnects the metal-oxide varistor (MOV) blocks from system voltage during normal operation.
Material efficiency: lower rated voltage arrester required, reducing MOV quantity and overall material use.
No disconnector or ground lead needed: simplifies installation and maintenance.
Compact design: ideal for multiple-circuit towers with short clearances; enables live-line installation.
Complete solutions: available with polymer insulators for enhanced performance.
Standards compliance: conforms to the latest IEC 60099-8 standard for externally gapped surge arresters.

body.text: Optimized software analysis for transmission line surge arrester applications

Siemens Energy offers software analysis (simulation) based on Cigré studies to examine and conduct preliminary tests of customer-specific applications as a way of determining the optimal, cost-effective solution. With this approach, the customer only needs to equip particular phases or individual line segments with line surge arresters, and can still ensure sufficient lightning protection of the overhead line.

In the first phase of an analysis, all important parameters of the transmission line under study are entered into the simulation software, and the installations to be examined are selected. This approach takes the following factors into consideration:

items: Line parameters: operating voltage, number of three-phase circuits, ground wire data, length, span length and sag on line, conductor type, diameter, and clearances
Tower data: tower surge impedances and footing resistance, tower geometry (position and distances of the individual phases and any existing ground wires)
Insulator data: arcing distance, connection length, rated lightning impulse withstand voltage
Lightning activity: keraunic level (lightning strokes per year and km²), network topology (elevation profile)
Customer priorities: fewer short interruptions, prevention of phase and multisystem short-circuits, elimination of ground wires

faqs.q: What are the common signs that a surge arrester needs replacement?
faqs.a: The failure rate of our high voltage surge arresters is estimated to be far lower as 0.1% per year, which corresponds to a mean time between failure (MTBF) of more than 1000 years. More specific figures cannot be given, since the total number of reported arrester failures by our customers is by far too low to perform statistic calculations with sufficient accuracy. The reported and investigated arrester failures were mainly caused by exceeding the electrical specification (e.g. by direct lightning stroke, voltage transfer) or loss of tightness by external stresses (e.g. by transport damage). Consequently, the inherent failure rate of Siemens high voltage surge arresters is virtually zero and can be neglected. Get answers: FAQs on medium-voltage surge arresters
What is a surge arrester?

A lightning strike or an electrical surge can cause several irreversible damage to electrical devices, when this lightning strike or electrical surge is above the certain insulation level of devices. The main task of a surge arrester is to limit the overvoltage and protect the valuable equipment. With the help and the correct implementation of surge arresters, lightning strikes and surges cannot damage the system or device.
How does a surge arrester work?

A surge arrester diverts lighting and switching surges by metal oxide varistors inside its housing. Metal oxide varistors (MOVs) are no-linear semiconductors. MOVs work as an insulator at normal voltages and the current cannot pass through it. MOVs start acting as a resistive conductor, while overvoltages occur. The overvoltages will be diverted to the ground.
What is the purpose of a surge arrester?

Surge arresters are designed to prevent ground faults and short circuits in power lines caused by lightning or switching overvoltages. Insulator flashovers, voltage dips and interruptions are prevented by eliminating all lightning and switching overvoltages above the insulator insulation level.
How often should surge arresters be tested and maintained?

Siemens Energy surge arresters are maintenance free and there are no serviceable parts in it. Visual examinations regarding outer damages or extreme pollutions may be carried out at regular intervals. If there is any monitoring device installed the specific rules of the system/device apply.
What are the common signs that a surge arrester needs replacement?

The failure rate of our high voltage surge arresters is estimated to be far lower as 0.1% per year, which corresponds to a mean time between failure (MTBF) of more than 1000 years. More specific figures cannot be given, since the total number of reported arrester failures by our customers is by far too low to perform statistic calculations with sufficient accuracy.

The reported and investigated arrester failures were mainly caused by exceeding the electrical specification (e.g. by direct lightning stroke, voltage transfer) or loss of tightness by external stresses (e.g. by transport damage). Consequently, the inherent failure rate of Siemens high voltage surge arresters is virtually zero and can be neglected.
Based on service experience as well as inspections and test on surge arresters taken back from service, the life expectancy of our high voltage surge arresters is considered to be at least 40 years.
What types of equipment can Siemens Energy surge arresters protect?

Siemens Energy surge arresters can ideally protect valuable equipment against overvoltages, such as transformers, circuit breakers, generators, motors, capacitors, traction vehicles, bushings and complete switchgear.
Since when has Siemens Energy been manufacturing surge arresters?

In 1925, an exciting journey began at Schaltwerk Berlin: the development of the first surge arrester (cathode arrester) - the beginning of arrester manufacturing at Siemens Energy. Today, 100 years later, our surge arresters are an indispensable core element for a safe and sustainable energy supply worldwide. We are the market leader - and with good reason: quality, innovation and decades of experience.
What materials are used for arrester housings?
Porcelain and polymer are common; polymer offers better resistance to pollution and lighter weight, while porcelain provides mechanical robustness.
How do surge arresters handle lightning impulses?
They absorb and divert the high-energy lightning surge currents, withstanding impulse voltages up to hundreds of kV peak.
How do polymer surge arresters compare to porcelain types?
Polymer arresters are lighter, have better pollution resistance, and lower risk of shattering, making them suitable for polluted or coastal areas.

items.title: Gas-Insulated Switchgear (DC-GIS)
items.description: The gas-insulated switchgear from Siemens Energy (DC-GIS) saves space, time & money, enabling numerous applications in the HVDC transmission.

body.text: Space limitations are an issue with numerous new applications for HVDC transmission. That's why Siemens Energy has broken new ground in insulation technology to make one of the most space-saving technologies in HV power transmission available for HVDC systems: gas-insulated switchgear (GIS).

Siemens Energy DC GIS are based on Siemens Energy's proven 8DQ1 switchgear technology. The encapsulated, compact, and modular gas-insulated switchgear for DC voltages of up to ±550 kV and currents of up to 5 kA reduce space requirements for HVDC switchyards considerably, boast outstanding climatic resistance. Furthermore, a gas-insulated substation can even be installed underground or commissioned in prefabricated container modules for further space and time savings as well as minimum visual impact.
Get maximum performance at minimum space.
bold: Get maximum performance at minimum space.

body.text: DC GIS is your answer to any size, climate, and time challenge

Modular Siemens Energy DC GIS help reduce the space requirements for HVDC systems, ensure safe and reliable operation even in demanding onshore and offshore applications, and enable quick project implementation.
Enormous space-savings in offshore applications

The use of Siemens Energy DC GIS reduces the size of an offshore HVDC converter platform by up to 10 percent, because space requirements for the switchgear itself are reduced by up to 95 %: While comparable air-insulated switchgear in standard configuration would require 4,000 cubic meters, Siemens Energy DC GIS require only 200 cubic meters.
A gas-insulated substation doesn't require a dedicated room. It can simply be added to another technology room on the platform, such as the converter or reactor room. This helps bring down costs.

Siemens Energy DC GIS are suitable for today's most demanding offshore applications. Type-tested according to applicable IEC standards and CIGRÉ recommendations, gas-insulated switchgears for DC are available for rated voltages of up to ±550 kV.
Less space consumption and visual impact onshore

Thanks to their outstandingly compact dimensions, Siemens Energy DC GIS make it much easier to build a switchyard exactly where it is required when space is limited. At the same time, they help curtail costs when land prices are at a premium. Siemens Energy GIS operate safely and reliably even under severe climatic conditions, which means that a gas-insulated substation doesn't require an extra housing in most cases. The comprehensive range of standardized modules available helps implement even complex arrangements and switchyard layouts without much interface engineering, while commissioning of the GIS switchgear is fast and cost-efficient.
Small footprint and reliable operation for transition stations

Siemens Energy DC GIS reduce space requirements for the switchyard of transition stations to a minimum: The modular, encapsulated, and compact Siemens Energy DC GIS for rated voltages of up to ±550 kV require remarkably less space than technically equivalent air-insulated switchgear – this way bringing down land costs and reducing the visual impact of the switchyard.

In most cases, Siemens Energy DC GIS can be installed in open air without a housing: They operate safely and reliably even under severe climatic conditions. This speeds up commissioning and helps keep costs at bay.
Thanks to the comprehensive range of standardized modules, even complex arrangements and switchyard layouts can be implemented with very little interface.
Transition stations with hidden switchgear
Siemens Energy DC GIS can be installed underground. This helps keep the visual impact of a transition station to an absolute minimum and reliably prevents unauthorized access.

Numerous standardized modules are available to enable the flexible implementation even of complex arrangements with next to no interface engineering for the connection of other equipment, such as control and protection devices.

Siemens Energy DC GIS are type-tested according to applicable IEC standards and CIGRE recommendations and are available for rated voltages of up to ±550 kV. This makes them suited for many new HVDC applications, such as multi-terminal or DC grid systems.
Containerized solutions for extra-fast commissioning

Siemens Energy DC GIS for rated voltages of up to ±550 kV can be delivered prefabricated and pretested in modular containers – a cost-effective solution whenever technical requirements such as extreme environmental conditions require DC GIS to be placed in a housing and when time is at a premium.
The entire substation arrangement is tested at the manufacturer's and the container builder's premises for the quickest possible commissioning and smooth, cost-effective interaction with civil works.
DC GIS layouts that are repeatedly needed, as is the case with transition stations within an HVDC scheme, for example, can be planned and supplied as a cost-effective, standardized series.
From cable to GIL with the least possible effort

Gas-insulated lines (GIL) can be used in HVDC transmission systems. In certain cases, for example, when restrictions due to natural barriers or existing infrastructure must be crossed with challenging routing and minimal use of space.

In such cases, a preassembled and pretested, containerized transition solution based on Siemens Energy DC GIS for rated voltages of up to ±550 kV is the most space-saving, quick, and cost-efficient solution. It also helps reduce space requirements, engineering effort, and visual impact.
Space-savings of up to 95 %
Compared with technically equivalent air-insulated switchgear, DC GIS require up to 95 percent less space.
Outstanding climatic resistance
DC GIS operate safely and reliably onshore and offshore in the temperature range of -30°C to + 50°C and even under severe conditions such as polluted and aggressive atmosphere.
Containerized arrangements available
DC GIS can be commissioned in prefabricated container modules to reduce environmental impact as well as local erection and commissioning efforts.
Underground installation possible
The encapsulated, compact, and modular DC GIS can be installed underground to prevent visibility of and public access to the gas-insulated substation.
Trendsetting technology put into practice
Siemens Energy DC GIS is a fairly new technology, but thanks to its great advantages it has already been included in the design of future HVDC projects that are being planned at the moment.

items.title: LIFE Blue GIS 420 kV - high-voltage and SF6-free
items.h1: LIFE Blue GIS 420 kV - high-voltage and SF6-free
items.description: Discover the LIFE Blue 420 kV GIS project — pioneering SF6-free, clean air insulated high-voltage switchgear for a climate-neutral power future.

body.text: Project objective

Almost all high-voltage circuit breakers (CB) and gas insulated switchgear (GIS) installed over the last fifty years have used SF6 gas for insulation. This is the most potent greenhouse gas currently known, with a global warming potential (GWP) of 24,300. While mature alternatives to SF6 are available for medium voltage applications, until now there are no commercially available climate-neutral alternatives with comparable performance at the 420 kV level.

In the course of this project, the EU LIFE program is funding the further development of the Blue 420 kV GIS as part of its commitment to climate neutrality, to the reduction of GHGs, and to the promotion of green technologies. The EU's support for this project aligns with its Green Deal objectives and its strategy to decarbonize the energy sector. The project also contributes to the EU's F-gas regulation and climate neutrality targets for 2050.
Project steps

The LIFE Blue 420 kV GIS project will demonstrate for the first time the economic viability of a climate-friendly and completely F-gas free 420 kV GIS which combines clean air insulation and vacuum switching technology with a digital low power instrument transformer (LPIT). This Blue GIS will replace an existing indoor GIS at TSO Elia in Vilvoorde, Belgium. The clean air set to be used instead of SF6 consists of nitrogen and oxygen and has a GWP of zero.

In collaboration with the EU's LIFE program, Siemens Energy and ELIA entered a partnership in October 2024, which is scheduled to continue until September 2028. Over the course of those four years, both parties will conduct.
Development and testing of the LPIT solution for Blue 420 kV GIS
Type testing of the CB (including LPIT)
Pilot installation of 1 GIS bay in the ELIA substation (including engineering, manufacturing, instrumentation and control)
Operation at ELIA substation for 1 year (+5 years) including monitoring, evaluation and technical assessment
Technical potential

Besides significant savings of greenhouse gases through being emission-free, any PFAS input is avoided – which is not the case with other alternatives to SF6. In addition, the project will deliver the world's first 420 kV LPIT with cast resin embedded sensors and clean air insulation, replacing conventional current and voltage transformers.

The LPIT will offer new digital possibilities in current and voltage metering and additional functions such as power quality measurement and will help to significantly reduce the size and copper cabling of SF6-free GIS solutions.
Wider project impact

270 replications of the project throughout Europe and worldwide are planned by 2032, for both existing GIS installations (as replacements) and for new substations. The project is part of the Siemens Energy roadmap and will serve as a blueprint for technology transfer, e.g. to even higher voltage levels.
Project funding

Created in 1992, the LIFE program is the EU's funding vehicle for the environment and climate action. To date it has co-financed more than 6,000 projects helping Europe to become greener, and since 2021 it has included the Clean Energy Transition sub-program. As part of the LIFE program, the EU contributes just over 4.1m euros as part of an overall budget of over 6 million euros.
Belgium is looking forward to LIFE Blue

Watch the steps of a pioneering high‑voltage grid project in Europe where an F‑gas‑free (SF6‑free) vacuum interrupter switchgear is being installed at the 420 kV transmission level for the first time.
The power of partnership

Collaboration is key in all of our projects. Here we work closely with the EU Programme for the Environment and Climate Action (LIFE) and Elia, operator of the electricity transmission network in Belgium. This joint project began on 1 October 2024, and is scheduled to continue until 30 September 2028.

The LIFE Programme is the EU's funding instrument for the environment and climate action. It began in 1992 and has co-financed thousands of projects in the field of environmental protection driving fundamental change in the environment and people's lives, with over 6,000 projects making a difference at the local level.

Siemens Energy AG, a global leader in energy technology, drives the energy transition with innovative solutions covering almost the entire energy value chain. Operating in over 90 countries with 100,000 employees, an estimated one-sixth of the electricity generated worldwide is based on Siemens Energy technology.

Elia Transmission Belgium operates the electricity transmission network in Belgium. They manage the Belgian high-voltage transmission grid (30 kV to 400 kV), which comprises over 8,903 km of overhead lines and underground cables. They preserve a service reliability level of 99.99 % and ensure that production and consumption are balanced around the clock.
News & Media
Enlit Europe November 2025

Warm greetings from vibrant Bilbao at Enlit Europe! It's been an amazing experience to be part of the EU Projects Zone, where we proudly presented our ambitious EU co-funded projects to phase out SF₆ at the 420 kV level.
Switchgear Magazine explores Blue

Read the interview with Ulf Katschinski and discover latest innovations on SF6-free vacuum-based technologies, learn about their readiness for large-scale deployment and how the EU Commission is supporting it.
kick-off to clean air

On 2nd October we were happy to kick-off the project together with our consortium members from Elia Group from Belgium. We are proud of this strong partnership and are looking forward to gain and share operational experience on the next level of Blue switchgear with Zero emissions.

Our latest, innovative dry-type transformer, CAREPOLE was selected for 2022 EUISSCA Sustainable Supply Chain Award! CAREPOLE is an eco-friendly alternative for safer and more reliable distribution grids.
Our environmentally friendly CAREPOLE is setting new standards
Are you in need of a reliable, digital (Sensformer), eco-friendly and durable cast-resin transformer? We have an answer for you: CAREPOLE.

body.text: CAREPOLE was developed by Siemens Energy for your overhead distribution line networks. CAREPOLE answers the challenges which transformers can possibly meet. Its windings are sealed with cast resin under vacuum, separated from the core, and the insulation is solid and resist the dielectric loads in the distribution network. The cast resin also protects your unit against severe weather conditions. High- and low-voltage bushings are cast in one piece with the windings. This technical design makes CAREPOLE especially reliable and unsusceptible to failures. Do you need an off-load tap changer? We can provide one near one of the top high-voltage bushings. It is set via a patented tap panel when the transformer is de-energized.
Weatherproof design

Your CAREPOLE withstands any weather conditions and ensures a reliable operation. The winding surfaces and core are in direct contact with the ambient air, resulting in efficient natural heat exchange. The frame surrounding the core creates a solid mechanical structure that protects the unit against corrosion and direct sunlight. The frame also serves as a lifting and fastening mechanism for the transformer. A special manufacturing process and advanced sealing compound ensure lownoise operation and perfect contact between frame and core. The core is wound from highquality electrical steel. The solid insulation of CAREPOLE is stable under all weather conditions and prevents moisture from penetrating the windings and core.
Overload and short circuit capability

CAREPOLE can withstand higher temperatures than liquid-filled transformers, due to the solid insulation. Accordingly, CAREPOLE units can be overloaded for longer periods of peak demand and can better withstand short-circuit effects.

One key factor of the energy market is sustainability. CAREPOLE makes power distribution grids safer and more environmentally friendly because it operates without flammable mineral oil-based insulating fluids. The cast resin used as insulation and for the body of the transformer has excellent electrical and mechanical properties, and is environmentally friendly and self­extinguishing. CAREPOLE does not pose any risk to water sources or nature reserves caused by oil leaks, tank explosions, soil contamination or fires in the event of a fault. Besides, CAREPOLE does not lose any fuel in the case of an external fire. These features can reduce the costs of liability insurance. They also increase the reliability of the distribution grid.

CAREPOLE can be ordered with ready-to-use sensors, allowing you to perform your own monitoring. The connectivity system securely transmits operational data to an advanced analytics and visualization platform, providing you real-time insights into asset health and fleet status. With these digital features, potential failures can be quickly identified and addressed. You may even be able to prevent issues by detecting operational irregularities at an early stage. This transparency provided by CAREPOLE increases the reliability of your distribution grid, enabling smarter and more efficient operation.
Maintenance-free

CAREPOLE is very efficient in operation, and power loss is reduced to an absolute minimum. CAREPOLE is nearly maintenance- free, so your maintenance costs are negligible. Service activities are limited to checking the installation, vegetation conditions and wildlife management. The unit has a service life of 30+ years. There is no need to replace or change it during this time.
Easy to install

You can directly replace liquidfilled overhead distribution transformers by CAREPOLE units of identical electrical power. They have identical fixing mechanisms to the pole and have been specifically developed for urban, rural or coastal outdoor installation. Installation and grid connection are particularly simple. Since CAREPOLE is a solid unit, it can be mounted at almost any angle on the pole and energized immediately after installation.
Ratings

You can order CAREPOLE in the single-phase power range from 25 kVA to 50 kVA. It offers a maximum voltage capacity of 25 kV and can be equipped with a tap changer (± 2 x 2.5%), one or two high voltage bushings, and other accessories typical for overhead distribution transformers (e.g. surge arresters, wildlife protector).

items.title: Fluid-immersed distribution transformers
items.description: Compact, reliable and highly efficient power transformation. Available with fully bio-degradable ester insulating oil for enhanced operation at high temperatures.

faqs.q: The core
faqs.a: The iron core forms the central element of every transformer. High-grade, cold-rolled – and, depending on requirements laser-treated – metal sheets are precision-cut using computer-controlled machines to ensure compliance with even the smallest tolerances. The individual sheets are then assembled into cores using the step-lap technique or, in the case of transformers with a lower power rating, using precise winding technology. In this way, Siemens Energy's fluid-immersed distribution transformers achieve an especially good flux distribution at the joints, resulting in exceptionally low losses and minimal no-load noise.

faqs.q: Windings
faqs.a: Transformer windings are subject to extremely high electrical and mechanical stresses and must therefore be protected. The transformer windings of Siemens Energy distribution transformers are made of copper or aluminum. Low-voltage windings are made from strip or flat wire, and high-voltage windings are manufactured from round or profile wire. The use of insulating paper partially coated with epoxy resin (diamond-dotted paper) bonds the winding into a compact block during the drying process and additionally increases the short-circuit capacity.

faqs.q: Insulating liquids
faqs.a: The layer insulation is adapted to the alternating voltage strain that occurs in daily operation. Large-scale oil channels are provided to ensure sufficient cooling of the windings and to avoid hot spots. All leads are short-circuit-proof and surge-proof, contributing to the high reliability of the Siemens Energy transformer – and to an above-average service life.

faqs.q: Tank and cooling
faqs.a: Whether during transport or operation, the tank must remain sealed tight under mechanical stress and regardless of wind or weather. Corrosion protection is especially important. The surface is sandblasted and then multicoated. Upon request, hot-dip galvanization can provide even better protection. The distribution transformer’s tank must dissipate the entire heat loss. In hermetically sealed transformers, the corrugated walls absorb the changes in the insulation liquid’s volume. Alternatively, the transformer can be designed as an open system or fitted with an oil conservator that compensates for the additional volume. Some regions also use smooth-walled tanks and built-in radiators. Hermetically sealed units sometimes have an air or gas cushion to compensate for oil expansion. The sheet-steel lid is bolted – or, upon request, welded – to the tank. The steel thickness and the bracing are dimensioned to ensure that the lid withstands all necessary stress.

faqs.q: What is a fluid-immersed distribution transformer?
faqs.a: A fluid-immersed distribution transformer is an oil- or ester-filled transformer that converts higher medium-voltage levels down to lower voltages, typically up to 36 kV on the primary side and 250–800 V on the secondary side, while maintaining the same frequency.

faqs.q: What is the difference between dry type transformer and oil immersed transformer?
faqs.a: A dry-type transformer uses solid insulation and air for cooling, with no insulating liquid, making it suitable for indoor or fire-sensitive locations, whereas an oil-immersed transformer uses a sealed tank filled with insulating liquid that cools and insulates the active parts, enabling higher power density and excellent overload and thermal performance, especially in outdoor or utility applications.

faqs.q: How do liquid-filled transformers work?
faqs.a: Liquid-filled transformers operate on the principle of electromagnetic induction: an alternating current in the primary winding creates a magnetic field in the core that induces a voltage in the secondary winding, while the surrounding insulating liquid transfers heat away from the windings and core and maintains dielectric strength to ensure safe, continuous operation.

faqs.q: What is the process of oil filling in transformer?
faqs.a: For modern power and distribution transformers, oil filling typically involves first creating a deep vacuum in the tank to remove air and moisture from the insulation, then slowly filling the transformer with pretreated insulating oil—often through the bottom connection—to avoid air pockets, followed by deaeration, level adjustment, and final checks to ensure proper insulation, cooling, and leak-tightness.

faqs.q: Where are Siemens Energy fluid-immersed distribution transformers used?
faqs.a: They are used in utilities, industry, infrastructure, data centers, wind farms, and solar parks, serving as the final step before power reaches consumers or as the first step when feeding decentralized generation into the grid.

faqs.q: How do Siemens Energy oil-immersed transformers achieve high reliability and long service life?
faqs.a: High-grade core materials, robust winding designs, optimized cooling channels, advanced drying processes, and stringent testing (including short-circuit, vibration, and heat-run tests) contribute to low losses, mechanical strength, and long-term reliability.

faqs.q: Which fluids are available for filling transformers and why are they important?
faqs.a: Fluid filled transformers can use conventional mineral oil or biodegradable ester insulating liquids; ester fluids support operation at higher temperatures and improve environmental performance, especially in sensitive locations.

faqs.q: How does Siemens Energy ensure compliance with regulations and standards?
faqs.a: All fluid-immersed distribution transformers are tested according to international standards, and Siemens Energy monitors and complies with regulations like the European Eco Design Directive and US DOE rules, adapting designs as requirements evolve.

body.text: Distribution transformers can be both the last step in the conversion chain that bring electrical energy to the consumer as well as the first transformation step to feed decentrally-generated power into the power grid.

Distribution transformers by Siemens Energy are designed for superior reliability, efficiency and environmental performance. A modular architecture paired with design options ensure cost efficiency and easy minimal maintenance.
Fluid-immersed distribution transformers for optimal efficiency

items: Technology and design
Testing

body.text: The transformer's core-and-coil assembly consists of the core, windings, and connecting cables. High-quality drying and quick filling with insulation oil play a key role in extending the transformer's service life. Siemens Energy employs the latest techniques. For example, in vacuum low-frequency plants (LFH – low-frequency heating), the process of drying the solid insulation is combined with vacuum drying of the windings through low-frequency heating. The active part is heated by applying low-frequency current (< 1 Hz) to the high-voltage windings with the low-voltage windings short-circuited. While still in the plant, transformers are filled with preheated insulation liquid which is absorbed by the insulation material, thus preventing the intake of oxygen.
The core

The iron core forms the central element of every transformer. High-grade, cold-rolled – and, depending on requirements laser-treated – metal sheets are precision-cut using computer-controlled machines to ensure compliance with even the smallest tolerances. The individual sheets are then assembled into cores using the step-lap technique or, in the case of transformers with a lower power rating, using precise winding technology. In this way, Siemens Energy's fluid-immersed distribution transformers achieve an especially good flux distribution at the joints, resulting in exceptionally low losses and minimal no-load noise.
Windings

Transformer windings are subject to extremely high electrical and mechanical stresses and must therefore be protected. The transformer windings of Siemens Energy distribution transformers are made of copper or aluminum. Low-voltage windings are made from strip or flat wire, and high-voltage windings are manufactured from round or profile wire. The use of insulating paper partially coated with epoxy resin (diamond-dotted paper) bonds the winding into a compact block during the drying process and additionally increases the short-circuit capacity.
Insulating liquids

The layer insulation is adapted to the alternating voltage strain that occurs in daily operation. Large-scale oil channels are provided to ensure sufficient cooling of the windings and to avoid hot spots. All leads are short-circuit-proof and surge-proof, contributing to the high reliability of the Siemens Energy transformer – and to an above-average service life.
Tank and cooling

Whether during transport or operation, the tank must remain sealed tight under mechanical stress and regardless of wind or weather. Corrosion protection is especially important. The surface is sandblasted and then multicoated. Upon request, hot-dip galvanization can provide even better protection.

The distribution transformer's tank must dissipate the entire heat loss. In hermetically sealed transformers, the corrugated walls absorb the changes in the insulation liquid's volume. Alternatively, the transformer can be designed as an open system or fitted with an oil conservator that compensates for the additional volume.

Some regions also use smooth-walled tanks and built-in radiators. Hermetically sealed units sometimes have an air or gas cushion to compensate for oil expansion. The sheet-steel lid is bolted – or, upon request, welded – to the tank. The steel thickness and the bracing are dimensioned to ensure that the lid withstands all necessary stress.

Transformers of Siemens Energy are dispatched to the customer only after successfully passing the final inspection and testing. Each Siemens Energy transformer factory has a high-voltage test bay, where specialists conduct a wide range of tests, from voltage tests and temperature-rise tests, to special tests for insulation resistance, partial discharge measurement, harmonics, and noise level. Short-circuit, vibration and othe special tests are performed in internationally recognized and approved institutes. Siemens Energy tests in accordance with the applicable standards and provides our customers with additional certificates on request.

body.text: Standard and large fluid-immersed transformers

Standard fluid-immersed transformers are crucial elements of suburban areas, forming the link between the electrical grid and consumers. Ratings for medium-sized fluid-immersed transformers stand between 2,500 kVA and 6,300kVA. They offer a maximum voltage capacity of 36kV.

Large distribution transformers come with higher voltage capacity and power level than medium-sized fluid-immersed transformers. The technology differs to ensure the transformer will function at maximum capacity. The voltage of a large distribution transformer can go up to 145kV and its power rating from 6.3 up to 30MVA.
Pole- and pad-mounted distribution transformers

Pole-mounted transformers are available as single-phase or 3-phase units. Siemens Energy also offers pad-mounted distribution transformers with the same ratings as pole-mounted units. Pole-mounted distribution transformers are specifically built for applications in North America because the electric grid there differs from those in other parts of the world, such as Europe or Eastern Asia. Their voltage level and power capacity are similar to those of standard medium-sized fluid-immersed transformer, with a voltage level of up to 36kV and and a rating of up to 2,500kVA.
Resisting every storm

Wind turbine operators need reliable and safe transformers so that the turbine never fails. With their expertise in transformers since 1892, and about 10,000 units built for wind farms in the last 20 years, Siemens Energy has been at the frontline of wind application transformers technology. An extensive research and development budget and senior engineering experts have contributed to making Siemens Energy the leading supplier for this application.

body.text: Special design, testing and assembly
On-shore and off-shore design
In wind applications, the characteristics of the transformer depend on the nature of the project. Wind farms on-shore and off-shore will require different power levels.

On-shore: 4.0 - 10MVA Off shore: 10.0 - 20.0MVA for all types, for installation in nacelles and towers, with forced cooling oil/air, high temperature materials; 6.0 - 10.0 MVA with forced cooling oil/water, massive tank for highest mechanical loads, and for installation in the nacelle.
Tried-and-tested quality

The Fluid-immersed distribution transformers REN has been subjected to numerous tests according to international standards to ensure maximum capacity and longevity. This includes extensive internal and external programs to test its suitability, Such as successful testing of short-circuit and vibration stability, highest corrosion, heat run tests as well as salt spray tests for components for offshore application.
1 transformer, 3 possible locations

For wind application, Fluid-immersed distribution transformers REN can be installed in three areas within the wind farm: in the transformer substation located beside the wind turbines, inside the wind turbine tower, or they can even be directly installed inside the nacelle of the turbine. Ratings for this particular application can go up to 9,8MVA and come with a rated voltage of up to 66 kV.

Siemens Energy builds resilient and customizable distribution transformers which not only deliver reliable and superior performance in harshest conditions, but also perfectly fit the needs of customers in industry. Siemens Energy's fluid-immersed distribution transformers IND are designed to supply energy for heavy-duty drives for steel mills, oil rigs, offshore installations, and conveyance facilities, and for the complete range of uses for drives in industry.

Static converter facilities with appropriate valves are required for transforming and controlling electric energy for these applications. Static converter transformers provide the link to the supply network. They must endure heavier dynamic and thermal stress due to rapid changes in the load and allow for frequent start-uploads. Siemens Energy's special winding design achieves a high short-circuit withstand capability making the transformer insusceptible to the stress caused by frequent drive peak loads. Another positive factor is the great heat capacity and high overload capability of this type of transformer.

Siemens Energy has developed a laboratory-tested painting system and corrosion protection (e.g. salt spray tests) for Siemens Energy fluid-immersed distribution transformers IND used for application or in chemical environment.

Installed next to the solar panels in a transformer substation, fluid-immersed distribution transformers REN for solar application come with a rating of up to 5 MVA and a rated voltage of up to 36kV. Thanks to Siemens Energy's transformers' touch-proof design, fluid-immersed distribution transformers REN can be installed both outside and inside without extra housings.

Solar farms face harsh weather conditions and still need operate at all times. Its design options make fluid-immersed distribution transformers REN a highly reliable solution – resistant to high corrosion, harsh weather conditions and temperature variations.
Fluid-immersed distribution transformers REN converts MV to LV with identical frequency Ratings: ≤ 15 MVA / ≤ 72,5 kV

faqs.q: Electrically safe allominium foil winding
faqs.a: The coils of the high-voltage windings are made of aluminum foil. Why foil windings? They combine simple winding techniques with high electrical safety.Insulation is subjected to less electrical stress than in other types of windings.The result: high power frequency and impulse voltage withstand capability. faqs.q: No gas inclusions during casting process
faqs.a: The high voltage windings are potted with epoxy resin under vacuum at a high temperature: Undesirable gas inclusions are prevented.Freedom from partial discharges (up to twice the rated voltage) is provided. The conductor strip and insulation material are bonded together by heating: A compact unit with sufficient strength to reliably withstand radial forces is created.

faqs.q: Temperature monitoring
faqs.a: PTC thermistor temperature sensors, PT 100 resistance temperature detectors or a capillary tube thermometer can be employed for temperature supervision of GEAFOL transformers.

faqs.q: Radial-flow fans
faqs.a: Radial-flow fans with temperature-dependent control can be installed to provide capacity reserves and to cover peak load periods. In this way, the transformer output can be raised by up to 50 percent.

faqs.a: To provide protection for the transformers against environmental influences and to prevent people from coming into contact with the transformer, we offer standard housings, and optionally, modified housing designs.

faqs.q: What does an HVDC converter transformer do?
faqs.a: It adapts AC voltage and enables efficient interaction between the grid and converter systems.

faqs.q: How does an HVDC transformer support AC/DC conversion?
faqs.a: It adjusts voltage levels before power electronic converters perform rectification or inversion.

faqs.q: Why are HVDC transformers critical for power transmission?
faqs.a: They enable efficient long-distance transmission, renewable integration, and improved grid stability.
